etymology_story.zh: Matelot 借自法语 matelot（水手），通常进一步追溯到中古荷兰语 mattenoot，原义约为“共用铺位的伙伴”。词义从船上的铺位同伴发展为水手，英语中则常带非正式的海军色彩。
etymology_story.en: Matelot was borrowed from French matelot, meaning sailor, usually traced further to Middle Dutch mattenoot, roughly “bunk companion.” The meaning developed from a shipboard sleeping companion to a sailor, and the English word often has an informal naval flavour.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 matelot 是不可再分析的整体借词，不能把结尾 -ot 当作活跃的英语后缀；复数为 matelots。没有常用的英语派生动词或形容词；法语 matelote 与其有词源关系，在英语中可指一种炖鱼菜，但不是英语 matelot 的规则派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, matelot is an unsegmented loanword; its ending -ot is not a productive English suffix, and its plural is matelots. It has no common English-derived verb or adjective; French matelote is etymologically related and can name a fish stew in English, but is not a regular English derivative of matelot.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sailor（水手）最通用，可指职业水手或从事帆船活动的人；seaman（海员）较强调职业或海军身份，也可能是具体军衔名称；jack tar（水手）带传统、诙谐或旧时色彩，matelot 则常见于英国非正式海军语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sailor is the broadest term and can include recreational sailors; seaman more strongly suggests an occupational or naval role and can also name a rank; jack tar has a traditional, humorous, or historical flavour, while matelot is associated with informal British naval usage.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“船上共用铺位的伙伴”联想到“水手”；可借 mate“伙伴”辅助联想，但它不是现代英语中的实际构词成分。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a shipboard bunk companion becoming a sailor; mate can support the association, although it is not an actual modern English component of matelot.

senses.meaning_en: To treat cotton with caustic alkali to improve its lustre, strength, and ability to absorb dye.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由英国纺织技术革新者 John Mercer 的姓氏加动词后缀构成；他于1850年为相关工艺取得专利。这个人名由此成为棉纺织品碱处理工艺的名称。[来源：Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/mercerize)
etymology_story.en: The word combines the surname of British textile innovator John Mercer with a verb-forming suffix; Mercer patented the process in 1850. His name consequently became associated with this alkali treatment of cotton textiles. [Source: Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/mercerize)

morphology_enriched.zh: Mercer（默瑟，人名）+ -ise（构成表示处理过程的动词）。词形：mercerises、mercerised、mercerising；派生词：mercerisation（丝光处理）、merceriser（丝光机或相关处理装置）；mercerised 也用作分词形容词，表示“经丝光处理的”。对应的 -ize 拼写词族为 mercerize、mercerizes、mercerized、mercerizing、mercerization、mercerizer。
morphology_enriched.en: Mercer, a surname, + -ise, a suffix forming a process verb. Inflections: mercerises, mercerised, mercerising. Derivatives: mercerisation, the treatment process, and merceriser, a machine or apparatus used for it; mercerised also functions as a participial adjective meaning treated by this process. The corresponding -ize family is mercerize, mercerizes, mercerized, mercerizing, mercerization, and mercerizer.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mercerize（丝光处理）是同一词的另一种拼写；alkali-treat（进行碱处理）范围较广，不一定指丝光工艺；finish（进行整理加工）泛指改善织物性能或外观的后整理。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mercerize is an alternative spelling with the same meaning; alkali-treat describes a broader range of alkaline treatments; finish is a general textile term for processing that improves a fabric's properties or appearance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Mercer 的工艺：棉经碱处理，获得丝般光泽。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Mercer's process: alkali-treated cotton gains a silky shine.

senses.english_definition: A murex is a sea snail that usually has a spiny shell and belongs to a group that includes species formerly used to make purple dye.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在16世纪借入拉丁语 murex，原指可提供紫染料的海螺。该名称后来也进入动物分类命名，用于骨螺属 Murex，英语普通名词则可包括若干近缘属的骨螺。[来源：Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/murex)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Latin murex, a name for a marine shellfish associated with purple dye, in the sixteenth century. The name also entered zoological classification as Murex, while the English common noun can include snails from related genera. [Source: Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/murex)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再按常用英语词缀拆分的借词。复数为 murexes 或 murices，后者保留拉丁语 muric- 词干；相关专业词有 muricid（骨螺科动物；骨螺科的）、muricine（骨螺类的，较罕用）和 Muricidae（骨螺科）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is a borrowed base without a productive English prefix-and-suffix breakdown. Its plurals are murexes and murices, the latter preserving the Latin stem muric-. Related specialist forms include muricid, a member of the family or an adjective describing it; muricine, an uncommon adjective referring to murexes; and Muricidae, the family name.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: muricid（骨螺科动物）按科分类，覆盖范围通常更广；rock snail（岩螺）是部分骨螺的俗称，使用范围因地区而异；sea snail（海螺）是更宽泛的上位词，三者不能在所有语境中互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Muricid identifies a member of the wider family Muricidae; rock snail is a common name applied to some muricids, with regional variation; sea snail is a much broader category. These terms are not interchangeable in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the spiny shell with the ancient purple dye.

senses.meaning_zh: 未产的；无既往分娩史的

etymology_story.zh: 该词属于19世纪形成的医学拉丁语词族，结合了源自拉丁语 nullus（无）的成分和源自 parere（生育、产出）的成分。其核心是“没有既往生产经历”，动物学中也可用于表示尚未产卵。[来源：Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/nullipara)、[Dictionary.com](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/nulliparous)
etymology_story.en: The word belongs to a nineteenth-century medical Latin family combining an element from Latin nullus, meaning none, with one from parere, meaning to bear or produce. Its central idea is having no previous reproductive delivery, extended in zoology to females that have not laid eggs. [Sources: Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/nullipara), [Dictionary.com](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/nulliparous)

morphology_enriched.zh: nulli-（无；可进一步分析为 null- + 连接元音 -i-）+ -parous（生育或生产的）。同族词：nullipara（未产妇），复数 nulliparae 或 nulliparas；nulliparity（未产状态）。同构相关词有 primiparous（初产的）、multiparous（经产的）；nulligravid（从未妊娠的）共享 nulli-，但表达不同概念。
morphology_enriched.en: nulli-, meaning none and analyzable as null- plus the linking vowel -i-, + -parous, meaning bearing or producing offspring. Family members include nullipara, a woman with no previous births; its plurals nulliparae and nulliparas; and nulliparity, the condition. Related formations include primiparous, having borne once, and multiparous, having borne more than once; nulligravid shares nulli- but means never having been pregnant.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nonparous（未产的）是专业近义词；never having given birth（从未分娩过）是通俗释义；nulligravid（从未妊娠的）仅为相关词，未产者可以曾经妊娠。临床产次统计还需依照所用体系的孕周标准，不能只看是否生育过活产儿。[来源：NCBI](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/medgen/604496)、[UNSW 术语表](https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/npesu/research-reports/2025-09-anzard/2025-09-Assisted-Reproductive-Technology-in-Australia-and-New-Zealand-2023.pdf)
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nonparous is a specialist near-equivalent; never having given birth is the plain-language paraphrase; nulligravid is related but means never pregnant, whereas a nulliparous person may have been pregnant. Clinical parity also depends on the gestational threshold used by the relevant system, rather than simply on whether there has been a live birth. [Sources: NCBI](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/medgen/604496), [UNSW glossary](https://www.unsw.edu.au/content/dam/pdfs/medicine-health/npesu/research-reports/2025-09-anzard/2025-09-Assisted-Reproductive-Technology-in-Australia-and-New-Zealand-2023.pdf)

mnemonic_anchor.zh: nulli- 是“零”，-parous 看“生产史”：零产次，不等于零次妊娠。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Nulli- means zero; -parous concerns births: zero previous births does not mean zero pregnancies.

etymology_story.en: Oilbird combines oil and bird, referring to the historical practice of rendering oil from the birds' fat-rich chicks. That former use supplied the bird's English name. [Source: Oilbird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oilbird#Etymology)

morphology_enriched.zh: oil（油脂，名词）+ bird（鸟，名词）→ oilbird（名词复合词）；复数 oilbirds。没有常用的直接派生动词、副词或形容词；oilbird colony 等表达中的 oilbird 是名词作定语。同物异名 guacharo 和 fatbird 不是其派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: oil, a noun, + bird, a noun, → oilbird, a compound noun; plural oilbirds. There are no established common directly derived verbs, adverbs, or adjectives; oilbird in oilbird colony is a noun used attributively. Guacharo and fatbird are alternative names, not derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: guacharo（油鸱，亦写 guácharo）是同一种鸟的另一名称；fatbird（肥鸟、油鸱）是较少见的别称。两者主要区别在名称来源和使用习惯，不表示不同物种。[来源：Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/oilbird)
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Guacharo, also written guácharo, names the same species; fatbird is a less familiar alternative name. The differences concern naming traditions and usage, rather than separate species. [Source: Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/oilbird)

mnemonic_anchor.zh: oil + bird：雏鸟脂肪多，过去可炼油。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Oil + bird: fatty chicks once supplied oil.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自德语 Ostmark，字面意思是“东部的马克”，用来指称东德货币并与西德马克相区别。该词保留在历史叙述中，所指货币已于1990年被德国马克取代。[来源：Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/ostmark)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed German Ostmark, literally east mark, as a name distinguishing East Germany's currency from the West German mark. The word remains in historical accounts, although the currency was replaced by the Deutsche mark in 1990. [Source: Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/ostmark)

morphology_enriched.zh: 德语来源结构：Ost（东）+ Mark（马克，货币单位）；英语中作为借入的复合名词使用，也写作 Ostmark。英语规则复数为 ostmarks；没有常用的直接派生动词、形容词或副词，mark 是其来源成分而非英语派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: German source structure: Ost, east, + Mark, the monetary unit. English uses it as a borrowed compound noun, also spelled Ostmark. The regular English plural is ostmarks; there are no common directly derived verbs, adjectives, or adverbs, and mark is a source component rather than an English derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: East German mark（东德马克）是明确、通俗的对应名称；GDR mark（民主德国马克）强调所属国家；mark（马克）单独使用容易与其他历史上的马克货币混淆，需由语境限定。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: East German mark is the explicit everyday equivalent; GDR mark identifies the issuing state more formally; mark alone is ambiguous because several historical currencies used that name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Ost 是“东”，Mark 是“马克”：合起来就是东德马克。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ost means east and Mark means mark: the East German mark.

etymology_story.zh: perisher 由 perish（死亡、毁灭）加后缀 -er 构成，早期可指将要死去或遭毁灭的人。后来在英国口语中发展为对讨厌或淘气之人的称呼，也可用于亲昵的责怪。
etymology_story.en: Perisher was formed from perish and -er and could originally refer to someone who perishes or is doomed. In informal British usage, it developed into a term for an objectionable or mischievous person, sometimes used affectionately.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：perish（死亡、毁灭）+ -er（指人后缀）→ perisher；复数为 perishers。常用相关词族包括 perish、perished、perishing、perishable（易腐坏的）、perishables（易腐食品）、perishability（易腐性）、imperishable（不朽的；不易毁坏的）和 imperishability（不朽性）；这些词并非都由 perisher 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: perish + the person-forming suffix -er → perisher; plural perishers. The main related family includes perish, perished, perishing, perishable, perishables, perishability, imperishable, and imperishability; these are related through perish rather than all being derivatives of perisher.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: rascal（淘气鬼）常带亲昵意味；scamp（顽皮鬼）突出活泼、爱恶作剧；nuisance（讨厌的人或事）突出造成烦扰。perisher 带有较鲜明的英国旧式口语色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rascal often suggests affectionate disapproval; scamp emphasizes lively mischievousness; nuisance emphasizes the annoyance someone or something causes. Perisher has a particularly dated British conversational flavor.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Link perish, meaning to come to destruction, with a little troublemaker who causes havoc; remember the affectionate sense, not a literal threat.

etymology_story.zh: perse 经中古英语 pers 借自古法语 pers，通常追溯至中世纪拉丁语 persus，并与“波斯的”这一名称相联系。这个历史色名用于深蓝、蓝灰或蓝紫色及相应织物，各时期所指色调并不完全一致。
etymology_story.en: Perse entered Middle English as pers from Old French pers and is generally traced to Medieval Latin persus, associated with the name Persian. It became a historical term for dark blue, blue-gray, or purplish-blue colors and fabrics, with some variation in the shade intended.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为不可再分析的借入词 perse，不拆成 per- 与 -se。作颜色名或织物名时通常为不可数名词；没有常用的现代派生词族，perse cloth 等是词组，不是派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, perse is an unanalyzable loanword, not a combination of per- and -se. As a color or fabric noun it is normally uncountable; it has no common modern derivative family, and expressions such as perse cloth are phrases rather than derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bluish-gray（蓝灰色）突出灰中带蓝；slate-blue（石板蓝）通常指较暗、偏灰的蓝色；purplish-blue（紫蓝色）突出蓝中带紫。它们只能近似说明 perse 的历史色域，不能统一替代其所有用法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bluish-gray emphasizes gray with a blue tint; slate-blue usually denotes a muted, grayish blue; purplish-blue emphasizes a violet tint. These approximate parts of perse's historical color range rather than replacing every historical use.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect perse with its Persian association and picture an old bolt of dark blue-gray cloth; the image is a memory aid, not an exact color specification.

etymology_story.zh: pipistrelle 借自法语 pipistrelle，后者来自意大利语 pipistrello（蝙蝠），最终可追溯至拉丁语 vespertilio（蝙蝠）。拉丁语名称与 vesper（傍晚）相关，体现了蝙蝠在暮色中活动的特点。
etymology_story.en: Pipistrelle was borrowed from French pipistrelle, from Italian pipistrello, ultimately tracing back to Latin vespertilio, meaning bat. The Latin name is associated with vesper, meaning evening, reflecting the animal's activity around dusk.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 pipistrelle 作为整体借入词处理，不宜拆成具有现代英语意义的词根和后缀。复数为 pipistrelles；没有常用的英语派生词族，pipistrelle bat 是名词作定语的组合，Pipistrellus 则是相关的拉丁化属名。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, pipistrelle is treated as a whole borrowed base rather than divided into productive English roots and suffixes. Its plural is pipistrelles; it has no common English derivative family, pipistrelle bat uses the noun attributively, and Pipistrellus is the related Latinized genus name.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bat（蝙蝠）是范围更广的上位词；vesper bat（蝙蝠科蝙蝠）指其所属的较大类群；pipistrelle bat 与 pipistrelle 基本同义，但明确补出了动物类别。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bat is the broader everyday term; vesper bat refers to the larger family group to which pipistrelles belong; pipistrelle bat is essentially equivalent to pipistrelle but makes the animal category explicit.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 沿着词源记“傍晚 → 蝙蝠”：暮色里捕虫的小蝙蝠，就是 pipistrelle 的典型画面。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the historical link from evening to bat: picture a tiny bat catching insects at dusk.

senses.meaning_zh: 捕鱼的；垂钓的；渔人的（正式或诙谐用语）

senses.english_definition: Piscatorial activities, interests, or skills are connected with catching fish.

etymology_story.zh: piscatorial 源于拉丁语 piscatorius（渔人的、捕鱼的），与 piscator（渔人）相联系；这些词最终都源自 piscis（鱼）。英语保留了这一拉丁词族的书面色彩，也常用它来诙谐地谈论钓鱼。
etymology_story.en: Piscatorial derives from Latin piscatorius, meaning relating to fishers or fishing, and is connected with piscator, meaning fisher; both ultimately come from piscis, meaning fish. In English, its learned character also makes it useful for humorous references to fishing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可分析为拉丁来源词干 piscator-（渔人）+ 形容词后缀 -ial；进一步的历史结构包含 pisc-（鱼）。相关词有 piscator（渔人，罕用）、piscatory（捕鱼的）和 piscatorially（以捕鱼或垂钓的方式，罕用）；pisciculture（养鱼业）共享 pisc- 词根，但不是由 piscatorial 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: The word can be analyzed as the Latin-derived stem piscator-, meaning fisher, plus the adjective suffix -ial; its deeper historical structure contains pisc-, meaning fish. Related words include the rare noun piscator, the adjective piscatory, and the rare adverb piscatorially; pisciculture shares pisc- but is not derived from piscatorial.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fishing-related（与捕鱼有关的）最直接、中性；angling（垂钓的，作定语）通常限于用鱼钩和钓线钓鱼；piscatory（捕鱼的）与 piscatorial 很接近，同样偏书面。piscatorial 可泛指捕鱼，也常带故作文雅的幽默感。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fishing-related is direct and neutral; attributive angling usually concerns fishing with a hook and line; piscatory is a close, similarly literary alternative. Piscatorial can cover fishing broadly and often sounds playfully elevated.

etymology_story.zh: pneumoconiosis 属于十九世纪形成的医学术语，与较长的形式 pneumonoconiosis 有关，采用希腊语来源的“肺”“尘”和“病理状态”等构词成分。这个名称直接描述了粉尘进入肺部并引起疾病的关系。
etymology_story.en: Pneumoconiosis belongs to nineteenth-century medical terminology and is related to the longer form pneumonoconiosis, using Greek-derived elements for lung, dust, and a pathological condition. The name directly expresses the connection between dust in the lungs and disease.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代医学构词：pneum/o（肺）+ coni（尘）+ -osis（病理状态）→ pneumoconiosis；coni- 来自希腊语 konis（尘）。复数为 pneumoconioses；相关形式有 pneumoconiotic（尘肺病的，也可作名词指尘肺病患者）及较长异形 pneumonoconiosis。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern medical structure: pneum/o, meaning lung, + coni, meaning dust, + -osis, indicating a pathological condition → pneumoconiosis; coni- comes from Greek konis, meaning dust. The plural is pneumoconioses; related forms include pneumoconiotic, an adjective and also a noun for an affected person, and the longer variant pneumonoconiosis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dust lung（尘肺）是较通俗的对应说法；silicosis（矽肺）特指吸入结晶型二氧化硅粉尘引起的尘肺；asbestosis（石棉肺）特指石棉引起的肺纤维化。后两者是具体类型，不能在所有语境中替代总称 pneumoconiosis。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dust lung is a less technical equivalent; silicosis specifically results from inhaling crystalline silica dust; asbestosis is pulmonary fibrosis caused by asbestos. The latter two are specific types and cannot replace the umbrella term pneumoconiosis in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pneumo- 肺 + coni- 尘 + -osis 病：肺里积尘而成病。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pneumo- lung + coni- dust + -osis disease: dust in the lungs produces disease.

etymology_story.zh: 表示清酒的 saki 是日语 sake 的英语异体拼写，日语原词可泛指酒，英语通常专指日本米酿清酒。表示猴子的 saki 则经法语传入，源于南美洲原住民语言中的动物名称，与酒名没有词源关系。
etymology_story.en: The drink name saki is an English spelling variant of Japanese sake, which can mean alcoholic drink generally in Japanese but usually denotes Japanese rice wine in English. The monkey name entered through French from an Indigenous South American animal name and is etymologically unrelated.

morphology_enriched.zh: 两个词义在现代英语中都作为不可进一步拆分的借词处理。酒名的拼写变体有 sake、saké、saki，通常作不可数名词；猴名的复数为 sakis，常见组合有 saki monkey（僧面猴）和 white-faced saki（白面僧面猴）；没有常用的派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Both words are morphologically simple loans in modern English. The drink has the spelling variants sake, saké, and saki and is normally uncountable; the monkey has the plural sakis and occurs in saki monkey and white-faced saki. Neither has a common productive family of derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sake 是清酒义更通行的拼写；rice wine（米酒）范围更广，不仅指日本清酒；saki monkey 与猴名 saki 指同类动物，表达更明确。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sake is the more usual spelling for the drink; rice wine is broader and includes drinks other than Japanese sake; saki monkey refers to the same animal as saki but makes the zoological meaning explicit.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 两条独立线索：杯中的 saki 是清酒，树上的 saki 是僧面猴；同形不代表同源。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Two separate anchors: saki in a cup is rice wine; a saki in a tree is a monkey. Shared spelling does not mean shared origin.

etymology_story.zh: sanserif 是排印术语 sans serif 的合写变体，由借自法语的 sans（没有）和英语 serif（衬线）组成。名称直接描述字形末端没有衬线这一特征；serif 本身的更早词源尚不确定。
etymology_story.en: Sanserif is a closed spelling variant of the typographical term sans serif, combining French sans, meaning 'without,' with English serif. The name describes the absence of finishing strokes on letters; the earlier origin of serif is uncertain.

morphology_enriched.zh: sans（没有）+ serif（衬线）→ sans serif；sanserif 是合写变体，也常见连字符形式 sans-serif。相关词有 serif（衬线）、serifed／seriffed（有衬线的）和 sans-serif（无衬线的；无衬线字体）；可数名词 sanserif 的复数为 sanserifs。
morphology_enriched.en: Sans ('without') + serif forms sans serif; sanserif is a closed variant, alongside the hyphenated sans-serif. Related forms include serif, serifed or seriffed, and sans-serif as an adjective or noun. The countable noun sanserif has the plural sanserifs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sans serif 是同一术语的通行分写形式；sans-serif 常用于形容词；grotesque（无衬线字体）是传统排印名称，在现代字体分类中也可专指某些无衬线风格，不能在所有语境中完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sans serif is the usual open spelling of the same term; sans-serif is especially common as an adjective; grotesque is a traditional typographical name that can also designate particular styles of sans-serif type, so it is not interchangeable in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sans＝没有，serif＝衬线：字画末端没有“小脚”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sans means 'without': remove the little finishing 'feet' of letters to get sanserif.

etymology_story.zh: schizo 是 schizophrenic 的俚语截短形式；后者与 schizophrenia 同属一个词族，其希腊语词源成分分别表示“分裂”和“心智”。后来该词被泛用于辱骂他人或形容矛盾、无常的表现；这种引申并不构成医学描述，精神分裂症也不等于“多重人格”。
etymology_story.en: Schizo is a slang clipping of schizophrenic, which belongs to the same family as schizophrenia and ultimately contains Greek elements meaning 'split' and 'mind.' It later developed insulting and figurative uses for contradictory or erratic behavior; these are not clinical descriptions, and schizophrenia does not mean multiple personalities.

morphology_enriched.zh: schizophrenic 截短 → schizo，并可作名词或形容词；名词复数为 schizos。相关词族有 schizophrenia（精神分裂症）、schizophrenic（精神分裂症的；患者）和 schizophrenically（以精神分裂症相关的方式）；schizo- 是表示“分裂”的学术构词成分，不能与独立俚语 schizo 的语体混同。
morphology_enriched.en: Schizophrenic is clipped to schizo, which functions as a noun or adjective; the noun plural is schizos. Related forms include schizophrenia, schizophrenic, and schizophrenically. The learned combining form schizo- means 'split' and should be distinguished in register from the independent slang word.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: person with schizophrenia（精神分裂症患者）是中性、以人为本的表达；schizophrenic 作为形容词可用于临床描述，但作名词称呼人时可能显得标签化；erratic（反复无常的）只描述不稳定表现，不暗示精神分裂症，适合替代其比喻性用法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Person with schizophrenia is a neutral, person-centered expression; schizophrenic can be a clinical adjective, although its use as a noun may sound labeling; erratic describes unpredictable behavior without implying schizophrenia and can replace the figurative use.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记作 schizophrenic 的截短俚语；词根“分裂”是历史线索，不是“多重人格”的定义。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember it as clipped schizophrenic: 'split' is an etymological clue, not a definition of multiple personalities.

senses.pos: n. 名词（历史兵器术语）
senses.meaning_zh: 铠甲腰部下垂、保护髋部或大腿上部的甲片

senses.english_definition: A tasse is a piece of armor that hangs below the waist and protects the hip or upper part of the thigh.

etymology_story.zh: tasse 属于中世纪甲胄词汇，与法语中表示“袋、口袋”的 tasse 及其指小形式 tassette 有历史联系，英语 tasset 也源于这一词系。袋子的名称被用于从腰部垂下的护甲，反映了它的位置和悬垂形态。
etymology_story.en: Tasse belongs to medieval armor vocabulary and is historically connected with French tasse, meaning 'pouch,' and its diminutive tassette, the source of English tasset. The pouch name was applied to armor hanging from the waist, reflecting its position and suspended form.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 tasse 作为不可进一步拆分的历史借词处理，复数为 tasses。相关形式有 tasset（同类护甲；复数 tassets）和较少见的 tassette；它们是历史相关形式，不宜把 tasset 当作现代英语中由 tasse 加上能产后缀 -et 生成的词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, tasse is an unanalyzed historical loan, with the plural tasses. Related forms include tasset, plural tassets, and the less usual tassette. These are historically related forms; tasset should not be presented as a productive modern English formation from tasse plus -et.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tasset 是更通行的对应甲胄术语；thigh guard（大腿护甲）是范围更广的功能性名称；cuisse（大腿甲）通常指包覆大腿的甲胄部件，与从腰部悬垂的 tasse 并不完全相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tasset is the more usual corresponding armor term; thigh guard is a broader functional description; cuisse usually denotes armor enclosing the thigh and is not precisely the same as a tasse suspended from the waist.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 腰间像袋子一样垂下的甲片：从“袋”联想到护住大腿上部的护甲。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a pouch hanging from a belt, then replace it with an armor plate protecting the upper thigh.

etymology_story.zh: toerag 由 toe（脚趾）和 rag（破布）复合而成，原指代替袜子使用的裹脚布。这种与贫困生活相联系的物品名称后来被用于贬称人，并发展为英国英语中的侮辱语。
etymology_story.en: Toerag combines toe and rag and originally named a cloth wrapped around the foot instead of a sock. Through its association with poverty, the object name became a contemptuous label for a person and developed into a British insult.

morphology_enriched.zh: toe（脚趾）+ rag（破布）→ toerag，是名词加名词构成的复合词，复数为 toerags；另有连字符拼写 toe-rag。没有常用的派生词族；toe 和 rag 各自的派生词不属于 toerag 的直接派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Toe + rag forms the noun–noun compound toerag, with the plural toerags; toe-rag is an alternative spelling. It has no common derivative family, and derivatives of toe or rag individually are not direct derivatives of toerag.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: scoundrel（恶棍）更强调不诚实或不道德；rotter（坏蛋）是较老派的英国非正式骂语；rat（卑鄙小人）常突出背叛或不忠。toerag 是带轻蔑色彩的英国口语，也可在熟人间半开玩笑地使用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Scoundrel emphasizes dishonesty or bad character; rotter is a rather old-fashioned British informal insult; rat often suggests betrayal or disloyalty. Toerag is contemptuous British colloquial language, although it can sometimes be used teasingly among familiar people.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: toe + rag＝裹脚破布；由寒酸物品名转成轻蔑的人称。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Toe + rag gives a makeshift foot covering; the humble object name later became a contemptuous name for a person.

etymology_story.zh: 借自拉丁语 tunica，原指贴身穿的长衣，也是英语 tunic 的来源。解剖学和植物学将“覆盖身体的衣服”这一意象用于组织的包膜或外层。
etymology_story.en: Tunica was borrowed from Latin tunica, a garment worn next to the body, which also gave English tunic. Anatomy and botany extended the image of a covering garment to a tissue covering or outer layer.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借入的单纯词，不宜强拆成英语词根和后缀。单数 tunica，专业用语中复数通常为 tunicae，也可见英语化复数 tunicas；相关词有 tunic（束腰长衣）、tunicate（被囊动物；有被膜的）和 tunicated（有被膜的）。tunica intima 是拉丁语名词短语，不是派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, tunica is a borrowed simplex rather than a transparent root-and-affix formation. Its usual technical plural is tunicae; the regularized plural tunicas also occurs. Related words include tunic, tunicate, and tunicated. Tunica intima is a Latin noun phrase, not a derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: coat（包层）突出覆盖作用；sheath（鞘）常指包围细长结构的套状组织；membrane（膜）泛指薄层组织。tunica 是较专门的解剖学或植物学名称，不能在所有固定术语中与这些词互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Coat emphasizes a covering; sheath often describes a sleeve around an elongated structure; membrane generally denotes a thin tissue layer. Tunica is a more specialized anatomical or botanical term and is not interchangeable with these words in every established name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 tunica 想成组织穿的 tunic：器官的“衣层”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of a tunica as a tissue's tunic: a covering layer.

etymology_story.zh: 由 whin（荆豆等多刺灌木）与 chat（石䳭类小鸟）组成，名称把灌木环境与鸟的类别联系起来。chat 这一鸟名与其短促的鸣叫声有关。
etymology_story.en: Whinchat combines whin, meaning gorse or a similar prickly shrub, with chat, a name for certain small birds. The bird-name chat refers to their short, chattering calls.

morphology_enriched.zh: whin（荆豆灌木）+ chat（石䳭类小鸟）→ whinchat，是复合名词；复数 whinchats。没有常用的直接派生词；stonechat（黑喉石䳭等鸟类的名称）是共享 chat 成分的相关复合词，并非 whinchat 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Whin + chat forms the compound noun whinchat; its plural is whinchats. It has no common direct derivatives. Stonechat is a related compound sharing chat, rather than a derivative of whinchat.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有通行的严格同义普通名词。chat（石䳭类鸟）和 songbird（鸣禽）都是范围更广的上位词；stonechat 指近缘但不同的鸟，不能作为同义词替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no widely used exact common-name synonym. Chat and songbird are broader terms; stonechat names a related but different bird and is not an interchangeable synonym.

senses.meaning_en: elected local self-government bodies in imperial Russia
senses.english_definition: Zemstva were elected local bodies in imperial Russia that managed matters such as schools, public health, and roads.
senses.chinese_definition: 地方自治机构是俄国帝国时期经选举产生、负责学校、公共卫生和道路等地方事务的组织。
senses.collocation_zh: 省级地方自治机构；县级地方自治机构
senses.sentence_en: The zemstva helped establish schools and improve rural health services.
senses.sentence_zh: 这些地方自治机构帮助兴办学校，并改善农村医疗卫生服务。

etymology_story.zh: 借自俄语 земства，是 земство（zemstvo）的复数形式；该词与表示“土地、地方”的词根有关。英语保留俄语复数词尾，用来指俄国帝国晚期承担地方公共事务的自治机构。
etymology_story.en: Zemstva was borrowed from Russian земства, the plural of земство, or zemstvo, a word connected with land or territory. English retained the Russian plural ending for the local self-government bodies of the late imperial period.

morphology_enriched.zh: 英语中按 zemstvo 的借入复数学习：zemstvo → zemstva；也可使用英语规则复数 zemstvos。从俄语历史构词看，zem- 与“土地”有关，-stvo 构成抽象或集体名词；zemstva 中的 -a 是复数屈折词尾，不是英语派生后缀。没有常用的直接英语派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In English, learn zemstva as the borrowed plural of zemstvo; the regular English plural zemstvos is also used. Historically, Russian zem- relates to land, and -stvo forms abstract or collective nouns. The final -a in zemstva is a Russian plural inflection, not an English derivational suffix. There are no common direct English derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: local councils（地方议会或理事会）是宽泛对应词；district councils（县级地方议会）与 provincial assemblies（省级议会）分别突出不同层级。它们都不能完整表达 zemstva 特有的俄国历史制度背景。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Local councils is a broad equivalent; district councils and provincial assemblies specify different administrative levels. None fully conveys the distinctive historical Russian institution denoted by zemstva.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: zem- 联想“土地、地方”：一地公共事务由 zemstvo 管，多个就是 zemstva。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect zem- with land or locality: one local body is a zemstvo; several are zemstva.

senses.meaning_zh: 酸中毒的；与酸中毒有关的
senses.meaning_en: affected by or relating to acidosis
senses.english_definition: Someone who is acidotic has a disturbance in the body's acid–base balance that tends to make body fluids too acidic.
senses.chinese_definition: 一个人如果处于酸中毒状态，其体内就存在使体液趋于过酸的酸碱平衡紊乱。
senses.collocation_zh: 酸中毒患者；酸中毒状态
senses.sentence_en: The patient remained acidotic despite initial treatment.
senses.sentence_zh: 尽管接受了初步治疗，患者仍处于酸中毒状态。

etymology_story.zh: 由医学名词 acidosis（酸中毒）派生；acidosis 结合了源于拉丁语 acidus（酸的）的 acid 与表示病理状态的 -osis。其形容词采用 -osis 对应 -otic 的构词模式，如 hypnosis 与 hypnotic。
etymology_story.en: Acidotic derives from the medical noun acidosis, which combines acid, ultimately from Latin acidus meaning sour, with the condition-forming suffix -osis. Its adjective follows the -osis/-otic pattern also seen in hypnosis and hypnotic.

morphology_enriched.zh: 直接构词关系为 acidosis（酸中毒）→ acidot-（派生词干）+ -ic（……的）→ acidotic；不是在 acidosis 后直接添加 -ic。相关词族包括 acid（酸；酸的）、acidic（酸性的）、acidity（酸度）、acidify（酸化）、acidification（酸化）及 acidosis；acidosis 的复数为 acidoses。
morphology_enriched.en: The immediate formation is acidosis → acidot- + -ic → acidotic, with a stem change rather than simple addition of -ic to acidosis. The related family includes acid, acidic, acidity, acidify, acidification, and acidosis; the plural of acidosis is acidoses.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: acidic（酸性的）描述物质或环境的酸性；acidemic（酸血症的）特指血液 pH 低于正常范围；acidotic 指存在酸中毒过程。三者相关，但酸中毒可因代偿或混合性酸碱紊乱而不表现为血液 pH 降低，因此不能完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Acidic describes the acidity of a substance or environment; acidemic specifically means having a blood pH below the normal range; acidotic describes an acidosis process. They are related but not equivalent: compensation or a mixed acid–base disorder can allow acidosis without a low blood pH.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: acid 是“酸”，acidosis 是“酸中毒”，acidotic 就是“处于这种状态的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Acid gives the idea of acidity; acidosis names the disorder; acidotic describes that state.

senses.meaning_zh: 药蜀葵属植物，尤指药蜀葵
senses.meaning_en: a plant of the genus Althaea, especially marsh mallow
senses.english_definition: An althea is a plant of the mallow family, especially marsh mallow, which has traditionally been used in herbal preparations.
senses.chinese_definition: althea 指锦葵科的一种植物，尤指传统上用于草药制剂的药蜀葵。
senses.collocation_zh: 药蜀葵根；药蜀葵提取物
senses.sentence_en: The preparation contains an extract of althea root.
senses.sentence_zh: 这种制剂含有药蜀葵根提取物。

senses.meaning_zh: 木槿，尤用于北美园艺语境
senses.meaning_en: the flowering shrub Hibiscus syriacus, especially in North American gardening
senses.english_definition: An althea is a garden shrub, also called rose of Sharon, that produces large flowers in summer and autumn.
senses.chinese_definition: althea 也指木槿，是一种夏秋季开大型花朵的庭园灌木，英语另称 rose of Sharon。
senses.collocation_zh: 木槿灌木；木槿绿篱
senses.sentence_en: They planted an althea hedge along the driveway.
senses.sentence_zh: 他们沿着车道种了一排木槿绿篱。

etymology_story.zh: althea 是 althaea 的变体拼写，源自拉丁语 althaea，并可追溯至希腊语植物名 althaia，通常与表示“医治”的 althein 联系起来，反映药蜀葵的传统药用。该名称后来也用于同属锦葵科的观赏灌木木槿。
etymology_story.en: Althea is a variant spelling of althaea, from Latin althaea and ultimately Greek althaia, traditionally connected with althein, meaning to heal, in reference to marsh mallow's medicinal use. The name was later also applied to the ornamental mallow-family shrub Hibiscus syriacus.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借入的植物名，不作有生产力的英语词根与后缀拆分。拼写变体为 althaea，复数分别为 altheas 和 althaeas；Althaea 是药蜀葵属的拉丁学名。没有常用的直接派生词；althea root、althea bush 等是名词组合。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, althea is a borrowed plant name without a productive English root-and-affix breakdown. Its spelling variant is althaea, with plurals altheas and althaeas respectively; Althaea is the scientific genus name. There are no common direct derivatives. Expressions such as althea root and althea bush are noun combinations.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: marsh mallow（药蜀葵）对应其草本植物义；rose of Sharon（木槿）对应其园艺灌木义，但该俗名在其他地区也可能指别的植物；mallow（锦葵类植物）范围更广，不能精确确定物种。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Marsh mallow matches the herbaceous medicinal-plant sense; rose of Sharon matches the ornamental-shrub sense, although that common name can denote other plants in other regions. Mallow is broader and does not identify a precise species.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“医治”联想到药蜀葵；遇到花园里的 althea bush，则想到木槿。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the historical idea of healing to marsh mallow; in a garden, an althea bush usually means rose of Sharon.

senses.meaning_zh: 生长素；调节植物细胞伸长等生长过程的一类植物激素
senses.meaning_en: A plant hormone that regulates cell elongation and other growth processes.
senses.english_definition: An auxin is a hormone that helps control how a plant grows, including how its cells lengthen.
senses.collocation_zh: 生长素运输；生长素浓度
senses.sentence_en: Uneven distribution of auxin causes the shoot to bend towards the light.
senses.sentence_zh: 生长素分布不均使枝梢向光弯曲。

etymology_story.zh: auxin 是20世纪30年代从德语借入英语的科学名称，由希腊语 auxein（增长、使生长）与物质名称后缀 -in 构成，名称体现了它调节植物生长的作用。[词源与释义来源：牛津学习词典](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/us/definition/english/auxin)
etymology_story.en: Auxin entered English from German in the 1930s, combining Greek auxein, meaning 'to increase', with the substance suffix -in; its name reflects its role in plant growth. [Origin and definition: Oxford Learner’s Dictionaries](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/us/definition/english/auxin)

morphology_enriched.zh: 科学构词分析：aux-（生长）+ -in（物质名称后缀）；现代英语通常把 auxin 作为完整术语使用。词族包括 auxins（复数）、auxinic（生长素的；具有生长素作用的）、antiauxin（抗生长素）；常见复合形式有 auxin-like（类似生长素的）和 auxin-dependent（依赖生长素的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Scientific formation: aux- 'growth' + -in 'substance'; in modern English, auxin generally functions as a complete technical base. Family forms include auxins, auxinic 'relating to or acting like auxin', and antiauxin 'a substance opposing auxin action'; common compounds include auxin-like and auxin-dependent.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: plant hormone（植物激素）和 phytohormone（植物激素，较专业）都是上位词，并非生长素的精确同义词；indole-3-acetic acid／IAA（吲哚-3-乙酸）是一种主要的天然生长素，不能代表全部生长素。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Plant hormone and the more technical phytohormone are broader terms rather than exact synonyms; indole-3-acetic acid, or IAA, is a major naturally occurring auxin, rather than the entire class.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: aux- 表示“生长”，-in 标记“物质”：帮助调节植物生长的物质。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Aux- points to growth and -in to a substance: a substance that helps regulate plant growth.

etymology_story.zh: billycan 由 billy（户外炊事用金属容器）与 can（金属罐）组成，与澳大利亚等地的野外生活密切相关。billy 更早的来源存在争议，不宜把它与法语 bouilli 的联系当作定论。[构词来源：维基词典](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/billycan)；[billy 的器具义：剑桥词典](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/billy?topic=pots-and-pans)
etymology_story.en: Billycan combines billy, an outdoor cooking container, with can, and is closely associated with camping and bush life, especially in Australia. The earlier origin of billy is disputed, so a proposed connection with French bouilli should not be treated as certain. [Formation: Wiktionary](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/billycan); [the container sense of billy: Cambridge Dictionary](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/billy?topic=pots-and-pans)

morphology_enriched.zh: billy（野营锅）+ can（金属容器）→ billycan，为复合名词。复数为 billycans；拼写变体有 billy-can 和 billy can，相关形式包括 billy、billy tin 和 billypot；没有常用的直接派生动词或形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Billy 'camping pot' + can 'metal container' → billycan, a compound noun. The plural is billycans; spelling variants include billy-can and billy can, while related forms include billy, billy tin, and billypot; there are no common directly derived verbs or adjectives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: billy（野营锅）基本同义，表达更简短；camping pot（野营炊锅）是更宽泛的名称；kettle（水壶）主要用于烧水，通常有壶嘴，结构和用途与 billycan 不完全相同。

etymology_story.zh: bistre 于18世纪从法语借入英语，更早的来源不明；它先指以木烟灰制成的绘画颜料，继而也指这种颜料呈现的褐色。[词源与释义来源：柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/bistre)
etymology_story.en: Bistre entered English from French in the eighteenth century, with its earlier origin uncertain; the pigment made from wood soot also gave its name to the resulting brown colour. [Origin and definitions: Collins Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/bistre)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 bistre 是不可再作常用词根、词缀拆分的借词；变体拼写为 bister，派生形容词 bistred 表示“呈烟褐色的”。bistre paint 等搭配属于名词作前置修饰语，不必另立常用形容词词性。[词形与语法来源：柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/bistre)
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, bistre is a borrowed base without a productive root-and-affix breakdown; bister is a spelling variant, and bistred is a derived adjective meaning 'coloured with or like bistre'. Uses such as bistre paint are attributive noun uses and do not require a separate common adjective entry. [Forms and grammar: Collins Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/bistre)

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sepia names a different brown pigment and colour; umber is an earth pigment; brown is the general colour term and does not convey bistre’s particular material origin.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“烟灰变颜料，颜料变色名”：一词连接材料与颜色。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Soot becomes pigment, and pigment becomes a colour name: one word links material and colour.

etymology_story.zh: boletus 来自新拉丁语属名 Boletus，追溯至拉丁语 boletus（蘑菇）及希腊语 bōlitēs；现代用法将古代泛指蘑菇的名称收窄为特定属的菌类名称。[词源与释义来源：柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/boletus)
etymology_story.en: Boletus comes through the New Latin genus name Boletus from Latin boletus 'mushroom' and Greek bōlitēs; modern usage narrows an ancient mushroom name to fungi of a particular genus. [Origin and definition: Collins Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/boletus)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语把 boletus 作为完整的借入名词使用，不能将 -us 当作英语中可自由添加的后缀。复数有 boletuses 和 boleti；相关词有 bolete（牛肝菌类蘑菇），分类学词干 bolet- + -aceae 构成 Boletaceae（牛肝菌科），相关形容词 boletoid 表示“牛肝菌状的”。属名 Boletus 首字母大写，普通名词 boletus 通常小写。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats boletus as a complete borrowed noun; -us is not a freely attachable English suffix here. Plurals are boletuses and boleti; related forms include bolete, the taxonomic formation bolet- + -aceae → Boletaceae 'the bolete family', and boletoid 'resembling a bolete'. Capitalize Boletus as a genus name, but normally use lowercase for the common noun boletus.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bolete（牛肝菌类蘑菇）范围通常更广，包括其他相关属；cep（美味牛肝菌）通常特指 Boletus edulis；porcini（牛肝菌，烹饪用语）通常指美味牛肝菌及一些近缘食用种，不能泛指所有 boletus。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bolete is generally broader and includes related genera; cep usually means Boletus edulis; porcini is a culinary term generally covering B. edulis and certain close edible relatives, rather than every boletus.

etymology_story.zh: 鱼名义由 brook trout 缩短后加亲昵后缀 -ie 形成，是钓鱼语境中的俗称。甜点义则独立融合 brownie 与 cookie，名称直接体现两种甜点的结合。[鱼名用法：缅因州内陆渔业与野生动物局](https://www.maine.gov/ifw/fish-wildlife/fisheries/species-information/brook-trout.html)；[甜点释义：剑桥词典](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/brookie)
etymology_story.en: The fish name shortens brook trout and adds the familiar suffix -ie, producing an informal angling term. The dessert name independently blends brownie and cookie, directly reflecting the combination of the two treats. [Fish usage: Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife](https://www.maine.gov/ifw/fish-wildlife/fisheries/species-information/brook-trout.html); [dessert definition: Cambridge Dictionary](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/brookie)

morphology_enriched.zh: 鱼名：brook（取自 brook trout）+ -ie（亲昵后缀）→ brookie；甜点名：brownie 的开头与 cookie 的结尾拼合 → brookie，属于混成词，不能把这里的 -ie 单独解释为亲昵后缀。两义复数均为 brookies，没有常用的直接派生动词或形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Fish sense: brook, from brook trout, + the familiar suffix -ie → brookie. Dessert sense: the beginning of brownie blends with the ending of cookie → brookie; its final -ie is not independently a familiar suffix in this formation. Both senses have the plural brookies, with no common directly derived verbs or adjectives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 鱼名义：brook trout（溪红点鲑）是标准名称，squaretail（方尾鳟）是地域性俗称。甜点义：brownie-cookie bar（布朗尼曲奇条）是较透明的描述性名称，但 brookie 也可做成单个饼状，不限于切条或切块形式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the fish, brook trout is the standard name and squaretail is a regional nickname. For the dessert, brownie-cookie bar is a transparent descriptive equivalent, although a brookie can also be baked as an individual cookie rather than a bar.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 溪里看 brook，烤盘里看 brownie + cookie：同一拼写，两条构词路径。
mnemonic_anchor.en: In a stream, think brook; in a baking tray, think brownie + cookie: one spelling, two formations.

etymology_story.zh: 该词借自拉丁语 calamus，意为“芦苇、芦苇笔”，更早来自希腊语 kalamos；英语沿用了植物名称，并以芦苇般的中空形态称呼羽根。[《韦氏词典》词源与释义](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/calamus)
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin calamus, meaning a reed or reed pen, ultimately from Greek kalamos; English retained the plant name and also applied the word to the reedlike hollow base of a feather. [Merriam-Webster etymology and senses](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/calamus)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 calamus 作为完整的借入词学习，不宜拆成具有独立现代意义的词根和后缀。单数 calamus → 拉丁式复数 calami；常见专业组合有 calamus wall（羽根壁）、calamus oil（菖蒲油）和 calamus rhizome（菖蒲根茎），这些属于组合词语，并非新的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, calamus is best treated as a whole borrowed word rather than divided into productive roots and affixes. Singular calamus → Latin plural calami; specialist combinations include calamus wall, calamus oil, and calamus rhizome, which are combinations rather than new derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: quill（羽根、翎管）在羽毛解剖语境中与 calamus 接近，但也可指羽毛笔或豪猪刺；rachis（羽轴）指羽根上方承载羽片的部分，并非羽根；sweet flag（菖蒲）对应植物义，不能替代羽根义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Quill closely matches the feather sense but can also mean a writing implement or a porcupine spine; rachis means the upper shaft supporting the vane, not the calamus; sweet flag matches the plant sense only.

etymology_story.zh: capitula 是 capitulum 的拉丁式复数；capitulum 经新拉丁语进入英语，源自拉丁语表示“小头”的词，后来用于形似小头的花序和解剖结构。[《韦氏词典》词源与释义](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/capitulum)
etymology_story.en: Capitula is the Latin plural of capitulum, which entered English through New Latin from a Latin word meaning 'small head'; the name was applied to headlike flower clusters and anatomical structures. [Merriam-Webster etymology and senses](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/capitulum)

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史构词为 capit-（来自 caput“头”的词干）+ 指小成分 -ulum → capitulum；英语中的复数屈折为 capitulum → capitula，即将 -um 换为 -a。相关专业派生词有 capitular（小头的；该词另有“教士会的”等义）和 capituliform（小头状的、头状花序状的）；capitula 本身不是另一个独立词根，也不是动词。
morphology_enriched.en: Historically, capit- is the stem associated with Latin caput 'head', and -ulum supplies diminutive meaning: capitulum 'small head'. English preserves the plural inflection capitulum → capitula, replacing -um with -a; specialist relatives include capitular 'relating to a capitulum' and capituliform 'shaped like a small head or capitulum'.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: flower heads（花头、头状花序）是植物义的通俗对应表达；inflorescences（花序）范围更广，包括多种排列类型；condyles（髁）同属圆形关节结构的相关术语，但不能与 capitula 在所有解剖名称中互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Flower heads is the accessible botanical equivalent; inflorescences is broader and includes many flower arrangements; condyles is a related anatomical term for rounded joint structures, but it is not interchangeable with capitula in every anatomical name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: capit- 表示“头”：一个小头 capitulum，多个小头 capitula；花头、骨小头都抓住“小头状”这一形态。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Capit- points to a head: one little head is a capitulum, several are capitula, whether they are flower heads or anatomical heads.

etymology_story.zh: 扑克牌义经中古英语 carte 借自中古法语，苏格兰地区保留了这种词形，菜单义也与法语 carte 有关；击剑义则是 quarte 的拼写变体，源于表示“第四”的词，属于另一条词源路径。[《韦氏词典》carte](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/carte)、[《柯林斯词典》carte](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/carte)

morphology_enriched.zh: carte + 复数后缀 -s → cartes；末尾 -s 在英语读法中读 /s/，法语读法则不发音。相关形式包括标准英语同源词 card/cards（牌／纸牌）；à la carte（按菜单单点）和 carte blanche（全权委托）是含 carte 的借入短语，并非 cartes 的派生词；击剑词 carte/quarte 应单独归族。
morphology_enriched.en: Carte + plural -s → cartes; the ending is /s/ in an English pronunciation but silent in French. Card/cards is a cognate English form; à la carte and carte blanche are borrowed expressions containing carte rather than derivatives of cartes, while fencing carte/quarte belongs to a separate family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cards（纸牌）是日常标准英语表达，cartes 的纸牌义带苏格兰地区色彩；menus（菜单）是菜单义的普通对应词；quartes（第四姿势或第四防守）是击剑义更明确的对应形式，不能与前两义混用。

etymology_story.zh: catechol 由 catechu（儿茶，一种植物提取物）的名称缩略后加化学命名后缀 -ol 构成，名称保留了它与早期植物来源材料的联系。[《柯林斯词典》词源](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/catechol)
etymology_story.en: Catechol was formed from a shortened form of catechu, the name of a plant extract, plus the chemical suffix -ol, preserving a connection with the natural materials associated with its early preparation. [Collins etymology](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/catechol)

morphology_enriched.zh: catech(u) + -ol → catechol；-ol 是用于醇、酚等名称的化学后缀，不是独立日常词。主要词族包括 catecholic（邻苯二酚的）、catecholate（邻苯二酚去质子化后形成的阴离子或相关配体）、catecholamine（儿茶酚胺）、catecholaminergic（涉及儿茶酚胺的）和 pyrocatechol（邻苯二酚的另一名称）；catechols 可统称含相应结构的化合物。
morphology_enriched.en: Catech(u) + -ol → catechol; -ol is a chemical suffix used in names of alcohols and phenols. Principal family members include catecholic, catecholate for a deprotonated form or corresponding ligand, catecholamine, catecholaminergic, and the alternative name pyrocatechol; the plural catechols can refer collectively to compounds containing the corresponding structural unit.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pyrocatechol（邻苯二酚）是同一物质的另一名称；benzene-1,2-diol（苯-1,2-二酚）用系统命名明确两个羟基的位置；1,2-dihydroxybenzene（1,2-二羟基苯）也指同一物质，差异主要在命名方式。catechin（儿茶素）是不同物质，现代化学语境中不能替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pyrocatechol is an alternative name for the same substance; benzene-1,2-diol explicitly identifies the hydroxyl positions using systematic nomenclature; 1,2-dihydroxybenzene names the same structure in another form. Catechin is a different substance and is not interchangeable in modern chemical usage.

etymology_story.zh: 铈于 1803 年被发现，并以 1801 年发现的天体 Ceres（谷神星）命名；新拉丁语名称 cerium 因而把新发现的元素与当时新发现的天体联系起来。[英国皇家化学会：铈](https://periodic-table.rsc.org/element/58/cerium)
etymology_story.en: Cerium was discovered in 1803 and named after Ceres, the celestial body discovered in 1801; its New Latin name therefore linked a newly discovered element with a recently discovered astronomical object. [Royal Society of Chemistry: cerium](https://periodic-table.rsc.org/element/58/cerium)

morphology_enriched.zh: 命名结构为 Cer-（取自 Ceres 的名称）+ 元素名后缀 -ium → cerium。主要词族有 cerous（铈的；传统命名中尤指三价铈的）、ceric（传统命名中指四价铈的）和 ceria（二氧化铈，CeO2）；常见组合包括 cerium(III)（三价铈）、cerium(IV)（四价铈）及 cerium oxide（氧化铈）。
morphology_enriched.en: The naming structure is Cer-, taken from Ceres, + the element-name suffix -ium → cerium. Principal relatives include cerous, traditionally associated with cerium(III), ceric, traditionally associated with cerium(IV), and ceria, meaning cerium dioxide, CeO2; common combinations include cerium(III), cerium(IV), and cerium oxide.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cerium 没有可直接替换的普通英语近义词：Ce 是其化学符号，element 58（58号元素）是另一种指称方式；rare-earth metal（稀土金属）是上位类别，包含铈及其他元素，并非同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cerium has no ordinary interchangeable lexical synonyms: Ce is its chemical symbol, and element 58 is another designation; rare-earth metal is a broader category containing cerium and other elements, not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Ceres（谷神星）+ -ium（元素名）→ cerium（铈）：用“天体名字给元素命名”连接记忆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ceres + the element ending -ium → cerium: remember an element named after a celestial body.

senses.meaning_zh: 对立；相反；明显不一致
senses.meaning_en: Opposition or marked incompatibility between things.
senses.english_definition: Contrariety is a difference between things whose qualities, ideas, or purposes are opposed to each other.
senses.collocation_en: contrariety of opinion; contrariety of interests
senses.collocation_zh: 意见对立；利益相冲突

senses.meaning_zh: 故意唱反调；执拗，乖戾，主要用于文学或较旧的表达
senses.meaning_en: A disposition to oppose others, chiefly in literary or older usage.
senses.english_definition: Contrariety is a tendency to disagree with people or resist what they want simply because you wish to oppose them.
senses.collocation_en: sheer contrariety; a spirit of contrariety
senses.collocation_zh: 纯粹出于唱反调；故意作对的心态

senses.sentence_zh: 他纯粹为了唱反调，否决了自己前一天还支持的建议。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古法语 contrariété 传入英语，最终来自晚期拉丁语 contrarietas，后者由表示“相反的”的 contrarius 派生，与 contra（相对、反对）同源。其“相反、对立”的基本意义也延伸为人的执拗或故意作对。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through Middle French contrariété, ultimately from Late Latin contrarietas, derived from contrarius, meaning 'opposite,' and related to contra, 'against.' Its basic meaning of opposition also developed into a description of deliberate opposition in someone's behavior.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可借词族关系分析为 contrar-（与 contrary“相反的”对应的词干）+ -iety（抽象名词词尾）；历史上它是借入词，并非英语简单添加 -ety 而成。主要词族包括 contrary（相反的；相反事物）、contrarily（相反地；执拗地）、contrariness（执拗；相反的性质）和 contrariety；复数为 contrarieties。
morphology_enriched.en: A useful modern family-based analysis is contrar-, the stem associated with contrary, plus the abstract-noun ending -iety; historically, the word was borrowed rather than formed in English by simply adding -ety. Principal family members include contrary, contrarily, contrariness, and contrariety; the plural is contrarieties.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: opposition 强调双方的对立或抵触；contradiction 强调陈述或事实之间不能同时成立的矛盾；contrariness 更常描述人的执拗或故意作对。contrariety 较正式，可表示相反性质，也可用于文学性的人格描述。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Opposition emphasizes opposing positions or forces; contradiction emphasizes statements or facts that cannot both hold; contrariness more often describes stubborn or deliberate disagreement. Contrariety is more formal and can describe either opposed qualities or, in literary usage, a contrary disposition.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 contra“相对、反对”：事物方向相反，就是“对立”；人总往反方向走，就是“唱反调”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to contra, 'against': things pulling in opposite directions show opposition; a person always pulling the other way shows contrariness.

senses.meaning_zh: 脱氨酶；催化分子脱去氨基的酶
senses.meaning_en: An enzyme that catalyzes the removal of an amino group from a molecule.
senses.english_definition: A deaminase is an enzyme that helps remove an amino group from a molecule during a chemical reaction.
senses.collocation_zh: 腺苷脱氨酶；胞苷脱氨酶
senses.sentence_en: Adenosine deaminase catalyzes the conversion of adenosine to inosine.
senses.sentence_zh: 腺苷脱氨酶催化腺苷转化为肌苷。

etymology_story.zh: 这是用科学构词成分组成的英语术语：de- 表示“去除”，amin- 与 amine（胺）及 amino（氨基）有关，-ase 用于酶名。名称直接说明这类酶催化脱去氨基的反应。
etymology_story.en: This scientific term combines de-, meaning 'removal,' amin-, associated with amine and amino groups, and the enzyme-forming suffix -ase. Its name directly identifies the amino-group-removing reaction that these enzymes catalyze.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式为 de-（去除）+ amin-（胺或氨基相关词干）+ -ase（酶）。主要相关派生词包括 deaminate（使脱氨）、deaminates、deaminated、deaminating、deamination（脱氨作用）和 deaminase；酶名的复数为 deaminases。amino acid（氨基酸）属于相关术语，并非 deaminase 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The structure is de- ('removal') + amin- (an amine- or amino-related stem) + -ase ('enzyme'). Principal related forms include deaminate, deaminates, deaminated, deaminating, deamination, and deaminase; the enzyme noun has the plural deaminases. Amino acid is a related term rather than a derivative of deaminase.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: deaminating enzyme（催化脱氨的酶）是释义性近义表达；aminohydrolase（氨基水解酶）只适用于通过水解脱去氨基的相关酶，不能替代所有 deaminase；enzyme（酶）是范围更广的上位词。该技术名称没有两三个可在所有语境中互换的普通近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Deaminating enzyme is a descriptive equivalent; aminohydrolase applies to relevant enzymes that remove amino groups through hydrolysis and does not cover every deaminase; enzyme is the broader category. This technical name does not have several ordinary synonyms that are interchangeable in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: de- 去掉 + amin- 氨基 + -ase 酶：帮助“去氨基”的酶。
mnemonic_anchor.en: De- removes, amin- points to an amino group, and -ase signals an enzyme: an enzyme that removes an amino group.

senses.meaning_zh: 下火车；使乘客等下火车，常用于正式、铁路或军事语境
senses.meaning_en: To get off a train or cause passengers to leave one, especially in formal, railway, or military contexts.
senses.english_definition: When people detrain, they get off a train; if someone detrains passengers or troops, they arrange for them to get off.
senses.collocation_en: detrain at a station; detrain troops
senses.collocation_zh: 在车站下火车；让部队下火车
senses.sentence_en: Passengers were instructed to detrain at the next station.
senses.sentence_zh: 乘客接到通知，须在下一站下车。

etymology_story.zh: 该词由英语前缀 de-（离开、移出）与 train（火车）构成，随着铁路运输的发展而出现。它既可表示乘客下车，也可表示安排人员下车，与表示“上火车或使上火车”的 entrain 相对。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in English from de-, indicating departure or removal, and train, as railway transport developed. It can describe either leaving a train or arranging for people to leave one, contrasting with entrain, 'to board or put aboard a train.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式为 de-（离开、移出）+ train（火车）。常用变化形式为 detrains、detrained、detraining；相关名词 detrainment 表示“下火车；组织人员下火车”，较少见。对应词族包括 entrain（上火车；使上火车）和 entrainment（上火车；装运），但 entrainment 在其他专业领域另有含义。
morphology_enriched.en: The structure is de- ('departure or removal') + train. Regular forms are detrains, detrained, and detraining; the less common noun detrainment means leaving a train or organizing people's departure from one. Corresponding formations include entrain and entrainment, although entrainment also has other technical meanings.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: get off 是日常最自然的“下车”表达；alight 较正式，可指下火车、公交车等；disembark 常用于下船或飞机，也可泛指离开交通工具。detrain 明确限定为下火车，且语体较正式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Get off is the usual everyday expression; alight is formal and can refer to leaving a train or bus; disembark commonly concerns ships or aircraft but can refer more broadly to leaving transport. Detrain specifically concerns trains and has a formal register.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: de- 表示“离开”：离开 train，就是下火车；en-train 则是上火车。
mnemonic_anchor.en: De- takes you away from the train: detrain means get off; entrain takes you aboard.

senses.meaning_zh: 嗜酒成癖者；有强烈、难以控制的饮酒欲望的人，属旧式用语
senses.meaning_en: A person with an overpowering, compulsive desire to drink alcohol; a dated term.
senses.english_definition: A dipsomaniac is someone who feels a very strong need to drink alcohol and finds that desire difficult to control.
senses.collocation_en: a chronic dipsomaniac; an incurable dipsomaniac
senses.collocation_zh: 长期嗜酒成癖者；被认为无可救药的嗜酒者

senses.meaning_zh: 嗜酒成癖的；与无法控制的饮酒欲望有关的，较少见且属旧式用语
senses.meaning_en: Affected by or relating to an uncontrollable desire for alcohol; an uncommon, dated use.
senses.english_definition: Someone described as dipsomaniac has a powerful, difficult-to-control desire to drink alcohol.
senses.collocation_zh: 嗜酒成癖的倾向；嗜酒成癖的患者
senses.sentence_en: The old medical report described the patient as dipsomaniac.
senses.sentence_zh: 那份旧医学报告称该患者嗜酒成癖。

etymology_story.zh: 该词属于十九世纪围绕 dipsomania（嗜酒狂）形成的医学词汇，结合了源于希腊语 dipsa“口渴”的 dipso- 与表示狂热或病态冲动的 mania 词族。词源中的一般“口渴”在这里专指对酒精的强烈渴求，如今这一称谓已显陈旧。
etymology_story.en: The word belongs to the nineteenth-century medical vocabulary built around dipsomania, combining dipso-, from Greek dipsa, 'thirst,' with the mania family of words for frenzy or compulsive impulses. General thirst was specialized here to an overpowering desire for alcohol, and the label now sounds dated.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 dipso-（渴）+ maniac（有狂热或强迫性冲动的人；狂热的）。主要词族包括 dipsomania（嗜酒狂）、dipsomaniac（嗜酒成癖者；嗜酒成癖的）和 dipsomaniacal（嗜酒成癖的）；名词复数为 dipsomaniacs。形容词 dipsomaniacal 通常比形容词用法的 dipsomaniac 更明确。
morphology_enriched.en: A modern analysis is dipso- ('thirst') + maniac ('a person with a mania,' or 'maniacal'). Principal family members are dipsomania, dipsomaniac, and dipsomaniacal; the noun plural is dipsomaniacs. Dipsomaniacal is a more explicit adjective than the adjectival use of dipsomaniac.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: alcoholic 在传统用法中指酒精成瘾者，但 person with alcohol dependence（酒精依赖者）措辞更中性；drunkard（酒鬼）带贬义，强调经常醉酒；heavy drinker（大量饮酒者）只说明饮酒量大，不必然表示依赖。dipsomaniac 是强调难以控制的饮酒冲动的旧式称谓。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Alcoholic traditionally refers to someone addicted to alcohol, while person with alcohol dependence is more neutral wording; drunkard is disapproving and emphasizes habitual drunkenness; heavy drinker describes consumption without necessarily implying dependence. Dipsomaniac is a dated label emphasizing an uncontrollable drinking impulse.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: dipso- 是“渴”，maniac 是“成狂”：对酒渴求到了失控的程度。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Dipso- means thirst and maniac suggests compulsion: a thirst for alcohol that feels out of control.

senses.meaning_zh: 狗狗；对狗的亲昵称呼，常见于网络俚语
senses.meaning_en: An affectionate, informal word for a dog, especially in internet slang.
senses.english_definition: A doggo is a dog, especially one that someone is talking about in an affectionate or playful way.
senses.collocation_en: a good doggo; a cute doggo
senses.collocation_zh: 一只乖狗狗；一只可爱的狗狗
senses.sentence_en: Your doggo looks very pleased with his new toy.
senses.sentence_zh: 你家狗狗看起来对自己的新玩具很满意。

senses.meaning_zh: 隐蔽地；不动声色地，主要用于英式非正式短语 lie doggo
senses.meaning_en: Quietly and out of sight or notice, chiefly in the informal British expression lie doggo.
senses.english_definition: If someone lies doggo, they stay quiet or hidden so that other people will not notice them.
senses.collocation_zh: 隐蔽不动；暂不露面；保持低调
senses.sentence_en: They decided to lie doggo until the reporters had gone.
senses.sentence_zh: 他们决定暂时不露面，等记者走了再说。

etymology_story.zh: 亲昵称呼的名词 doggo 可理解为 dog 加上非正式词尾 -o，并因网络语言而广为传播。更早的副词 doggo 见于 lie doggo“隐蔽不动”等表达，其确切来源不明，可能与狗安静伏卧的形象有关；不能把这一推测当作确定词源。
etymology_story.en: The affectionate noun doggo can be understood as dog with the informal ending -o and became widely familiar through internet language. The older adverb in lie doggo has an uncertain origin, possibly connected with the image of a dog lying quietly; that explanation remains a possibility rather than an established derivation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 名词构词公式为 dog（狗）+ -o（非正式、亲昵词尾），拼写中 g 双写；复数为 doggos。相关词包括 dog、doggy 和 doggie（小狗；狗狗），其中 doggy 也可作形容词表示“狗的；像狗的”。副词 doggo 通常固定用于 lie doggo，不宜机械套用名词的构词解释。
morphology_enriched.en: The noun is dog + the informal, affectionate ending -o, with doubled g in the spelling; its plural is doggos. Related forms include dog, doggy, and doggie, with doggy also functioning as an adjective meaning 'relating to or resembling dogs.' The adverb usually occurs in lie doggo and should not automatically be assigned the noun's morphological explanation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 名词：dog 是中性通用词，doggie 是亲昵或儿童用语，pooch 是轻松随意的称呼；doggo 尤其带有网络语言的俏皮感。副词短语：lie low 强调暂时低调以免引人注意，keep out of sight 强调不让人看见；lie doggo 兼有安静潜伏、不引人注意之意。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the noun, dog is neutral, doggie is affectionate or child-directed, and pooch is casual; doggo has a particularly playful internet flavor. For the adverbial expression, lie low emphasizes avoiding attention for a time, while keep out of sight emphasizes remaining unseen; lie doggo suggests staying quietly concealed or unnoticed.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 名词：dog 加上俏皮的 -o，就是“狗狗”。短语：想象狗安静伏着，用这个画面记 lie doggo“隐蔽不动”；这是记忆图像，并非确定词源。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Noun: dog plus a playful -o gives 'doggo.' Phrase: picture a dog lying silently to remember lie doggo, 'stay quietly hidden'; this is a memory image, not a proven etymology.

senses.meaning_zh: 凸棱饰；器皿或建筑装饰上的圆凸瓣纹
senses.meaning_en: A rounded ornamental ridge or lobe on an object or architectural surface.
senses.english_definition: A gadroon is one of a series of rounded raised shapes used to decorate an object, especially a metal vessel or an architectural feature.
senses.collocation_en: a border of gadroons; spiral gadroons
senses.collocation_zh: 一圈凸棱饰边；螺旋状凸棱饰
senses.sentence_en: A row of gadroons decorates the lower part of the silver bowl.
senses.sentence_zh: 银碗下部饰有一圈圆凸瓣纹。

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 godron，其较早形式为 goderon，指圆凸的装饰纹样。英语保留了这一装饰艺术含义，常用于描述金属器皿、家具和建筑构件上的凸棱。
etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed from French godron, earlier goderon, referring to a rounded ornamental feature. English retained this decorative meaning, particularly for raised ornament on metalwork, furniture, and architectural elements.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以 gadroon 为整体词基，不宜强拆词根词缀。常用相关形式：gadroons（复数）、gadrooned（饰有凸棱纹的）、gadrooning（凸棱装饰或制作这种装饰的工艺）；godroon 是异体拼写。此处 CEFR-C2 仅为教学难度估计，并非经核实的官方逐词评级。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, gadroon is best treated as a whole base rather than divided into productive roots and affixes. Relevant forms include gadroons, gadrooned, and gadrooning, meaning the ornament or the process of producing it; godroon is a spelling variant. The CEFR-C2 tag here is a teaching-level estimate, not a verified official word rating.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 相关装饰术语：reeding（细凸棱饰）强调成列的细窄凸条；fluting（凹槽饰）强调向内凹入的槽纹；gadroon 通常指更饱满、呈瓣状的凸起，三者不能完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Related decorative terms are reeding, which consists of narrow raised ridges, and fluting, which consists of recessed grooves. A gadroon is typically a fuller, rounded lobe, so these terms are not exact substitutes.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把整词绑定到一个画面：银碗边缘一圈鼓起的圆瓣。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor the whole word to one image: a silver bowl edged with plump, raised lobes.

senses.meaning_zh: 使不便；打扰；给……添麻烦（正式）
senses.meaning_en: To inconvenience or trouble someone; formal.
senses.english_definition: If something incommodes you, it causes you inconvenience or makes things less comfortable for you.
senses.collocation_en: incommode anyone; be incommoded by the noise
senses.collocation_zh: 给任何人添麻烦；受到噪声打扰
senses.sentence_en: I hope our early departure will not incommode you.
senses.sentence_zh: 希望我们提前离开不会给您添麻烦。

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 incommoder，最终来自拉丁语 incommodare（使不便），与 incommodus（不方便的）有关。其历史结构是表示否定的 in- 加 commodus（合适的、方便的），英语保留了“使人不便”的含义。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word from French incommoder, ultimately from Latin incommodare, meaning to inconvenience, associated with incommodus, inconvenient. Its historical structure combines negative in- with commodus, suitable or convenient.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜以 incommode 为动词词基；历史上可分析为 in-（否定）+ commod-（方便、合适）。屈折形式：incommodes、incommoded、incommoding；相关词包括 incommodious（不方便的）、incommodiously（不方便地）、incommodiousness（不方便），以及历史同源但意义已分化的 commode（便椅；五斗柜）。此处 CEFR-C2 为教学难度估计，并非经核实的官方逐词评级。
morphology_enriched.en: Synchronically, incommode functions as a verb base; historically, it contains negative in- and commod-, associated with convenience or suitability. Inflections are incommodes, incommoded, and incommoding. Related words include incommodious, incommodiously, and incommodiousness; commode is a historical relative whose meanings have diverged. The CEFR-C2 tag is a teaching-level estimate, not a verified official word rating.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: inconvenience（使不便）最中性、最常用；trouble（麻烦）含义更宽，也可指使人担忧；disturb（打扰）强调中断安静、休息或活动。incommode 较正式，并带有旧式表达色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Inconvenience is the most neutral everyday equivalent. Trouble is broader and can include causing worry, while disturb emphasizes interrupting peace, rest, or an activity. Incommode is formal and somewhat old-fashioned.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史逻辑：in- 否定“方便”→让别人不方便。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the historical logic: in- negates convenience, so to incommode someone is to make things inconvenient for them.

senses.meaning_zh: 四声道的；采用四路声音通道重放的
senses.meaning_en: Using four audio channels for sound reproduction.
senses.english_definition: A quadrophonic recording or sound system uses four sound channels to reproduce sound from different directions around the listener.
senses.collocation_zh: 四声道声音；四声道音响系统
senses.sentence_en: The album was originally released in a quadrophonic format.
senses.sentence_zh: 这张专辑最初以四声道格式发行。

etymology_story.zh: 这是二十世纪音响技术中的构词，结合了拉丁语来源的“四”和希腊语来源的“声音”成分，并受到 stereophonic（立体声的）等词的构词模式影响。quadraphonic 是同义异体拼写。
etymology_story.en: This twentieth-century audio term combines a Latin-derived element meaning four with a Greek-derived element meaning sound, following the pattern of words such as stereophonic. Quadraphonic is an alternative spelling with the same meaning.

morphology_enriched.zh: quadro-（四）+ phon-（声音）+ -ic（形容词后缀）→ quadrophonic。相关形式包括 quadrophonically（以四声道方式）、quadrophony（四声道声音或技术）；另有拼写系列 quadraphonic、quadraphonically、quadraphony。此处 CEFR-C2 为专业词汇教学难度估计，并非经核实的官方逐词评级。
morphology_enriched.en: Qu adro- meaning four, phon- meaning sound, and adjectival -ic form quadrophonic. Related forms include quadrophonically and quadrophony, referring to four-channel sound or its technology. Alternative spellings include quadraphonic, quadraphonically, and quadraphony. The CEFR-C2 tag is a teaching-level estimate for this specialist term, not a verified official word rating.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: four-channel（四声道的）是音频语境中的直接对应表达；surround-sound（环绕声的）范围更广，不限定四个声道；stereophonic（立体声的）在通常的音响用法中多指双声道。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Four-channel is a direct equivalent in an audio context. Surround-sound is broader and does not specify exactly four channels. Stereophonic usually refers to two-channel reproduction in ordinary audio usage.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 四个方向传来声音：quadro-＝四，phon-＝声音。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture sound arriving from four directions: quadro- means four and phon- means sound.

senses.meaning_zh: 切开；分裂；分离（正式或专业用语）
senses.meaning_en: The act or process of splitting or separating.
senses.english_definition: Scission is the splitting of something into separate parts, or a division that results from this.
senses.collocation_en: scission into two parts; undergo scission
senses.collocation_zh: 分裂为两部分；发生分裂
senses.sentence_en: The membrane undergoes scission, separating the two compartments.
senses.sentence_zh: 膜发生分裂，使两个区室分离。

senses.meaning_zh: （化学中的）化学键断裂；分子链断裂
senses.meaning_en: The breaking of a chemical bond or molecular chain.
senses.english_definition: In chemistry, scission occurs when a chemical bond breaks, sometimes dividing a molecular chain into smaller pieces.
senses.collocation_zh: 分子链断裂；化学键断裂
senses.sentence_en: Exposure to ultraviolet light can cause chain scission in some polymers.
senses.sentence_zh: 紫外线照射可使某些聚合物发生分子链断裂。

etymology_story.zh: 源自表示“切开、分裂”的拉丁语 scissio，与拉丁语 scindere（切开、劈开）的分词词干 sciss- 有关。其“分开”的核心意义后来用于描述化学键、分子链等结构的断裂。
etymology_story.en: The word derives from Latin scissio, a cutting or splitting, associated with sciss-, the participial stem of scindere, to cut or split. Its central idea of separation later supported technical uses for the breaking of chemical bonds and molecular chains.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按拉丁语来源的词干 sciss-（切开、分裂）+ -ion（动作或过程名词后缀）理解，但不是现代英语自由词根的组合。相关词包括 scissile（易裂开的；可被切断的）、scissility（易裂性）和同源的 rescind（撤销）；scission 的复数为 scissions。此处 CEFR-C2 为教学难度估计，并非经核实的官方逐词评级。
morphology_enriched.en: The word can be understood as the Latin-derived stem sciss-, meaning cut or split, plus the process-noun ending -ion; it is not a combination of independent modern English words. Related vocabulary includes scissile, scissility, and the cognate rescind. Its plural is scissions. The CEFR-C2 tag is a teaching-level estimate, not a verified official word rating.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: splitting（分裂）最通用；cleavage（劈裂；裂解）常强调沿某一界面分开或化学键断裂；fission（裂变；分裂）常用于原子核或生物体的分裂。scission 尤其适合描述连接处或分子链被切断。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Splitting is the broad everyday term. Cleavage often concerns separation along an interface or the breaking of chemical bonds. Fission commonly describes nuclear or biological division. Scission is particularly useful when a connection or molecular chain is severed.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 sciss- 的“切开”逻辑：连接断开，整体分成几部分。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep the cutting logic of sciss-: a connection breaks and a whole separates into parts.

etymology_story.zh: 来自拉丁语 Silenus，源于古希腊语 Silēnos。该名称既用于狄俄尼索斯身边的特定神话人物，也与一类林野精灵的名称有关；英语中的大小写用法保留了这种专名与类名的区别。
etymology_story.en: The name comes through Latin Silenus from Greek Silēnos. It names a particular companion of Dionysus and is also associated with a class of woodland spirits; English capitalization distinguishes the individual name from the common noun.

morphology_enriched.zh: Silenus 是借入的完整专名，现代英语中不宜拆成具有独立意义的词根和后缀。相关形式：Silenic（西勒诺斯的；具有其特征的，罕见形容词）；小写类名 silenus 的传统复数为 sileni。此处 CEFR-C2 仅表示阅读此类专业文化词汇所需的估计难度，专名本身没有经核实的官方 CEFR 逐词评级。
morphology_enriched.en: Silenus is a borrowed proper name and should not be divided into independently meaningful modern English roots and suffixes. Related forms include the rare adjective Silenic, meaning relating to or resembling Silenus; the common noun silenus traditionally has the plural sileni. CEFR-C2 indicates an estimated reading difficulty for this specialist cultural vocabulary; the proper name has no verified official CEFR word rating.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 专名 Silenus 没有严格近义词。相关称谓包括 tutor of Dionysus（狄俄尼索斯的导师）和 companion of Dionysus（狄俄尼索斯的伙伴）；satyr（萨堤尔）是相关神话精灵的类别名称，不能在所有语境中替代该专名。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The proper name Silenus has no exact synonym. Tutor of Dionysus and companion of Dionysus are descriptive alternatives. Satyr names a related category of mythological spirit and cannot replace the proper name in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the character through a scene: the wine god's elderly tutor riding a donkey.

senses.meaning_zh: 首领；头人；军事统帅，尤指南亚地区的称号

etymology_story.zh: 英语经南亚语言借入这一称号，最终源自波斯语 sardār，由 sar（头）和 -dār（持有者）组成，指居于领导地位的人。英语中的 sirdar 也曾专指埃及军队的总司令。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the title through South Asian languages from Persian sardār, formed from sar, meaning 'head', and -dār, meaning 'holder'. In English, sirdar also became the historical title of the commander-in-chief of the Egyptian army.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 sirdar 视为不可进一步拆分的借词词干。词形与派生：sirdar → sirdars（复数）；sirdar + -ship → sirdarship（首领的职位或身份，罕见）。sardar 是相关拼写变体，不是派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, sirdar functions as an unanalysed borrowed stem. Forms and derivatives: sirdar → sirdars, the plural; sirdar + -ship → sirdarship, a rare noun for a chief's office or status. Sardar is a related spelling variant, not a derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chief emphasizes the highest position within a group; leader is the broadest term; commander emphasizes military authority. Sirdar carries a particular regional and historical association as a title.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史词源中的“头”对应群体的“领头人”：sirdar → 首领。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the historical element 'head' with the person at the head of a group: sirdar → chief.

etymology_story.en: Sneck goes back to Middle English forms such as snek and snekke, meaning a latch; its earlier origin is uncertain. It survives chiefly in Scottish and northern English dialects and also functions as a verb meaning to fasten a latch.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：sneck（门搭扣，名词）→ sneck（扣上搭扣，零派生动词）。词形：snecks、snecked、snecking；un-（解除）+ sneck → unsneck（解开门搭扣），相应词形为 unsnecks、unsnecked、unsnecking。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: sneck, the noun meaning a latch, → sneck, a verb formed by conversion. Inflected forms are snecks, snecked, and snecking. The reversative prefix un- + sneck gives unsneck, meaning to unlatch, with forms unsnecks, unsnecked, and unsnecking.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 名词 latch（门搭扣）是最直接的通用对应词；catch（扣件）范围更广，可指多种固定装置。动词 latch（扣上搭扣）对应 sneck 的动作义，但没有其地域色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: As a noun, latch is the closest general equivalent, while catch covers a wider range of fastening devices. As a verb, latch expresses the same basic action as sneck without its regional associations.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一个 sneck 是门搭扣；把门 sneck 起来，就是把搭扣扣上。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A sneck is the latch; to sneck the door is to put that latch into place.

senses.meaning_zh: 稍加修饰；整理仪容；打扮，常用于英式非正式语境
senses.meaning_en: To make small improvements to someone's appearance or to the appearance of something.
senses.english_definition: If you titivate yourself or something, you make small changes to make yourself or it look neater or more attractive.

etymology_story.zh: titivate 是十九世纪较早形式 tidivate 的变体，通常认为与 tidy（整洁的；整理）有关，但具体构词过程并不确定。它表示通过细小修整使外表更整齐或更好看。
etymology_story.en: Titivate developed in the nineteenth century as a variant of the earlier tidivate, usually associated with tidy, although its precise formation is uncertain. It refers to improving appearances through small adjustments.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 titivate 视为整体动词词干，不宜硬拆成具有确定意义的前缀和词根。词形：titivates、titivated、titivating；派生：titivat(e) + -ion → titivation（修饰；打扮），titivat(e) + -or → titivator（进行修饰的人，罕见）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, titivate is best treated as a whole verb stem rather than divided into independently meaningful parts. Inflections are titivates, titivated, and titivating. Derivatives include titivat(e) + -ion → titivation, the act of making such improvements, and titivat(e) + -or → titivator, a rare term for someone who does so.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: spruce up（收拾得整洁漂亮）可用于人或场所；smarten up（使更整洁精神）强调外观改善；preen（精心打扮、自我欣赏）常带自得意味。titivate 尤其强调细小、略带琐碎意味的修饰。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Spruce up applies to making people or places neat and attractive; smarten up emphasizes a more presentable appearance; preen often suggests self-admiration while grooming. Titivate particularly suggests small, sometimes fussy adjustments.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 tidy（整理）当作联想线索：小整理，小修饰，便是 titivate。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use tidy as an association: a little tidying and touching up → titivate.

senses.meaning_zh: 水痘，医学用语
senses.meaning_en: The medical term for chickenpox.
senses.english_definition: Varicella is an infectious disease, commonly called chickenpox, that causes an itchy rash with small blisters.
senses.collocation_zh: 水痘疫苗；水痘感染
senses.sentence_en: The report used the medical term varicella for chickenpox.
senses.sentence_zh: 这份报告使用医学术语 varicella 来指水痘。

etymology_story.zh: varicella 来自新拉丁语，是在 variola（天花）基础上形成的变体指小形式。这个名称反映了两种疾病在痘疹外观上的历史联系，并不表示它们是同一种疾病。
etymology_story.en: Varicella comes from New Latin as an altered diminutive of variola, meaning smallpox. The name reflects a historical association between their eruptions, although they are distinct diseases.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 varicella 是整体医学名词；其历史指小结构不宜当作现代英语的自由构词公式。相关派生有 varicell(a) + -ar → varicellar（水痘的）、varicell(a) + -ous → varicellous（水痘的，较少见）；相关复合术语有 varicella-zoster virus（水痘-带状疱疹病毒）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, varicella is a whole medical noun; its historical diminutive structure is not a productive English formation. Related derivatives include varicell(a) + -ar → varicellar and varicell(a) + -ous → varicellous, a less common adjective, both meaning relating to chickenpox. A related compound term is varicella-zoster virus.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chickenpox（水痘）是日常用语中的直接同义词；primary varicella-zoster virus infection（水痘-带状疱疹病毒原发感染）是强调病因的医学释义。varicella 属于医学语域；shingles（带状疱疹）不是它的同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chickenpox is the direct everyday synonym; primary varicella-zoster virus infection is a medical paraphrase emphasizing the cause. Varicella belongs to the medical register; shingles is not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史上的“小痘病”名称 → 医学词 varicella → 日常词 chickenpox（水痘）。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Historical 'little pox' naming → medical varicella → everyday chickenpox.

senses.meaning_zh: 唉；哎呀，表示悲伤或遗憾，属古旧或戏仿用语
senses.meaning_en: An old-fashioned exclamation expressing sorrow or regret.
senses.english_definition: People say alack to express sadness or regret, especially in old literature or when imitating its style.
senses.collocation_en: alas and alack; alack the day
senses.collocation_zh: 唉呀，真是不幸；唉，真是倒霉的一天
senses.sentence_en: Alack, we have arrived too late!
senses.sentence_zh: 唉，我们来得太晚了！

etymology_story.zh: alack 可追溯到中古英语 alak 等形式，通常解释为感叹成分 a 与表示损失或不幸的 lack 结合而成。它原本用于哀叹，如今主要见于旧文学或刻意模仿古风的表达。
etymology_story.en: Alack goes back to Middle English forms such as alak and is usually explained as the exclamation a combined with lack in the sense of loss or misfortune. Once an expression of lament, it now occurs chiefly in older literature or deliberately archaic speech.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 alack 是固定感叹词，没有常用屈折变化或能产派生。相关历史表达：alack + the day → alack the day（哀叹语）；该短语也形成连写形式 alackaday。the day 是短语成分，不是后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, alack is a fixed interjection with no usual inflections or productive derivatives. A related historical expression is alack + the day → alack the day, a lament, which also produced the fused form alackaday. The day is a phrase component, not a suffix.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: alas（唉；可惜）同样表达悲伤或遗憾，但现代正式文字中仍可见；oh dear（哎呀）更口语化，常表示轻度担忧或失望。alack 的古旧、戏剧化色彩更强。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Alas similarly expresses sorrow or regret and still appears in modern formal writing; oh dear is more conversational and often expresses mild concern or disappointment. Alack sounds more strongly archaic and theatrical.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联想“啊，失去了！”：a + lack 的历史线索 → 遗憾的一声“唉”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'Ah, a loss!': the historical a + lack association anchors a sigh of regret.
