senses.meaning_zh: 【非正式，略带粗俗色彩】赶快；马上；迅速地
senses.meaning_en: Very quickly or immediately, in informal and sometimes mildly vulgar usage.
senses.english_definition: If you tell someone to do something PDQ, you mean that they should do it very quickly or without delay.
senses.collocation_en: get here PDQ; get it done PDQ
senses.collocation_zh: 马上到这里来；赶快把它做完
senses.sentence_en: We need to get this leak fixed PDQ.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们得赶快把这个漏水问题修好。

etymology_story.zh: PDQ 是 pretty damn quick（非常快；赶快）的首字母缩写，十九世纪已有记录。后来也常用较委婉的 pretty darn quick 来解释这三个字母。[词源依据](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/pdq)
etymology_story.en: PDQ originated in the nineteenth century as an initialism of pretty damn quick. The milder expansion pretty darn quick is also used. [Etymology source](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/pdq)

morphology_enriched.zh: P(retty) + D(amn/darn) + Q(uick) → PDQ，属于逐字母读出的首字母缩写，不是词根加词缀。变体拼写有 pdq 和 P.D.Q.；没有常用派生词或屈折变化。
morphology_enriched.en: P(retty) + D(amn/darn) + Q(uick) → PDQ, an initialism pronounced letter by letter rather than a root-and-affix formation. Written variants include pdq and P.D.Q.; there are no common derivatives or inflected forms.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: quickly（迅速地）侧重动作速度；immediately（立即）侧重没有等待；pronto（马上）同样口语化，常带催促意味。PDQ 兼有“快”和“别耽搁”的催促语气。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Quickly emphasizes speed; immediately emphasizes the absence of delay; pronto is similarly informal and often sounds like an urgent instruction. PDQ combines speed with an insistent demand for prompt action.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 三个字母就是三个催促词：Pretty Damn Quick——赶快办。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Expand the three letters into the urgent instruction Pretty Damn Quick.

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆。peart + -ly → peartly（精神饱满地）。

usage_note: 主要见于美国南部和中部方言，标准日常英语更常用 lively 或 cheerful。

senses.meaning_zh: 【方言，尤见于美国南部及中部】精神饱满的；活泼的；身体爽健的
senses.meaning_en: Lively, cheerful, or feeling well, especially in regional American usage.
senses.english_definition: Someone who is peart is lively and cheerful, especially when they are feeling better after an illness.
senses.collocation_zh: 感到精神不错；看起来精神饱满
senses.sentence_en: Grandma was feeling peart enough to work in the garden again.
senses.sentence_zh: 奶奶感觉精神恢复得不错，又能到花园里干活了。

etymology_story.zh: peart 是 pert 的变体，而 pert 是中古英语 apert 的缩略形式，最终源自拉丁语 apertus“敞开的”。peart 保留了“活泼；精神好”的积极意义，而 pert 后来还发展出“冒失；无礼”的含义。[词源依据](https://www.etymonline.com/word/peart)
etymology_story.en: Peart is a variant of pert, a shortened form of Middle English apert, ultimately from Latin apertus, meaning 'open'. Peart preserves the positive sense of liveliness, whereas pert also developed the meaning 'impudent'. [Etymology source](https://www.etymonline.com/word/peart)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以 peart 为完整词基，不应拆为 pear + -t。词族包括 peart + -ly → peartly（活泼地；精神饱满地）、peart + -ness → peartness（活力；爽健）及方言动词 pearten（使振作；振作起来）；比较级为 pearter，最高级为 peartest。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat peart as a complete modern base, not pear + -t. Its family includes peart + -ly → peartly ('in a lively manner'), peart + -ness → peartness ('liveliness or good spirits'), and the dialect verb pearten ('to enliven or become livelier'); its comparative and superlative are pearter and peartest.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: lively（活泼的）强调活动力；sprightly（精神矍铄的）突出轻快有活力，常用于年长者；cheerful（心情愉快的）主要强调情绪。peart 常同时表示心情好和身体恢复精神。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lively emphasizes activity; sprightly suggests light, energetic movement, often in an older person; cheerful mainly describes mood. Peart can combine good spirits with a sense of physical recovery.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 peart 与 pert 的“活泼”旧义相连：病后重新精神起来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link peart to the lively sense of pert: picture someone brightening up after an illness.

pronunciation.note: 采用 Oxford 英式读音 /ˈwɒtʃə/。

forms: 感叹词，不变形。
family: what cheer? 是历史来源短语；hello 是现代常用对应表达。

morphology.text: what + cheer → what cheer? → wotcha（你好）；这是旧招呼语连读后形成的词，整词记忆。

etymology.text: 十九世纪末由英语旧式问候 what cheer? 的读音变化而来。把它联想成见面时轻快的一声招呼。

usage_note: 英国非正式口语，表示见面招呼，类似 hello。句首按常规写 Wotcha；不是提问，也不是道别。

senses.meaning_zh: 嗨；你好（英国俚语，用于随意打招呼）
senses.meaning_en: hello; an informal British greeting
senses.english_definition: You say 'wotcha' when you greet someone in a very informal, friendly way.
senses.collocation_zh: 嗨，伙计！；大家好！
senses.sentence_en: “Wotcha, mate!” he called as I walked into the pub.
senses.sentence_zh: 我走进酒吧时，他喊道：“嗨，伙计！”

etymology_story.zh: wotcha 是旧式问候语 what cheer? 的口语缩合形式，通常与变体 wotcher 联系在一起。原先询问对方近况的表达，后来凝固为相当于“你好”的招呼语。
etymology_story.en: Wotcha is a colloquial contraction of the older greeting 'what cheer?', associated with the alternative spelling wotcher. An expression asking how someone was doing became a fixed greeting meaning 'hello'.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为不可再分析的独立感叹词使用，没有可产的前缀、后缀或常用派生词族；wotcher 是拼写变体，不是派生词。历史上的短语缩合不等于现代的词根加词缀构词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, wotcha functions as an unanalyzable interjection, with no productive prefix, suffix, or established derivative family. Wotcher is a spelling variant rather than a derivative; the historical phrase contraction is not a modern root-plus-affix formation. [Collins English Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/wotcha)

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hello（你好）最通用，适用场合广；hi（嗨）轻松而常见；hiya（嗨）同样亲切随意。wotcha 的英国地域色彩和俚语色彩更明显，有时带有诙谐或老派口吻。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hello is the most generally applicable greeting; hi is relaxed and widespread; hiya is similarly friendly and informal. Wotcha has a stronger British slang flavor and can sound jocular or old-fashioned.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 what cheer? 连读压缩成 wotcha：问近况，变成见面的一声“嗨”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Compress 'what cheer?' into wotcha: asking how someone is becomes a quick 'hello'.

pronunciation.note: Collins 在英语词条中保留法语读音 /avjɔ̃/；末尾为鼻化元音，不把 n 单独读出。

forms: 单数 avion；复数 avions，目录同时记录这两种形式。
family: aviation 航空；avian 鸟类的，二者共享拉丁语 avis 的来源。

morphology.text: 历史构词：avi-（拉丁语 avis，鸟）+ -on（法语名词后缀）→ avion（飞机）。作为英语借词时整词记忆。

etymology.text: 英语从法语借入 avion，法语造词以拉丁语 avis“鸟”为基础。把飞机想成机械的鸟，有助于记住它。

usage_note: 法语借词，英语中罕用且带法语色彩；日常英语优先用 aircraft、airplane 或 aeroplane。本卡展示词典保留的法语读法。

senses.meaning_zh: 飞机（英语中的罕见法语借词）
senses.meaning_en: an airplane; a rare French loanword in English
senses.english_definition: An avion is an airplane; the word is occasionally borrowed from French into English.
senses.collocation_en: Rare contextual combinations: an early avion; a military avion
senses.collocation_zh: 罕见语境组合：早期飞机；军用飞机
senses.sentence_en: The French caption identifies the aircraft as an “avion”.
senses.sentence_zh: 法文说明用“avion”一词指称这架飞机。

etymology_story.zh: 英语 avion 借自法语，法语词以拉丁语 avis“鸟”为基础创造。它把鸟类飞行的意象用于人造飞行器；现代普通英语通常使用 plane、airplane 或 aeroplane。[《韦氏词典》](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/avion)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed avion from French, where the word was coined from Latin avis, meaning 'bird'. It applies the image of a flying bird to a human-made aircraft; ordinary modern English generally uses plane, airplane, or aeroplane. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/avion)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 avion 作为整体借词使用，不宜把它分析为英语中可自由组合的 avi- + -on；复数为 avions。相关词根家族包括 avian（鸟类的）、aviation（航空）、aviator（飞行员）和 aviary（大型鸟舍）；这些词并非都直接由 avion 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats avion as a whole-word borrowing, not as a productive English combination of avi- and -on; its plural is avions. Its broader root family includes avian, aviation, aviator, and aviary, although these are not all direct derivatives of avion.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: airplane（飞机）是美式英语常用词；aeroplane（飞机）是英式英语对应词；aircraft（航空器）范围更广，还包括直升机等。avion 在英语中罕见，通常保留明显的法语色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Airplane is the usual American term; aeroplane is its British counterpart; aircraft is broader and also includes vehicles such as helicopters. Avion is rare in English and generally retains a distinctly French flavor.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: avis＝鸟：avion 就是飞上天空的“机械鸟”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Avis means 'bird': picture an avion as a mechanical bird.

forms: 单数 cuttle；规则复数 cuttles。本卡不采用同形动词的变化。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆。cuttle + fish → cuttlefish（乌贼），这是常见的复合词形式。

etymology.text: 从古英语 cudele 经中古英语 cotul、codull 传到现代英语。cuttlefish 保留这个老词，再加 fish 帮助人们辨认海洋动物。

usage_note: 本卡取名词动物义，是 cuttlefish 的较少见说法；不要与 cuddle“拥抱”混淆。

senses.meaning_zh: 乌贼；墨鱼（cuttlefish 的较少见名称）
senses.meaning_en: a cuttlefish

senses.collocation_zh: 专门语境组合：一块乌贼骨；供鸟食用的乌贼骨

senses.meaning_zh: 将整理后的布匹折叠成层（纺织术语，及物）
senses.meaning_en: to fold finished cloth into successive pleats or layers
senses.english_definition: If a machine cuttles cloth, it folds the finished cloth back and forth into an orderly stack.
senses.collocation_en: Technical combinations: cuttle cloth; a cuttling machine

etymology_story.zh: 动物名称 cuttle 经中古英语 cotul、codull 源自古英语 cudele，保存在复合词 cuttlefish 中，并可转指乌贼骨。纺织动词来自表示“折叠的一层布”的另一个 cuttle，其更早来源不明，不应解释为动物名称的引申。[《韦氏词典》](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/cuttle)
etymology_story.en: The animal name cuttle comes through Middle English cotul and codull from Old English cudele, survives in cuttlefish, and can also denote cuttlebone. The textile verb comes from a separate noun meaning a folded layer of cloth, of uncertain earlier origin, rather than from the animal name. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/cuttle)

morphology_enriched.zh: cuttle 是独立词基，不可拆成 cut + -tle。动物义的主要复合词为 cuttle + fish → cuttlefish（乌贼）和 cuttle + bone → cuttlebone（乌贼骨）；纺织动词的屈折形式为 cuttles、cuttled、cuttling，相关表达有 cuttling machine（折布机）。
morphology_enriched.en: Cuttle is a free base, not cut plus a suffix -tle. Its main animal-related compounds are cuttle + fish → cuttlefish and cuttle + bone → cuttlebone; the textile verb has the forms cuttles, cuttled, and cuttling, with cuttling machine as a related technical expression.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cuttlefish（乌贼）是动物义更常用、更明确的同义词；cuttlebone（乌贼骨）专指其硬质内壳；pleat（打褶、折叠）与纺织动词义接近，但适用范围更广。squid（鱿鱼）是另一类头足动物，不是严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cuttlefish is the clearer and more usual synonym for the animal; cuttlebone specifically names its hard internal shell; pleat overlaps with the textile verb but has a wider range of uses. Squid names a different group of cephalopods and is not an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 动物义连记 cuttlefish 和 cuttlebone：乌贼与乌贼骨；纺织义另记“布匹来回折成层”，两条词源分开。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the animal sense to cuttlefish and cuttlebone; separately picture cloth folding back and forth for the textile verb.

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆。dewan + -ship → dewanship（dewan 的职位或任期）。

etymology.text: 经印地语 dīwān 借入，往前是波斯语中表示“账簿”的词。由管账的线索记住这位财政官员。

usage_note: 印度历史官职名，也拼 diwan；有些历史语境另指土邦首相。本卡限定财政大臣义，不能泛指所有官员。

etymology_story.zh: dewan 经印地语 dīwān 借入英语，其上源是表示“账簿、登记册”的波斯语词。词义从行政账册及其管理机构发展到掌管财政的官员，并用于某些印度土邦首席大臣的头衔。[《韦氏词典》](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/dewan)
etymology_story.en: Dewan entered English through Hindi dīwān, ultimately from a Persian word for an account book or register. Its meaning developed from administrative records and their offices to officials managing finance, and it also became a title for the chief minister of certain Indian princely states. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/dewan)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 dewan 作为整体借词使用，没有可分析的英语前后缀；复数为 dewans，diwan 是拼写变体。dewan + -ship → dewanship（迪万的职位或任期，罕见）；相关历史词 dewani／diwani 指迪万的职权，尤其是财政或税收管理权。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats dewan as a whole-word borrowing without analyzable English affixes; its plural is dewans, and diwan is a spelling variant. Dewan + -ship gives the rare dewanship, meaning the office or tenure; the related historical term dewani or diwani concerns a dewan's authority, especially over revenue administration.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: finance minister（财政大臣）对应财政职能；chief minister（首席大臣）对应土邦行政首长职能；vizier（维齐尔、大臣）是某些伊斯兰政权中的高级官员头衔。三者只能按历史语境对应，不能一概替换 dewan。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Finance minister matches the financial role; chief minister matches the role of head of a princely state's administration; vizier is a senior ministerial title in certain Islamic governments. These terms overlap with dewan only in particular historical contexts.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 账簿 → 管账的高官 → 财政大臣或首席大臣。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Account book → senior official in charge of accounts → finance minister or chief minister.

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆。日语复合例：hira-（普通的）+ kana（假名）→ hiragana（平假名）；复合时 k 浊化为 g。

etymology.text: 直接借自日语 kana“假名”。把两套熟悉的名称 hiragana、katakana 放在一起，就能记住它是统称。

usage_note: kana 统称日语假名，包含 hiragana 和 katakana；英语中通常小写，复数仍作 kana。

senses.meaning_zh: 日语假名；平假名和片假名的统称
senses.meaning_en: the Japanese phonetic writing systems hiragana and katakana collectively
senses.english_definition: Kana is the Japanese system of phonetic writing that includes hiragana and katakana.
senses.collocation_zh: 用假名书写；假名字符
senses.sentence_en: Beginners usually learn kana before studying many kanji.

senses.meaning_zh: 一个假名字符
senses.meaning_en: an individual character in hiragana or katakana
senses.english_definition: A kana is a character belonging to either hiragana or katakana, usually representing a unit of Japanese sound called a mora.
senses.collocation_zh: 单个假名字符；每个假名字符
senses.sentence_en: The teacher asked us to copy each kana five times.
senses.sentence_zh: 老师要求我们把每个假名抄写五遍。

etymology_story.zh: kana 借自日语“仮名”，历史上与 kari“临时的、借用的”和 na“名称、文字”有关，指借汉字表音而形成的文字。英语将其用于假名系统及其中的单个字符。[《柯林斯英语词典》](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/kana)
etymology_story.en: Kana was borrowed from Japanese 仮名, historically associated with kari, 'temporary or borrowed', and na, 'name or written sign', referring to writing developed by using Chinese characters phonetically. English uses the word for the writing systems and for individual characters within them. [Collins English Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/kana)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 kana 作为整体借词使用，复数通常仍为 kana；kana characters 中的 kana 是名词作定语，不必另立形容词词性。相关日语复合借词有 hiragana（平假名）、katakana（片假名）、furigana（注音假名）、hentaigana（变体假名）和 man'yōgana（万叶假名）；部分复合词中的 k 因日语连浊变为 g，并非英语派生规则。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats kana as a whole-word borrowing, normally with the unchanged plural kana; in kana characters, it is a noun modifier rather than a separate adjective. Related Japanese compound borrowings include hiragana, katakana, furigana, hentaigana, and man'yōgana; the change from k to g in some compounds is Japanese rendaku, not an English derivational rule.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: syllabary（音节文字系统）是较宽泛的类别词，假名严格说主要记录音拍；hiragana（平假名）和 katakana（片假名）是 kana 的两个子类，不能各自完全替代其统称。kanji（汉字）属于另一套文字，不是 kana 的同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Syllabary is the broader conventional category, although kana primarily represent morae rather than syllables. Hiragana and katakana name the two constituent systems, so neither alone replaces the collective term kana; kanji names a different writing system.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hiragana ＋ katakana 共同归入 kana：两套表音字符，一个统称。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hiragana and katakana both belong under kana: two phonetic scripts, one umbrella term.

forms: 形容词；比较程度用 more lorn、most lorn。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆。love + lorn → lovelorn（因失恋而伤心的），lorn 保留“失去、被留下”的感觉。

etymology.text: 由古英语 lēosan“失去”，经中古英语 lesen 的过去分词 loren，发展成 lorn。失去所依靠的人，便有了孤苦的情绪。

usage_note: 主要用于文学，语气比普通的 alone 更带失落、被遗弃感；日常更常见 forlorn。

etymology_story.zh: lorn 源自古英语 loren，是 lēosan（失去）的过去分词，后来发生词形缩短。它从“失去的、被留下的”发展出“被遗弃而孤苦的”这一文学意义。
etymology_story.en: Lorn comes from Old English loren, the past participle of lēosan, meaning 'to lose', with later shortening of the form. Its meaning developed from 'lost or left behind' into the literary sense 'abandoned and lonely'.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，lorn 通常作为不可再作有效拆分的形容词理解，没有能产的前后缀结构。常见复合词为 love（爱情）+ lorn → lovelorn（因单恋或失恋而痛苦的）；forlorn（孤苦绝望的）是历史上的同源词，不宜按现代前缀规则机械分析。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, lorn is normally treated as an adjective without a productive internal affix structure. Its established compound is love + lorn → lovelorn, meaning unhappy because of unreturned or lost love; forlorn is historically related rather than a transparent modern prefix formation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: forlorn（孤苦绝望的）突出无助和希望渺茫；desolate（孤寂凄凉的）强调深切的空虚与悲伤；bereft（失去所爱或所依的）强调具体的丧失。lorn 带有更鲜明的诗歌或古雅色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Forlorn emphasizes helplessness and little hope; desolate stresses profound emptiness and sadness; bereft emphasizes the loss of someone or something valued. Lorn has a more distinctly poetic or old-fashioned tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史核心是“失去”：失去依靠，被留下来，便是 lorn。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with the historical idea of loss: someone left without support is lorn.

forms: 单数 pinfold；复数 pinfolds，目录记录了两种形式。
family: fold 畜栏；pound 也可指走失动物的收容圈。

morphology.text: 历史复合：pund-（围住的地方）+ fald（畜栏）→ 古英语 pundfald → pinfold（走失牲畜的收容圈）。这里的 pin 不是“别针”。

etymology.text: 来自古英语复合词 pundfald，经中古英语传下；两部分都和围圈有关，可以联想到把走失的牲畜围好，等待主人来领。

usage_note: 偏历史或地方用语，指收容走失牲畜的圈栏；不是常规买卖牲畜的市场。

senses.meaning_zh: 关押走失牲畜的围栏或畜圈（主要见于英国历史、地方用语）
senses.meaning_en: An enclosure for stray livestock, chiefly in British historical or regional usage.
senses.english_definition: A pinfold is an enclosure where stray farm animals are kept until their owners collect them.
senses.collocation_en: the village pinfold; a stone pinfold

senses.meaning_zh: 把牲畜关入收容圈；圈禁（罕用或古旧用法）
senses.meaning_en: To put animals in a pound or confine them; rare or archaic.
senses.english_definition: If someone pinfolds animals, they shut them inside an enclosure.
senses.collocation_en: pinfold stray cattle; pinfold the sheep
senses.collocation_zh: 把走失的牛关入收容圈；把羊圈起来
senses.sentence_en: The villagers pinfolded the stray cattle before nightfall.
senses.sentence_zh: 村民们在天黑前把走失的牛关进了收容圈。

etymology_story.zh: pinfold 可追溯到古英语 pundfald，由表示牲畜收容圈的 pund 和表示畜栏的 fald 组成。它经中古英语形式演变而来，词首的 pin 与“别针”无关。
etymology_story.en: Pinfold goes back to Old English pundfald, combining pund, an animal pound, with fald, a fold or enclosure. It developed through Middle English forms, and its first element is unrelated to pin meaning a small fastening object.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 pinfold 作为完整词项使用；历史上可分析为 pund（牲畜收容圈）+ fald（畜栏）。名词复数为 pinfolds；同形动词的屈折形式为 pinfolds、pinfolded、pinfolding。相关词 pound（牲畜收容所）和 fold（畜圈）并非由现代 pinfold 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats pinfold as a whole lexical item; historically it consists of pund 'animal pound' + fald 'fold'. The noun plural is pinfolds; verb forms are pinfolds, pinfolded, and pinfolding. The related words pound and fold are not modern derivatives of pinfold.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pound（走失动物收容所）最接近其收容和待领功能；pen（畜栏）泛指限制动物活动的围栏；fold（羊圈、畜圈）常指日常饲养或夜间圈护的场所。pinfold 尤其带有英国地方史色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pound is closest in its function of holding stray animals for collection; pen is a general enclosure that restricts animals' movement; fold often refers to an enclosure used for routine shelter, especially for sheep. Pinfold particularly evokes British local history.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 fold“畜圈”：把走失牲畜圈好，等主人来领。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to fold, an animal enclosure: stray livestock are enclosed until their owners return.

forms: 单数 aqua；本义复数 aquae。不要再加 -s；颜色义另用 aquas。
family: aqua 水；水剂；aqueous 水的、水性的。

morphology.text: 拉丁式词形：aqu-（aqua 的词干，水）+ -ae（复数词尾）→ aquae（水剂，复数）。这是词形变化，不是新的派生词。

etymology.text: 英语借入拉丁语 aqua“水”，并在传统用法中保留拉丁语复数 aquae。看到 aqu- 就想到水。

usage_note: 这是 aqua 在“水、药用水剂”义下的拉丁式复数。aqua 表示水绿色时，复数是 aquas，不用 aquae。本卡只学复数水剂义。

senses.meaning_zh: 药用水剂；芳香水剂（aqua 的拉丁式复数，传统药剂学用语）
senses.meaning_en: Medicinal or aromatic waters; the traditional pharmaceutical plural of aqua.
senses.english_definition: Aquae are water-based preparations, especially aromatic waters, used in traditional pharmacy.
senses.collocation_zh: 芳香水剂；药用水剂
senses.sentence_en: The old pharmacy manual listed several aquae used to flavor medicines.
senses.sentence_zh: 那本旧药剂学手册列出了几种用于给药物调味的芳香水剂。

etymology_story.zh: 英语在药剂学等专门领域借用了拉丁语 aqua（水），并保留其拉丁语主格复数 aquae。这个复数形式因此常见于传统药用水剂或芳香水剂的分类名称。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Latin aqua, meaning 'water', in specialist fields such as pharmacy and retained its Latin nominative plural aquae. The plural consequently appears in traditional classifications of medicinal and aromatic waters.

morphology_enriched.zh: aquae 是 aqua 的屈折形式，不是新派生词：aqua 的词尾 -a 换为拉丁式复数词尾 -ae → aquae。相关水义词族包括 aqueous（水的；水溶液的）、aquatic（水生的；水中的）、aquifer（含水层）和 aqueduct（输水道）；这些词与 aqua 共享拉丁语词源，并非由 aquae 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Aquae is an inflected form of aqua, not a new derivative: replace the final -a of aqua with the Latin plural ending -ae. Related water words include aqueous, aquatic, aquifer, and aqueduct; they share Latin ancestry with aqua rather than being derived from aquae.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: medicinal waters（药用水）强调治疗或药剂用途；aromatic waters（芳香水剂）特指含芳香物质的水性制剂；aqueous preparations（水性制剂）范围更广。aquae 是传统拉丁式药剂学名称，不能与所有水溶液完全等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Medicinal waters emphasizes therapeutic or pharmaceutical use; aromatic waters specifically denotes aqueous preparations containing aromatic substances; aqueous preparations is broader. Aquae is a traditional Latin-form pharmaceutical term and is not interchangeable with every kind of aqueous solution.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: aqua 是“水”，-ae 标示拉丁式复数：多种药用水剂。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Aqua means water; -ae marks the Latin plural: several medicinal waters.

forms: 比较级 burrier；最高级 burriest。
family: burr/bur 带刺、会黏附的果实；burry 是相应形容词。

morphology.text: burr/bur（带钩刺的果实）+ -y（带有……的）→ burry（沾有刺果的）；写 burry 时保留双 r。

etymology.text: 由英语 burr/bur 加形容词后缀而成；基础词可追溯到中古英语 burre。想想刺果挂在毛上的样子，就记住了这个形容词。

usage_note: 本卡取“含有或沾着刺果”的意思；另可形容刺人的触感或带颤音的说话声。不要与 bury“埋葬”混淆。

sentence: The dog came home with a burry coat after running through the hedge.

senses.meaning_zh: 长有或沾满刺果的；多刺果的
senses.meaning_en: Bearing, containing, or covered with burs.

senses.meaning_zh: 嗓音粗涩的；说话带明显颤舌音的
senses.meaning_en: Having a rough vocal quality or a noticeably burred pronunciation.
senses.english_definition: A burry voice has a rough sound or a noticeable rolling or throaty pronunciation of certain sounds, especially r.
senses.collocation_en: a burry voice; a burry accent

senses.sentence_en: He greeted us in a low, burry voice.
senses.sentence_zh: 他用低沉而略带粗涩的嗓音向我们问好。

etymology_story.zh: burry 由 burr 或 bur 加形容词后缀 -y 构成；表示刺果的基础词可追溯到中古英语 burre。声音方面的意义对应 burr 的另一用法，即粗涩或带颤舌音的说话声。
etymology_story.en: Burry is formed from burr or bur with the adjective suffix -y; the plant word goes back to Middle English burre. Its vocal meaning corresponds to another use of burr for a rough or noticeably rolled quality in speech.

morphology_enriched.zh: burr（刺果；粗涩或颤舌音）+ -y（具有……特征的）→ burry。采用 bur 拼写时，加 -y 前双写 r；比较级和最高级为 burrier、burriest，也可按语境使用 more burry、most burry。相关词族包括 bur/burr、burred（带刺果的；有毛刺的）和 burring（形成毛刺；发出粗涩或颤舌音）。
morphology_enriched.en: Burr 'prickly seed case; rough or rolled speech sound' + -y 'having the quality of' → burry. With the spelling bur, double the r before adding -y; comparative and superlative forms are burrier and burriest, with more burry and most burry also possible in context. Related forms include bur/burr, burred, and burring.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: prickly（多刺的）强调尖刺带来的触感，不一定有刺果；raspy（嗓音粗哑的）强调摩擦般的粗涩声音；trilled（发成颤音的）强调发音时的振动。burry 可具体表示沾有刺果，也可形容粗涩或带颤舌音的声音。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Prickly emphasizes a sharp, spiny texture without necessarily implying burs; raspy emphasizes a rough, scraping voice; trilled emphasizes vibration in articulation. Burry can specifically describe burs caught on something or a rough or burred quality of speech.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: burr + y：皮毛上“带刺果”，声音里“带粗涩或颤音”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Burr + y: burs in a coat, or a burr in a voice.

forms: 单数 dolman；复数 dolmans。
family: dolman sleeve 蝙蝠袖；dolman 另有骑兵短上衣义。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆。dolman + sleeve → dolman sleeve（蝙蝠袖；袖窿宽、袖口窄的袖型），这是固定的复合服饰名称。

etymology.text: 从土耳其语 dolama 经法语形式 doliman 演变为英语 dolman；土耳其语原词与“缠绕、裹住”有关，容易联想到裹身的宽松外衣。

usage_note: 历史服饰词，有土耳其长袍、骑兵短上衣等不同义。本卡专学宽袖女外套；dolman sleeve 是相关的袖型名称。

senses.collocation_zh: 土耳其式长袍；长款土耳其袍
senses.sentence_en: The portrait shows a man wearing a long dolman and a turban.
senses.sentence_zh: 这幅肖像画中的男子身穿长袍，头戴缠头巾。

etymology_story.zh: dolman 经法语 dolman、doliman 等形式传入英语，最终源自土耳其语 dolama，原指一种长袍，与“缠绕、裹住”的动词有关。这个名称后来也用于欧洲骠骑兵的饰辫短上衣和女式宽松外衣。
etymology_story.en: Dolman entered English through French forms such as dolman and doliman, ultimately from Turkish dolama, a robe name related to a verb meaning 'to wrap or wind'. The name was later applied to European hussars' braided jackets and loose women's outer garments.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 dolman 是整体借词，不能拆成有意义的英语 dol + man；复数为 dolmans。主要相关复合词是 dolman sleeve（蝙蝠袖：袖窿宽、向袖口收窄）及 dolman-sleeved（带蝙蝠袖的）；没有常用的单词式派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dolman is an unanalyzed loanword, not a meaningful combination of English dol + man; its plural is dolmans. Its principal related compounds are dolman sleeve, a sleeve with a wide armhole tapering toward the wrist, and dolman-sleeved. It has no common family of single-word derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cloak（斗篷）通常没有成形的袖子；mantle（披风、外披）强调覆盖肩部的外衣；jacket（短上衣）是较宽泛的服装名称。dolman 的具体形制须由语境判断，可指宽松女外衣，也可指紧身饰辫军服。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cloak usually denotes a sleeveless outer covering; mantle emphasizes an outer garment draped over the shoulders; jacket is a broader term for a short upper-body garment. The precise form of a dolman depends on context: it may be a loose women's garment or a fitted, braided military jacket.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从土耳其语“裹住身体”联想外衣，再用语境区分长袍、女外套和军服短上衣。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Begin with the Turkish idea of wrapping the body, then use context to distinguish the robe, women's outer garment, and military jacket.

forms: 单数 hilum；复数 hila。复数主语搭配 are，不用 is。
family: hilum 种脐（单数）；hilar 种脐的，另有解剖学用法。

morphology.text: 拉丁式词形：hil-（hilum 的词干）+ -a（中性名词复数词尾）→ hila（多个种脐）。这是复数变化，不给整个词再加 -s。

etymology.text: 植物学通过新拉丁语借用拉丁语 hilum，原有“微小之物”的意思。小小的种脐是一处连接留下的痕迹，hila 则是它的复数。

usage_note: hila 是 hilum 的复数。本卡取植物学“种脐”义；在解剖学中还可指器官的门部，不要混为一个义项。

senses.english_definition: The hila of seeds are the marks left where the seeds were attached to the structures that supported them.

senses.meaning_zh: 器官的门；血管、神经等进出器官的部位
senses.meaning_en: The regions where vessels, nerves, or ducts enter or leave organs.
senses.english_definition: The hila of organs are the areas through which structures such as blood vessels and nerves pass into or out of them.
senses.collocation_zh: 肺门；肾门
senses.sentence_en: The radiologist examined both pulmonary hila.

etymology_story.zh: hila 是 hilum 的拉丁式复数；拉丁语 hīlum 原指微小之物，尤其见于表示“一点也没有”的表达。科学英语采用 hilum 表示种子的连接痕迹，并将其用于器官中结构进出的部位。
etymology_story.en: Hila is the Latin plural of hilum, from Latin hīlum, meaning a very small thing and especially occurring in expressions meaning 'not a bit.' Scientific English adopted hilum for a seed's attachment scar and also used it for the entry and exit region of an organ.

morphology_enriched.zh: hilum 的词干 hil- + 拉丁语中性复数词尾 -a → hila，属于屈折变化，不是添加派生后缀，也不再加 -s。主要相关形式：hilum（单数）、hila（复数）、hilar（种脐的；器官门的）、hilar region（门区）。
morphology_enriched.en: The stem hil- of hilum + the Latin neuter plural ending -a → hila; this is inflection, not derivation, and no additional -s is needed. Principal related forms are hilum, hila, hilar, and hilar region.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: seed scar（种子疤痕）可通俗解释植物学意义的种脐，但范围较宽；hilus（门）是解剖学中 hilum 的另一形式，其复数为 hili；organ gateway（器官的出入口）只是解释性说法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Seed scar is a plain-language explanation of the botanical sense, but it is broader; hilus is an alternative anatomical form of hilum, with the plural hili; organ gateway is an explanatory paraphrase rather than a technical synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 种子看“连接印”，器官看“进出口”；一个 hilum，多个 hila。
mnemonic_anchor.en: On a seed, think attachment mark; in an organ, think gateway. One hilum, several hila.

forms: 缩略形容词，不变形；完整形式 orthochromatic。
family: orthochromatic 正色性的；panchromatic 全色性的。

morphology.text: ortho-（正、正确）+ chromatic（颜色的）→ orthochromatic（正色性的）→ 缩略成 ortho。不要把独立缩略词当成化学前缀。

etymology.text: 来自国际科学词汇 orthochromatic 的缩略。前面的 ortho- 和希腊语“正、正确”有关，完整词原是描述颜色明暗再现的技术名称。

usage_note: 本卡是摄影形容词，是 orthochromatic 的缩略形式；不要与化学中表示邻位的 ortho- 混用。常作前置修饰语，如 ortho film。

senses.pos: n. 名词（非正式医学用语）
senses.meaning_zh: 骨科或正畸科；骨科医生或正畸医生，具体依语境而定
senses.meaning_en: An informal shortening for orthopedics, orthodontics, or a practitioner in either field.

etymology_story.zh: 摄影用语 ortho 缩略自 orthochromatic，其中 ortho- 源于希腊语 orthos“直的、正确的”，chromatic 与颜色有关。化学中的邻位用法来自同一构词成分的专业发展，而医学口语中的 ortho 则分别缩略自 orthopedics、orthodontics 等词。
etymology_story.en: Photographic ortho is shortened from orthochromatic, combining an element from Greek orthos, 'straight' or 'correct,' with a word relating to colour. Chemical ortho developed as a specialized use of the same combining form, while informal medical ortho separately shortens words such as orthopedics and orthodontics.

morphology_enriched.zh: 摄影义：orthochromatic → ortho，属于截短；化学义：ortho- 表示邻位，常见于 ortho-substituted（邻位取代的）；医学义：orthopedics／orthopaedics、orthodontics 等 → ortho，也属于截短。相关形式包括 orthochromatic、orthochromatically、orthochromatism、orthopedic／orthopaedic、orthopedist／orthopaedist、orthodontic、orthodontist；这些并非都由独立词 ortho 再派生而来。
morphology_enriched.en: In photography, orthochromatic → ortho is clipping; in chemistry, ortho- marks adjacent substitution, as in ortho-substituted; medical ortho also results from clipping words such as orthopedics and orthodontics. Related forms include orthochromatic, orthochromatically, orthochromatism, orthopedic/orthopaedic, orthopedist/orthopaedist, orthodontic, and orthodontist; these are not all derivatives of the independent word ortho.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: orthochromatic（正色性的）是摄影义的完整对应词；1,2-disubstituted（1,2-二取代的）可精确说明苯环上的邻位关系；orthopedics（骨科学）只对应部分医学语境，不能代替表示正畸的 ortho。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Orthochromatic is the full equivalent in photography; 1,2-disubstituted precisely describes the relevant adjacent arrangement on a benzene ring; orthopedics matches only some medical uses and cannot replace ortho when orthodontics is intended.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先看语境再补全：胶片 → orthochromatic；苯环 → 邻位；牙套 → orthodontics。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Expand it through context: film → orthochromatic; benzene ring → adjacent positions; braces → orthodontics.

etymology_story.zh: pottle 来自中古英语 potel，借自盎格鲁法语中与 pot“罐、壶”相关的指小形式。它曾指两夸脱的容量或相应容器，在新西兰英语中则保留并发展为食品小容器的名称，不再限定半加仑。
etymology_story.en: Pottle comes through Middle English potel from an Anglo-French diminutive related to pot. It denoted a two-quart measure or vessel, while New Zealand English retained and extended it to small food containers without a fixed half-gallon capacity.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 pottle 视为整体词干，不机械拆成 pot + -tle；复数为 pottles。相关组合：pottle pot（旧式两夸脱壶）、pottle-sized（小盒大小的）；pottleful 表示一容器的量，但较少见。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, pottle is best treated as a whole stem rather than mechanically split into pot + -tle; its plural is pottles. Related formations include pottle pot, pottle-sized, and the uncommon pottleful, meaning the amount one container holds.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tub（食品盒）强调宽口容器，是现代新西兰义的近义词；pot（罐、小杯）范围更广；half-gallon measure（半加仑量器）只对应历史容量义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tub is close to the modern New Zealand sense and suggests a wide-mouthed container; pot is broader; half-gallon measure matches only the historical capacity sense.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Use pot as the association: historically a half-gallon vessel, now also a small yoghurt container in New Zealand.

senses.meaning_en: To cut or finish an edge in a series of decorative points.
senses.english_definition: If you vandyke the edge of a piece of material, you shape or decorate it with a series of points.
senses.collocation_en: vandyke an edge; a vandyked hem

etymology_story.zh: Vandyke 源自佛兰德画家 Anthony van Dyck 的姓名，其肖像画中的尖形胡须、宽蕾丝领和尖齿饰边使这些式样与他的名字联系起来。英语随后也把这一名称用作动词，表示将边缘做成尖齿状。
etymology_story.en: Vandyke comes from the name of the Flemish painter Anthony van Dyck, whose portraits associated his name with pointed beards, broad lace collars, and pointed trimmings. English also developed a verb meaning to finish an edge with a series of points.

morphology_enriched.zh: Vandyke 是人名转成的普通词，不按现代英语词根词缀拆分；也写作 vandyke，胡须名称还常写作 Van Dyke。名词复数 Vandykes／vandykes；动词变化 vandykes、vandyked、vandyking；vandyked 也可作分词形容词，表示带尖齿边的。
morphology_enriched.en: Vandyke is an eponym and has no useful modern root-and-affix breakdown; vandyke is also used, and the beard style is often written Van Dyke. Noun plurals are Vandykes/vandykes; verb forms are vandykes, vandyked, and vandyking; vandyked also functions as a participial adjective meaning edged with points.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: goatee（山羊胡）主要指下巴上的胡须，不一定带髭；pointed beard（尖形胡须）只描述轮廓；在饰边义中，zigzag edging（锯齿形边饰）较宽泛，而 Vandyke 强调连续的装饰性尖齿。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Goatee mainly denotes chin hair and does not necessarily include a moustache; pointed beard describes shape alone; for trimming, zigzag edging is broader, while Vandyke specifically suggests a sequence of decorative points.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住范戴克肖像里的“尖”：下巴胡须尖，领口花边也尖。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the points in a Van Dyck portrait: a pointed chin beard and pointed lace edging.

senses.meaning_zh: 英国旧时的土地计量或佃地单位，通常约三十英亩，但各地不一
senses.meaning_en: An old English unit of landholding, often about thirty acres but varying locally.
senses.english_definition: A yardland was an amount of land used as a unit in medieval England, often reckoned at about thirty acres, although its size varied from place to place.
senses.collocation_en: hold a yardland; half a yardland
senses.collocation_zh: 持有一份 yardland 的土地；半份 yardland 的土地
senses.sentence_en: The manor's records show that the family held half a yardland.
senses.sentence_zh: 庄园档案显示，这户人家持有半份 yardland 的土地。

etymology_story.zh: yardland 由 yard 和 land 组成，其中 yard 使用与量杆、土地计量有关的旧义，而不是现代“庭院”的意思。这个词用于英国历史上的土地持有与计量制度，所指面积随地区和习惯而变化。
etymology_story.en: Yardland combines yard in an old sense connected with a measuring rod or land measure, rather than a courtyard, with land. It belonged to historical English systems of landholding and measurement, and its extent varied with local custom.

morphology_enriched.zh: yard（与量杆、土地计量有关的旧义）+ land（土地）→ yardland；复数为 yardlands。常见相关组合有 half-yardland（半份 yardland）和 yardland holder（持有一份 yardland 土地的佃户）；没有常用的独立派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Yard, in its older measuring sense, + land → yardland; the plural is yardlands. Related combinations include half-yardland and yardland holder; there is no established family of common derived words.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: virgate（维尔盖特）是最接近的历史对应术语；holding（所持土地、佃地）泛指一份土地，不限定其计量单位；hide（海德）是另一种通常更大的旧土地单位，在一些地方按四个 yardlands 计算，但不能视为固定换算。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Virgate is the closest historical equivalent; holding refers generally to land held by someone without specifying a unit; hide is another, usually larger historical unit, sometimes reckoned as four yardlands, although that relationship was not universal.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: yard 在这里关联“丈量”：量出的旧式田份，面积依地方习惯而定。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect yard with measuring: a customary measured holding of land whose size depended on the locality.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借用法语 célesta，该名称由 céleste“天上的；美妙的”改造而来，最终源于拉丁语 caelestis“天上的”。这个名称呼应了乐器清亮、空灵的音色。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French célesta, a name adapted from céleste, meaning 'heavenly', ultimately from Latin caelestis. The name evokes the instrument's clear, ethereal sound.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，celesta 是整体借入的词，不宜硬拆为英语词根和词缀。相关形式：celestas（复数）、celeste（异名）、celestist（钢片琴演奏者，较少见）；celestist 属于词干调整后的派生，不能简单解释为 celesta 直接加 -ist。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, celesta is a whole-word borrowing rather than a transparent combination of English roots and affixes. Related forms are celestas, the plural; celeste, an alternative name; and celestist, an uncommon term for a player, formed with an adjusted stem and -ist.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: celeste 是同一乐器的异名；keyboard glockenspiel 指键盘式钟琴，与钢片琴结构相近，但并非始终可以互换；glockenspiel 通常指直接用槌敲击金属音条的钟琴，音色一般更明亮。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Celeste is an alternative name for the same instrument. Keyboard glockenspiel names a related keyboard-operated instrument but is not always interchangeable with celesta. Glockenspiel usually refers to metal bars struck directly with mallets and generally has a brighter sound.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “天上的声音”：按下琴键，敲出空灵的铃音。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'heavenly sound': piano-like keys produce delicate bell-like notes.

etymology_story.zh: demy 经中古英语来自古法语 demi“半”，最终源于拉丁语 dimidius“一半的”。它后来固定用于纸张和书籍开本名称，但不应仅凭“半”的词源推断某一种现代规格的具体尺寸。
etymology_story.en: Demy came through Middle English from Old French demi, meaning 'half', ultimately from Latin dimidius. It became established in paper and book-format terminology, although its origin alone does not determine the dimensions of a modern sheet.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，demy 是不可再作实用拆分的借词，不是由独立词根 dem 和后缀 -y 构成。相关复合术语包括 double demy（双 demy 规格）和 demy octavo（demy 八开本）；纸张义没有常用的现代派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, demy is an unanalyzed borrowing, not a combination of a root dem and the suffix -y. Related compounds include double demy and demy octavo; the paper-size sense has no commonly used modern family of affixal derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: paper size 是“纸张规格”的上位词，并非同义规格名；royal 和 crown 是另外两种传统规格，不能替换 demy。表示具体尺寸时，应同时确认适用的规格体系。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Paper size is the broader category, not an equivalent size name. Royal and crown are other traditional sizes and cannot replace demy. The relevant sizing convention must be established when exact dimensions matter.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 由 demi“半”联想到纸张分切，再记住 demy 是固定规格名。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect demi, 'half', with divided sheets, then remember demy as an established paper-size name.

senses.sentence_zh: 这株茅膏菜用一片黏性叶片捕获了一只小苍蝇。

etymology_story.zh: 英语采用新拉丁语属名 Drosera，其来源是希腊语 droseros“带露水的”，与 drosos“露水”有关。名称指向叶片上像露珠一样闪亮、实际用于捕虫的黏液滴。
etymology_story.en: English adopted the New Latin genus name Drosera, derived from Greek droseros, meaning 'dewy', related to drosos, 'dew'. The name refers to the glistening, dew-like drops of sticky secretion that catch insects.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代普通英语中，drosera 通常作为整体植物名称使用；其历史构词基础与希腊语“露水”有关。相关形式：droseras（普通名词复数）、Drosera（正式属名）、Droseraceae（茅膏菜科，由词干 Droser- 加植物科名后缀 -aceae 构成），以及 droseraceous（茅膏菜科的，专业用语）。
morphology_enriched.en: In ordinary modern English, drosera functions as a whole plant name, historically based on Greek vocabulary for dew. Related forms include droseras, the common-noun plural; Drosera, the formal genus name; Droseraceae, formed from the stem Droser- and the botanical family suffix -aceae; and the technical adjective droseraceous.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sundew 是最直接、最常用的英语对应名称；carnivorous plant“食肉植物”和 insectivorous plant“食虫植物”都是范围更大的类别名称，不能单独确定为茅膏菜。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sundew is the direct and more familiar English equivalent. Carnivorous plant and insectivorous plant are broader category terms and do not identify a plant specifically as a drosera.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “露珠”其实是黏胶：看似带露，实际捕虫。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Its 'dewdrops' are insect traps: dewy in appearance, sticky in function.

senses.sentence_en: We planted helianthemums along the sunny edge of the rock garden.

etymology_story.zh: 英语采用新拉丁语属名 Helianthemum，该名称由表示“太阳”的希腊语 hēlios 和表示“花”的 anthemon 组合而成。它字面上是“太阳花”，呼应这类植物在阳光下开花的习性，并不表示向日葵属。
etymology_story.en: English adopted the New Latin genus name Helianthemum, combining Greek hēlios, 'sun', and anthemon, 'flower'. Its literal meaning, 'sun flower', reflects the plants' flowering in sunshine; it does not identify the sunflower genus.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是学术借词，其词源构造可分析为 heli-（太阳）+ anthem-（花）+ 新拉丁语词尾 -um；不能把整个 -anthemum 当作普通英语后缀。相关形式为 Helianthemum（正式属名）和 helianthemums（普通名词复数）；没有常用的现代英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: This learned borrowing can be analyzed historically as heli- ('sun') + anthem- ('flower') + the New Latin ending -um; the entire sequence -anthemum is not an ordinary English suffix. Related forms are Helianthemum, the formal genus name, and helianthemums, the common-noun plural; there is no commonly used modern English family of derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sunrose 是半日花的常见名称；rock rose 也可指半日花，但同样用于岩蔷薇属等相关植物；Cistus 指岩蔷薇属，是近缘属名，不能作为 Helianthemum 的严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sunrose is a common name for a helianthemum. Rock rose can also refer to it, but the name is shared with related plants. Cistus names a related genus and is not a strict synonym of Helianthemum.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: heli- 太阳 + anthem- 花：记住迎着阳光开放的半日花。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Heli- means sun and anthem- means flower: picture a sunrose opening in sunshine.

senses.meaning_zh: 应得的奖赏、报偿或赞誉，现主要用于文学语体
senses.meaning_en: a deserved reward, recompense, or share of praise, chiefly in literary use
senses.english_definition: Someone's meed is the reward or praise that they deserve or receive for something they have done.
senses.collocation_en: a meed of praise; a just meed
senses.collocation_zh: 应得的一份赞誉；公正的报偿
senses.sentence_en: The poet finally received her meed of praise.
senses.sentence_zh: 这位诗人终于获得了她应得的赞誉。

etymology_story.zh: meed 经中古英语承自古英语 mēd“奖赏；报酬”，属于英语继承的日耳曼语词汇。它过去可泛指报偿，现代则主要保留在文学性的奖赏或赞誉表达中。
etymology_story.en: Meed passed through Middle English from Old English mēd, meaning 'reward' or 'payment', and belongs to English's inherited Germanic vocabulary. Once a more general word for recompense, it now survives chiefly in literary expressions about reward or praise.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，meed 是单纯词，不宜再拆分；meeds 是可用的复数形式。历史派生包括 meedful（值得奖赏的；有功的）和 meedless（未获报偿的），均属古旧词，不能当作活跃的现代词族成员；动词用法也已过时。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, meed is a simple base word with no useful internal division; meeds is its possible plural. Historical derivatives include meedful, meaning deserving reward or meritorious, and meedless, meaning unrewarded. Both are archaic rather than active modern derivatives, and the verb use is obsolete.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: reward 是最普通的“奖赏”，可指物质或精神回报；recompense 强调对劳动、付出或损失的补偿；due 作名词时强调某人按理应得的一份。meed 带明显文学色彩，常与赞誉连用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Reward is the ordinary term for a material or nonmaterial benefit. Recompense emphasizes repayment for effort, service, or loss. Due, as a noun, emphasizes what someone rightfully deserves. Meed is distinctly literary and often accompanies praise.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 功绩换来应得的一份：meed = 文学语体中的“应得报偿”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Merit earns its share: meed is the literary word for a deserved reward.

senses.meaning_zh: 凌乱的；蓬乱的，尤指头发或衣服
senses.meaning_en: Untidy or rumpled, especially of hair or clothing; informal, chiefly American.
senses.english_definition: If someone's hair or clothes are mussy, they look untidy because they have been disturbed or crumpled.
senses.collocation_zh: 蓬乱的头发；凌乱的仪容
senses.sentence_en: She came downstairs with mussy hair and a sleepy smile.
senses.sentence_zh: 她头发蓬乱地走下楼，脸上带着睡意蒙眬的微笑。

etymology_story.zh: mussy 在十九世纪的美国英语中已有使用，由表示“弄乱、使起皱”的 muss 加形容词后缀 -y 构成。它常描写头发、衣服等被揉乱后的样子；muss 更早的来源并不完全确定。
etymology_story.en: Recorded in nineteenth-century American English, mussy was formed from muss, meaning to disorder or rumple, plus the adjective suffix -y. It commonly describes disturbed hair or clothing; the earlier origin of muss is not entirely certain.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：muss（弄乱；凌乱状态）+ -y（具有某种状态的）→ mussy。相关词形和派生词：muss、musses、mussed、mussing；比较级 mussier，最高级 mussiest；副词 mussily（凌乱地），名词 mussiness（凌乱）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: muss, meaning to rumple or a state of disorder, + -y, meaning characterized by, → mussy. Related forms and derivatives include muss, musses, mussed, mussing; comparative mussier and superlative mussiest; adverb mussily and noun mussiness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: messy（杂乱的）适用范围更广，也可指脏乱或局面复杂；rumpled（起皱而凌乱的）强调衣料、头发等被揉乱；disheveled（蓬头散发的）更强调人的头发和衣着失于整理。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Messy is broader and can describe dirt or complicated situations; rumpled emphasizes disturbance or creasing of hair or fabric; disheveled particularly describes a person's untidy hair and clothing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: muss 是“弄乱”，加 -y 就是“乱了的”：睡醒后的蓬乱头发。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Muss means to rumple; mussy means looking rumpled—picture hair after sleep.

senses.meaning_zh: 彼特拉克的；彼特拉克诗风的；采用彼特拉克式十四行诗形式的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to Petrarch, his poetic style, or the sonnet form associated with him.
senses.english_definition: A Petrarchan poem uses a form or style associated with the Italian poet Petrarch, often expressing love for an idealized and unattainable person.
senses.collocation_zh: 彼特拉克式十四行诗；彼特拉克诗派的惯用手法
senses.sentence_en: The poem follows the Petrarchan sonnet form, with an octave followed by a sestet.
senses.sentence_zh: 这首诗采用彼特拉克式十四行诗的形式，由一个八行诗节和随后的一个六行诗节组成。

senses.meaning_zh: 彼特拉克诗风的模仿者或追随者，限文学论述用语
senses.meaning_en: A follower or imitator of Petrarch's poetic style; a specialized literary use.
senses.english_definition: A Petrarchan is a poet who follows or imitates the style and conventions of Petrarch.
senses.collocation_en: the English Petrarchans; a Renaissance Petrarchan
senses.collocation_zh: 英国彼特拉克派诗人；一位文艺复兴时期的彼特拉克派诗人
senses.sentence_en: Like other Petrarchans, the poet portrays his beloved as both beautiful and unattainable.

etymology_story.zh: Petrarchan 由意大利诗人 Francesco Petrarca 的英语名字 Petrarch 加 -an 构成。随着其爱情诗及十四行诗传统在欧洲传播，这个词既用于表示与他有关，也用于描述模仿其诗歌形式、意象和爱情观的作品或诗人。
etymology_story.en: Petrarchan was formed by adding -an to Petrarch, the English name of the Italian poet Francesco Petrarca. As his love poetry and sonnet tradition spread across Europe, the word came to describe works and poets adopting his forms, imagery, and treatment of love.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：Petrarch（彼特拉克）+ -an（与……有关的；……的追随者）→ Petrarchan，可作形容词和名词；名词复数为 Petrarchans。相关词族包括 Petrarchism（彼特拉克主义或诗风）、Petrarchist（彼特拉克诗风的模仿者）和 Petrarchian（彼特拉克的或其风格的，较少见变体）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: Petrarch + -an, meaning relating to or a follower of, → Petrarchan, used as both adjective and noun; the noun plural is Petrarchans. Related family members include Petrarchism, the imitation of his poetic conventions; Petrarchist, an imitator; and Petrarchian, a less common alternative adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Petrarchian（彼特拉克的或其风格的）是较少见的近义形式；Italian（意大利式的）在十四行诗分类中常与 Petrarchan 对应，但范围更广；Petrarchist（彼特拉克派诗人）与名词 Petrarchan 近义，明确指模仿其诗风的人。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Petrarchian is a less common near-equivalent adjective; Italian often overlaps with Petrarchan when classifying sonnets but is otherwise much broader; Petrarchist closely matches the noun Petrarchan and explicitly identifies an imitator of his poetic style.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Petrarch + -an：从诗人的名字，直接记住他的诗风和追随者。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Petrarch + -an: the poet's name becomes the label for his style and its followers.

senses.meaning_zh: 花边、钩编或刺绣边缘的小装饰环或小尖齿
senses.meaning_en: A small decorative loop or point along the edge of lace, crochet, or embroidery.

senses.meaning_zh: 给织物边缘制作小环或小尖齿装饰，限针线工艺术语
senses.meaning_en: To finish or decorate an edge with small loops or points; a specialized needlework use.
senses.english_definition: If you picot an edge, you finish or decorate it with a series of small loops or points.
senses.collocation_en: picot an edge; a picoted hem
senses.collocation_zh: 给边缘制作小环饰边；带小环饰边的底边

senses.sentence_zh: 她用细棉线给手帕边缘做了一圈小环装饰。

etymology_story.zh: 英语 picot 借自法语同形词，原义为“小尖点”，由 pic 加小称后缀 -ot 构成。它在针线工艺中专指边缘微小的环状或尖齿状装饰，英语又将这个名词转用为表示制作这种饰边的动词。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed picot from French, where it meant a small point and was formed from pic with the diminutive suffix -ot. In needlework it names tiny projecting loops or points, and English also converted the noun into a verb for making such edging.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 picot 通常作为完整借词使用，不按英语词根和后缀继续拆分；历史法语结构为 pic（尖点）+ -ot（小称后缀）。名词复数为 picots；动词通过零派生形成，常见词形为 picots、picoted、picoting；picoted 也可作分词形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, picot is normally treated as a whole borrowed base rather than an English root-plus-suffix construction; its historical French structure is pic, point, + the diminutive -ot. The noun plural is picots; the verb is formed by conversion, with forms picots, picoted, and picoting; picoted can also function as a participial adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: loop（环）只说明环状结构，不必具有装饰作用；edging（饰边）指整条边缘装饰，picot 通常是其中一个小环或尖齿；scallop（扇贝形饰边）通常指较大、圆弧状的连续边饰。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Loop names a shape without necessarily implying decoration; edging denotes an entire decorative border, whereas a picot is usually one small projecting element; scallop usually denotes a larger rounded unit in a decorative edge.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“小尖点”想到花边上一个个微微凸出的小环。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with a little point: picture the tiny loops projecting from a lace edge.

senses.meaning_zh: 古罗马祭司团成员，负责宗教仪式及宗教事务
senses.meaning_en: A member of the ancient Roman college of priests responsible for religious observances and related matters.
senses.english_definition: A pontifex was a priest in ancient Rome who belonged to a college that supervised religious ceremonies and religious law.
senses.collocation_zh: 一位古罗马祭司；古罗马最高祭司
senses.sentence_en: As a pontifex, he helped supervise Rome's religious observances.
senses.sentence_zh: 作为祭司团成员，他协助监督罗马的宗教仪式。

etymology_story.zh: 英语直接借用了拉丁语祭司称号 pontifex，传统上将其分析为 pons“桥”的词干 pont- 与表示“制作者”的 -fex，因此常释为“造桥者”。这种词源分析与古代祭司实际职责之间的历史联系仍有争议，不能把“沟通人与神的桥梁”当作已证实的起源。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the Latin priestly title pontifex, traditionally analyzed as pont-, the stem of pons, bridge, plus -fex, maker, hence bridge-builder. The historical connection between this analysis and priestly duties remains disputed, so a bridge between humans and gods should be treated as a mnemonic rather than an established origin.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 pontifex 是完整的拉丁语借词，不是由可自由使用的英语词素构成；历史分析为 pont-（桥）+ -fex（制作者，与 facere“做”有关）。传统复数为 pontifices；历史相关词包括 pontiff（教皇；高级祭司）、pontifical（教皇的；自以为是的）和 pontificate（教皇任期；武断地发表意见），并非都由英语 pontifex 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, pontifex is a whole Latin borrowing rather than a productive combination of English morphemes; its traditional historical analysis is pont-, bridge, + -fex, maker, related to facere, to make. The traditional plural is pontifices; historically related words include pontiff, pontifical, and pontificate, though these are not all direct English derivatives of pontifex.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: priest（祭司；神父）是范围更广的通称；pontiff（教皇；高级祭司）在现代英语中通常指教皇；flamen（古罗马专祀祭司）指侍奉特定神祇的祭司，与 pontifex 所指的职务不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Priest is the broader general term; pontiff usually means the pope in modern English; flamen identifies a Roman priest assigned to a particular deity and denotes a different office from pontifex.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用传统拆分“桥 + 制作者”记词形，再把实际词义锁定为“古罗马祭司”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the traditional bridge + maker analysis to remember the form, then anchor the meaning in the Roman priestly office.

etymology_story.zh: stirk 经中古英语传承自古英语 stirc，是英语本土日耳曼语词汇中的幼牛名称。它后来主要保留在苏格兰和英格兰北部的地方用语及畜牧语境中。
etymology_story.en: Stirk passed through Middle English from Old English stirc, an inherited Germanic name for a young bovine. It subsequently survived chiefly in Scottish and northern English regional speech and livestock contexts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：stirk 是不可再作常规拆分的单纯词；复数为 stirks。苏格兰语小称形式 stirkie 可分析为 stirk + -ie，意为“小牛”；steer（阉公牛）是历史相关词，不是 stirk 的现代派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: stirk is a simplex word with no usual internal morphological division; its plural is stirks. The Scots diminutive stirkie can be analyzed as stirk + -ie, meaning a little or young bovine; steer is historically related rather than a modern derivative of stirk.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: calf（犊牛）通常指年龄更小、尤其未满一岁的牛；yearling（一岁左右的幼畜）强调年龄，可指牛以外的动物；heifer（未产犊母牛）限定性别和繁殖状态，而 stirk 可用于不同性别的幼牛。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Calf usually refers to a younger bovine, especially one under a year old; yearling specifies approximate age and can describe other animals; heifer specifies a female that has not calved, whereas stirk can refer to young cattle of either sex.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 stirk 与同源的 steer 联系起来：都是牛类词，但 stirk 重点是“年幼”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link stirk with its historical relative steer: both concern cattle, but stirk emphasizes youth.

etymology_story.zh: 由 toss（举起、倾倒）与 pot（饮酒用的杯或壶）复合而成，十六世纪已有记录，原指不断举杯喝酒的人。现代英国英语还用它辱骂愚蠢或可鄙的人。[词源与义项：柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/tosspot)
etymology_story.en: Recorded in the sixteenth century, tosspot combines toss with pot, a drinking vessel, evoking someone repeatedly tipping up a cup. It also functions in modern British English as an insult for a foolish or contemptible person. [Etymology and senses: Collins Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/tosspot)

morphology_enriched.zh: toss（举起、倾倒）+ pot（酒杯、酒壶）→ tosspot，属于动词加名词构成的指人复合名词。复数为 tosspots；没有常用的直接派生动词、形容词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: toss + pot → tosspot, a verb–noun compound naming a person. The plural is tosspots; there are no commonly used directly derived verbs, adjectives, or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: drunkard（酒鬼）直接强调惯常酗酒；sot（酒徒）更具旧式、文学色彩；idiot（蠢货）对应辱骂义，不涉及饮酒。tosspot 的具体意思取决于语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Drunkard explicitly describes habitual excessive drinking; sot is more literary and old-fashioned; idiot matches the insulting sense without implying alcohol use. Context determines which meaning tosspot carries.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 反复把 pot（酒杯）toss（举起倾倒）→ 酒鬼；作为骂人话，也可指蠢货。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Repeatedly toss up a drinking pot → a drunkard; as a general insult, a fool.

etymology_story.zh: 最终源自拉丁语 venter，意为“腹部、子宫、膨大处”；早期英语法律用法经盎格鲁法语传入，科学用法则与新拉丁语借词有关。“腹部”的形象进一步用于动物腹面、肌腹和植物颈卵器的膨大基部。[词源：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/venter)
etymology_story.en: Venter ultimately comes from Latin venter, meaning belly, womb, or bulge; early English legal usage passed through Anglo-French, while scientific usage involved New Latin. The belly image extends to an animal's underside, a muscle's fleshy enlargement, and the swollen base of an archegonium. [Etymology: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/venter)

morphology_enriched.zh: venter 是借入的完整名词，不应拆成英语 vent + -er。拉丁词干 ventr-（腹部）构成相关词族：ventral（腹侧的）、ventrally（在腹侧）、ventricle（心室；脑室，历史上源于“小腹腔”）、ventricular（心室的；脑室的）；普通英语复数为 venters。
morphology_enriched.en: Venter is a borrowed noun, not English vent + -er. Its Latin stem ventr- underlies the related family ventral, ventrally, ventricle, historically a small cavity, and ventricular; the regular English plural is venters.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: abdomen（腹部）是更常用、范围较明确的解剖名称；belly（肚腹）偏日常表达，也见于 muscle belly（肌腹）；underside（下侧、底面）只说明位置，不限定为腹部。venter 的准确所指随学科而变。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Abdomen is the more usual anatomical term for the abdominal region; belly is less formal, though muscle belly is standard terminology; underside indicates position without specifically identifying an abdomen. The precise meaning of venter depends on the discipline.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ventr- 抓住“腹”：身体的腹、肌肉的腹、颈卵器鼓起的腹。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor ventr- to belly: the body's belly, a muscle's belly, or an archegonium's swollen belly.

etymology_story.zh: 由 yard（营院、院落）与 bird（鸟，也可用于指人）复合而成，二十世纪四十年代已有美国俚语记录，其构词受到 jailbird（囚犯）的类比影响。它既用于指新兵或在营区做杂役的士兵，也用于指囚犯。[词源与义项：柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/yardbird)
etymology_story.en: Recorded in American slang in the 1940s, yardbird combines yard with bird and was formed by analogy with jailbird. Its established uses include military recruits, soldiers doing menial camp duties, and prisoners. [Etymology and senses: Collins Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/yardbird)

morphology_enriched.zh: yard（院落、营院）+ bird（鸟；俚语中指人）→ yardbird，属于名词加名词的复合词。复数为 yardbirds；没有常用的直接派生词；jailbird（囚犯）是构词相近的相关词，不是 yardbird 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: yard + bird → yardbird, a noun–noun compound. The plural is yardbirds; there are no common direct derivatives. Jailbird is a related compound with a similar formation, not a derivative of yardbird.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: recruit（新兵）中性地说明刚入伍；rookie（新手）强调经验不足，也用于军队之外；jailbird（囚犯、坐过牢的人）对应监狱义，带俚语和贬义色彩。yardbird 的军中义往往另带笨拙、杂役或受罚的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Recruit neutrally identifies someone newly enlisted; rookie emphasizes inexperience and also applies outside the military; jailbird matches the prison sense and is informal and disparaging. Military yardbird often additionally suggests ineptitude, menial work, or punishment.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 被叫作 yard（营院或监狱院子）里的 bird（鸟）→ 营里的新兵、杂役兵，或狱里的囚犯。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a bird in a camp or prison yard: an inexperienced soldier, a camp drudge, or a prisoner.

etymology.text: 英语化学命名由 alkyl 的词形与 -yne 组合而成，-yne 是 -ine 的变体。用名称里的 yne 提醒自己注意碳碳三键。

senses.meaning_zh: 炔烃；含碳碳三键的烃
senses.meaning_en: A hydrocarbon containing a carbon–carbon triple bond.
senses.english_definition: An alkyne is a hydrocarbon whose molecules contain a triple bond between two carbon atoms.
senses.collocation_zh: 端炔；内炔
senses.sentence_en: A terminal alkyne has a hydrogen atom attached to one of the carbon atoms in its triple bond.
senses.sentence_zh: 端炔的三键碳原子中，有一个连接着氢原子。

etymology_story.zh: 这是十九世纪末出现的化学命名词，由 alkyl（烷基）的词形与 -yne 组合而成；-yne 是 -ine 的变体。现代命名用 -yne 标示碳碳三键，与表示单键和双键系列的 -ane、-ene 相区别。[词源：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/alkyne)
etymology_story.en: Alkyne arose in late-nineteenth-century chemical terminology from the form of alkyl combined with -yne, an alteration of -ine. Modern nomenclature uses -yne for a carbon–carbon triple bond, contrasting with the -ane and -ene series. [Etymology: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/alkyne)

morphology_enriched.zh: alk-（从 alkyl 的词形缩取的命名成分）+ -yne（炔类词尾）→ alkyne。词族包括 alkynes（复数）、alkynyl（炔基；炔基的）、alkynic（炔类的）；相关命名词有 ethyne（乙炔）、propyne（丙炔）、butyne（丁炔）、diyne（二炔）、polyyne（多炔）。alkane（烷烃）与 alkene（烯烃）是并列类别，不是 alkyne 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: alk-, a naming element shortened from the form of alkyl, + -yne → alkyne. The family includes alkynes, alkynyl, and alkynic; related nomenclature includes ethyne, propyne, butyne, diyne, and polyyne. Alkane and alkene name parallel classes rather than derivatives of alkyne.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: acetylenic hydrocarbon（乙炔系烃）是传统的近义名称；acetylene（乙炔）只是一种具体炔烃，不能替代整个类别；unsaturated hydrocarbon（不饱和烃）范围更大，还包括烯烃等类别。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Acetylenic hydrocarbon is a traditional near-equivalent; acetylene names one particular alkyne rather than the entire class; unsaturated hydrocarbon is broader and also includes classes such as alkenes.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 看到 -yne，就锁定 C≡C：三键对应炔。
mnemonic_anchor.en: See -yne, think C≡C: a triple bond signals an alkyne.

etymology.text: 英语经拉丁语采用希腊语 askaris 这一肠道蠕虫名称。由虫名又形成表示感染疾病的 ascariasis。

senses.english_definition: Ascaris is the scientific name of a genus of roundworms that includes the human intestinal parasite Ascaris lumbricoides.

etymology_story.zh: 最终源自希腊语 askaris，意为“肠道蠕虫”；英语早期形式经中世纪拉丁语传入，现代属名则沿用新拉丁语 Ascaris。相关疾病名 ascariasis 在表示蛔虫的词干后加表示病症的 -iasis，指蛔虫感染所致的疾病。[词源：柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/ascaris)
etymology_story.en: The word ultimately comes from Greek askaris, an intestinal worm; early English forms passed through Medieval Latin, while the modern genus name uses New Latin Ascaris. The disease name ascariasis combines the worm-name stem with -iasis, a suffix denoting a pathological condition. [Etymology: Collins Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/ascaris)

morphology_enriched.zh: ascaris 是完整借词，不宜强拆为现代英语前后缀；传统复数为 ascarides。相关词族包括 ascarid（蛔虫；蛔虫类的）、ascariasis（蛔虫病）、ascaridiasis（蛔虫病）、ascaricidal（杀蛔虫的）、ascaricide（杀蛔虫剂）；Ascarididae 为蛔虫科。ascaris infection 中 ascaris 作前置修饰语，不必另立可独立使用的形容词义。
morphology_enriched.en: Ascaris is a whole-word borrowing without a productive modern English prefix–suffix analysis; its traditional plural is ascarides. Related forms include ascarid, ascariasis, ascaridiasis, ascaricidal, and ascaricide; Ascarididae names the family. In ascaris infection, ascaris functions attributively rather than requiring a separate independently usable adjective sense.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ascarid（蛔虫或蛔虫类线虫）是最接近的名称，但分类范围可较宽；roundworm（线虫、圆虫）包括大量其他线虫；intestinal worm（肠道蠕虫）按寄生部位命名，还可包括绦虫等非线虫寄生虫。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ascarid is the closest alternative, though its taxonomic scope can be broader; roundworm includes many other nematodes; intestinal worm describes location and can also include non-nematode parasites such as tapeworms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把虫名和病名成对记：Ascaris 是蛔虫，ascariasis 是蛔虫病。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pair the organism with its disease: Ascaris is the worm; ascariasis is the infection.

etymology_story.zh: 芭蕾术语 barre 借自法语 barre“横杆”，可上溯至中世纪拉丁语 barra。音乐中的 barre 与法语 barré“被横杆拦住的、横按的”有关，把横跨琴弦的手指比作一根横杆。
etymology_story.en: The ballet term barre comes from French barre, meaning “bar,” ultimately from Medieval Latin barra. The musical term is associated with French barré, meaning “barred,” comparing a finger across the strings to a bar.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代结构：barre + -s → barres；名词中 -s 表示复数，动词中表示一般现在时第三人称单数，均读 /z/。相关形式：名词 barre、barres；音乐动词 barre、barres、barred、barring；常见组合有 barre chord“横按和弦”、barre work“把杆训练”。健身义 barre 通常不可数，不能直接把 barres 解释为该义的普通复数。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: barre + -s → barres; -s marks either a plural noun or a third-person singular present-tense verb and is pronounced /z/. Related forms include the nouns barre and barres and the musical verb forms barre, barres, barred, and barring; common combinations include barre chord and barre work. Barre meaning an exercise activity is normally uncountable, so barres is not its ordinary plural.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bar“横杆”范围最广；handrail“扶手”强调供人扶握的支撑设施；音乐义中的 barré“横按”是相关术语的另一种拼写。Barres 在芭蕾语境专指练习把杆，在吉他语境则指横按指位。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bar is the broadest term for a rigid horizontal piece; handrail emphasizes something held for support; barré is an alternative spelling associated with the musical technique. Barres specifically denotes practice rails in ballet and barred finger positions in guitar playing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“横杆”：舞者扶横杆，吉他手用手指搭出横杆；-s 表示多根、多次指位或“他／她横按”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a bar: dancers hold one, and guitarists make one with a finger; -s marks plural bars or positions, or “he/she barres.”

etymology_story.zh: Burgage 在中古英语时期出现，其借词来源涉及盎格鲁法语 borgage、burgage 和中世纪拉丁语 burgagium，词基表示“城镇、设防聚落”。它由城镇概念发展为一种特定的城镇房产或土地保有制度名称。
etymology_story.en: Burgage entered Middle English through forms associated with Anglo-French borgage or burgage and Medieval Latin burgagium, built on a word for a town or fortified settlement. It came to name a particular way of holding urban land or property.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 burgage 作为整体借词处理；burg“城镇”+ -age“制度、状态”可用于理解其历史结构，但不是一次现代英语自由构词。它主要是不可数名词；burgages 可用于可数的保有地产或个别保有单位；常见组合有 burgage tenure、burgage plot“市地保有制地块”、burgage holder“市地保有人”，无常用动词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, burgage is normally treated as a whole borrowed word; burg “town” + -age “system or condition” helps explain its historical structure rather than a freely productive modern formation. It is chiefly uncountable; burgages can denote individual holdings. Established combinations include burgage tenure, burgage plot, and burgage holder; there are no common derived verbs or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tenure“土地保有方式”是上位概念；socage“索克保有制”在英格兰历史中通常涉及租金或规定服务，范围比 burgage 更广；tenancy“租佃关系”强调占有或租用关系，不能完整替代这一历史制度名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tenure is the general term for the conditions under which land is held; socage covers a broader historical category involving rent or specified services in England; tenancy emphasizes an occupation or rental relationship and does not fully replace this historical institutional term.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: burg 是“城镇”：把 burgage 记作“城镇里的旧土地保有制度”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Burg means “town”: remember burgage as an old system for holding town property.

etymology_story.zh: Costmary 源于中古英语 costmarie，由旧植物名 cost 与指圣母玛利亚的 Marie 组成。Cost 经古英语和拉丁语可追溯至希腊语 kostos“一种芳香植物或芳香根”，与表示“费用”的 cost 来源不同。
etymology_story.en: Costmary comes from Middle English costmarie, combining the old plant name cost with Marie, referring to the Virgin Mary. Cost goes through Old English and Latin to Greek kostos, an aromatic plant or root, and is unrelated in origin to cost meaning “expense.”

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史复合结构：cost“芳香植物”+ Mary“玛利亚”→ costmary；现代英语中通常作为整体植物名学习。可数复数为 costmaries，指植株或种类；指植物材料时可不可数使用；无常用形容词、动词或副词派生形式。Alecost、bible leaf 和 balsam herb 是别名，不是其派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Historical compound: cost “aromatic plant” + Mary → costmary; modern learners normally treat it as a whole plant name. The countable plural is costmaries, referring to plants or kinds; the name can be uncountable when referring to plant material. There are no common derived adjectives, verbs, or adverbs. Alecost, bible leaf, and balsam herb are alternative names rather than derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: alecost“酿酒香草”突出其传统的麦酒调味用途；bible leaf“圣经叶草”源于把芳香叶片夹入《圣经》的习俗；balsam herb“香脂草”强调香气。这些通常是同一植物的俗名，差别主要在命名侧重点。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Alecost highlights its traditional use in flavouring ale; bible leaf recalls the custom of placing its fragrant leaves inside Bibles; balsam herb emphasizes its scent. These generally name the same plant, with differences in naming emphasis rather than botanical meaning.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 旧词 cost 是“香草”，Mary 是“玛利亚”：记成“玛利亚的芳香草”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Old cost means “aromatic herb” and Mary names Mary: picture “Mary’s fragrant herb.”

etymology_story.zh: Dibber 由英语动词 dib“戳、在土中打孔”加工具后缀 -er 构成，十七世纪已有记录。它后来也用于定向越野的电子打卡器，其插入或点触检查点设备的动作与原来的戳孔动作相似。
etymology_story.en: Dibber was formed from the English verb dib, meaning to poke or make planting holes, with the instrument suffix -er, and is recorded from the seventeenth century. It later acquired an orienteering use for an electronic checking device, whose insertion or touching action resembles the original poking action.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：dib + -er → dibber，添加后缀时双写末尾 b；复数为 dibbers。相关动词形式有 dib、dibs、dibbed、dibbing；相关园艺词 dibble 可作名词“打孔棒”或动词“打孔栽种”，其形式有 dibbles、dibbled、dibbling。Dibble 是相关词，不是把 dibber 继续加后缀所得。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: dib + -er → dibber, doubling the final b; the plural is dibbers. Related verb forms include dib, dibs, dibbed, and dibbing. The related gardening word dibble is both a noun for the tool and a verb meaning to make planting holes or plant with one, with forms dibbles, dibbled, and dibbling. Dibble is related vocabulary, not a further suffixal derivative of dibber.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 园艺义的 dibble“打孔棒”基本同义；planting stick“种植棒”是较宽泛的描述性名称；定向越野义的 electronic punch“电子打卡器”强调记录检查点的功能，不能用于指园艺工具。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For gardening, dibble is essentially synonymous, while planting stick is a broader descriptive name. In orienteering, electronic punch emphasizes the control-recording function and does not denote the gardening tool.

etymology_story.zh: Gurnard 在中古英语时期借自古法语 gornard，原意与“发出咕噜声的东西”有关，可追溯至拉丁语 grunnire“发出呼噜声”。鱼名反映了这类鱼能够发出低沉声音的特点。
etymology_story.en: Gurnard entered Middle English from Old French gornard, associated with the meaning “grunter,” ultimately from Latin grunnire, “to grunt.” The name reflects the low sounds these fish can produce.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 gurnard 是不可再作实用拆分的整体鱼名，不宜把 -ard 当作现代可分析的后缀。复数可为 gurnard 或 gurnards，后者尤其可用于不同种类；相关名称有 gurnet“鲂鮄”的变体，以及 red gurnard“红鲂鮄”、grey gurnard“灰鲂鮄”、tub gurnard“角鲂鮄”等组合。无常用动词、副词或固定形容词派生词；gurnardlike 只是可临时构成的“像鲂鮄的”。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, gurnard is a whole fish name without a useful productive breakdown; -ard should not be treated as a modern analysable suffix here. Its plurals are gurnard and gurnards, with the latter especially suitable for different kinds. Related names include the variant gurnet and combinations such as red gurnard, grey gurnard, and tub gurnard. There are no common derived verbs, adverbs, or established adjectives; gurnardlike is merely a possible transparent formation meaning “like a gurnard.”

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gurnet“鲂鮄”是 gurnard 的变体；sea robin“海知更鸟鱼、鲂鮄”是北美常用的鲂鮄科鱼名；flying gurnard“飞鲂鮄”通常指另一科鱼类，虽在部分用法中也简称 gurnard，却不能在分类语境中与普通鲂鮄完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gurnet is a variant of gurnard; sea robin is a common North American name for fishes of the family Triglidae. Flying gurnard normally refers to a different family and, although sometimes shortened to gurnard, is not fully interchangeable with the ordinary term in taxonomic contexts.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to “grunt”: a sea fish that makes a low grunting sound explains the name.

etymology_story.zh: 源自古英语 mealm，指松散的土或沙，与其他日耳曼语言中表示沙土的词同源。词义后来用于白垩质岩土，并进一步延伸到制砖混合料及其烧制的砖。
etymology_story.en: Malm comes from Old English mealm, referring to loose earth or sand, and has relatives in other Germanic languages denoting sandy material. Its meaning developed to cover chalky earth and rock, then a prepared brickmaking mixture and the bricks made from it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 malm 是不可再作常用词根与词缀切分的单纯词。表示材料时通常不可数，表示砖时可数，复数为 malms；罕见派生词 malmy（白垩质的）由 malm + -y 构成，相关复合词有 malmstone（白垩质石灰岩）和 malm brick（白垩黏土砖）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, malm is a simple base without a productive internal root-and-affix division. It is usually uncountable as a material and countable as a brick, with the plural malms; the rare adjective malmy means chalky and consists of malm + -y, while related compounds include malmstone and malm brick.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chalk（白垩）强调松软的白色石灰岩；marl（泥灰岩、泥灰土）强调碳酸钙与黏土的混合；limestone（石灰岩）是更广的岩石类别。三者与 malm 的部分含义重叠，但都不能完整替代其制砖材料及砖的含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chalk emphasizes soft, white limestone; marl emphasizes a mixture of calcium carbonate and clay; limestone names the broader rock category. These words overlap with particular senses of malm but do not cover its full range of brickmaking meanings.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“松软的白垩质材料”：地下是岩土，调配后是砖料，烧成后是砖。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture soft, chalky material: in the ground it is earth or rock, when mixed it is brickmaking material, and when fired it becomes a brick.

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语 malmesey 经古法语等形式传入，名称最终可追溯到希腊港口 Monemvasia 的中世纪名称 Malvasia，该港曾参与甜葡萄酒贸易。这个酒名后来也用于其他产地的甜酒，尤其是甜型马德拉酒。
etymology_story.en: Middle English malmesey came through forms including Old French and ultimately derives from Malvasia, the medieval name of the Greek port Monemvasia, associated with the sweet-wine trade. The name later extended to sweet wines from other places, especially sweet Madeira.

morphology_enriched.zh: malmsey 在现代英语中作为完整借词处理，不能分析为 malm + -sey。通常作不可数名词，谈论不同品种或酒款时可用复数 malmseys；没有常用的派生动词或形容词。Malvasia（玛尔维萨葡萄及相关葡萄酒）是历史同源名称，并非由 malmsey 加词缀派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Malmsey is treated as a complete loanword in modern English and is not malm + -sey. It is normally uncountable, though malmseys can refer to different varieties or wines; it has no common derived verb or adjective. Malvasia, naming grapes and associated wines, is historically related rather than an affixal derivative of malmsey.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sweet Madeira（甜型马德拉酒）最接近其现代常见所指；dessert wine（甜点酒）范围更广；Malvasia（玛尔维萨）主要指一组葡萄品种及相关葡萄酒，不能在所有语境中与 malmsey 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sweet Madeira is closest to its usual modern reference; dessert wine is a broader category; Malvasia primarily names a group of grape varieties and associated wines and is not interchangeable with malmsey in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember a port name becoming a wine name: sweet wine shipped through a Greek port gave malmsey its name.

etymology_story.zh: 单数 plew 来自加拿大法语 pelu，与法语中表示“多毛的”的词有关，最终可追溯到拉丁语 pilus“毛发”。这个皮毛贸易用语以皮张上的毛为命名基础，尤其用于河狸皮。
etymology_story.en: The singular plew comes from Canadian French pelu, connected with French words meaning hairy and ultimately with Latin pilus, meaning hair. This fur-trade term names a skin through its covering of hair and was used especially for beaver skins.

morphology_enriched.zh: plew + -s → plews，是规则名词复数；单数 plew 读作 /pluː/，复数词尾在元音后读 /z/。plew 是完整借词，没有常用的派生动词或形容词；这里的 -s 是屈折词尾，不构成新的词类。
morphology_enriched.en: Plew + -s gives plews, a regular noun plural; singular plew is pronounced /pluː/, and the plural ending is /z/ after the vowel. Plew is a complete loanword with no common derived verb or adjective; -s is an inflectional ending and does not create a new part of speech.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: beaver skins（河狸皮）最直接地对应其所指；pelts（带毛兽皮）可指多种动物的完整皮张；furs（毛皮）范围更广，也可统指毛皮材料或商品。plews 另外带有北美历史皮毛贸易及计价的语境色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Beaver skins most directly matches the reference; pelts can mean whole skins with fur from various animals; furs is broader and can refer collectively to fur materials or goods. Plews additionally evokes the historical North American fur trade and its units of value.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “毛发”连到“带毛皮张”，再连到“拿河狸皮计价”；末尾 -s 表示多张。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect hair to a fur-covered skin, then to beaver skins used as value units; final -s marks more than one.

etymology_story.zh: 来自意大利语 signore 的复数 signori；signore 最终源自拉丁语 senior，原意为“较年长的”。表示年长与地位的称呼逐渐发展为对男子的礼貌敬称。
etymology_story.en: Signori comes from the Italian plural of signore, which ultimately derives from Latin senior, meaning older. A designation associated with age and status developed into a polite title for men.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是意大利语借入的复数形式：意大利语 signore 的词尾 -e 换为 -i，得到 signori；英语也使用单数形式 signor。signori 已表示复数，不能再加英语复数 -s；相关称谓有 signora（女士，复数 signore）和 signorina（小姐，复数 signorine），它们不是英语词缀派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: This is a borrowed Italian plural: Italian signore changes its final -e to -i, producing signori; English also uses the singular form signor. Signori is already plural and does not take an additional English plural -s; related titles include signora, plural signore, and signorina, plural signorine, rather than English affixal derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gentlemen（先生们）是一般称呼中最接近的英语对应；sirs（先生们）强调恭敬，常显得更正式；messieurs（诸位先生）来自法语，也用于多人姓名前。signori 保留明确的意大利语文化背景，常见于引语或意大利场景。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gentlemen is the closest ordinary English equivalent in direct address; sirs emphasizes deference and often sounds more formal; messieurs is borrowed from French and also occurs before multiple names. Signori retains a distinctly Italian setting and commonly appears in quotations or Italian contexts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为不可再分析的借词整体记忆，没有可独立识别的英语前缀或后缀。屈折形式：sirocco + -s → siroccos；异体拼写：scirocco。没有常用的派生词族，不宜把临时构造的 siroccoish 当作标准衍生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, sirocco is an unanalyzed loanword with no identifiable English prefix or suffix. Inflection: sirocco + -s → siroccos; spelling variant: scirocco. It has no common derivational family, and an occasional formation such as siroccoish should not be presented as a standard derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hot wind is a general description; simoom denotes an intensely hot, dry, dust-laden desert wind; khamsin chiefly names a seasonal hot wind in Egypt and nearby areas. These are related terms rather than interchangeable names for the sirocco.

etymology_story.en: English adopted the name in the sixteenth century from Latin sōlānum, meaning nightshade, which also supplied the New Latin botanical name. Its deeper origin is uncertain, so an interpretation such as 'sun plant' should not be treated as established. [Merriam-Webster history and definitions](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/solanum)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 solanum 是整体借词；在植物学构词中可识别词干 solan-，-um 是拉丁语词尾，并非能自由使用的英语后缀。主要相关词：solan- + -ine → solanine（龙葵碱）；solan- + -aceous → solanaceous（茄科的）；Solan- + -aceae → Solanaceae（茄科）；solanidine（龙葵啶，相关生物碱名称）。普通植物名复数可用 solanums；属名 Solanum 首字母大写，正式排版通常用斜体。
morphology_enriched.en: Solanum is a whole-word borrowing in modern English; botanical formations use the stem solan-, while -um is a Latin ending rather than a freely productive English suffix. Principal related forms are solan- + -ine → solanine, an alkaloid; solan- + -aceous → solanaceous, belonging to the nightshade family; Solan- + -aceae → Solanaceae, the family name; and solanidine, a related alkaloid name. The ordinary plant noun can take the plural solanums; the genus name Solanum is capitalized and normally italicized.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nightshade is a common name whose reference varies and can include plants outside Solanum; Solanum plant is an explicit paraphrase; solanaceous plant is broader, including other members of the family such as peppers and tobacco.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor solan- to the nightshade group: Solanum names the genus, and solanine names an associated alkaloid.

etymology_story.en: Wilco arose in the first half of the twentieth century as a shortened form of will comply, chiefly in radio communication. It combines acknowledgment and understanding of an instruction with a commitment to carry it out. [Collins history and usage](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/wilco)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：wil(l) + co(mply) → wilco，属于两个词的截短融合，不是词根加词缀。该感叹词没有常规屈折变化，也没有常用派生词族；源词 comply 的词族包括 complies、complied、complying、compliance（遵从）和 compliant（遵从的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: wil(l) + co(mply) → wilco, a fusion of clipped words rather than a root-plus-affix construction. The interjection has no regular inflections or common derivatives; the source verb comply has the related forms complies, complied, complying, compliance, and compliant.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: roger（收到）主要确认已收到信息，本身不承诺执行；understood（明白）强调理解；will do（会照办）是较日常的执行承诺。wilco 在通信语境中兼有理解和照办之意。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Roger chiefly acknowledges receipt without itself promising action; understood emphasizes comprehension; will do is an everyday promise to act. Wilco combines understanding with compliance in a communications setting.

mnemonic_anchor.en: WIL(L) CO(MPLY): understood, and action will follow.

etymology_story.en: English borrowed Turkish yaşmak in the nineteenth century as the name of a face veil. The English word retains that clothing sense, particularly in descriptions with a Turkish or Ottoman historical setting. [Collins word history](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/yashmak)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为整体借词记忆，没有可分析的英语词根与词缀。常规复数：yashmak + -s → yashmaks；异体拼写：yashmac。没有常用的派生词族；即使遇到 yashmaked 之类的语境性形式，也不能据此把 yashmak 列为常用动词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, yashmak is a whole-word borrowing without an English root-and-affix analysis. Regular plural: yashmak + -s → yashmaks; spelling variant: yashmac. It has no common derivational family; a contextual formation such as yashmaked does not establish a common verb yashmak.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: veil（面纱、罩纱）是范围最广的词；face veil（遮面纱）明确指遮住面部的织物；niqab（尼卡布面纱）通常指露出眼部的遮面服饰，与 yashmak 的文化背景和具体形式并不完全相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Veil is the broadest term; face veil explicitly identifies a covering for the face; niqab usually denotes a face covering that leaves the eyes visible and differs from yashmak in cultural associations and specific form.
