etymology_story.zh: 英语借用了意大利语 zingaro 的复数 zingari，作为对罗姆人的外部称谓，相关借词自近代早期已有记录。它通常被联系到希腊语 Athinganoi 这一历史群体名称，但更早的传承细节存在争议。[柯林斯词源与语体标注](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/zingari)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Italian zingari, the plural of zingaro, as an external name for Roma people, with related borrowing recorded since the early modern period. It is commonly linked to the Greek historical group name Athinganoi, although details of its earlier transmission remain disputed. [Collins history and register labels](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/zingari)

morphology_enriched.zh: 借入的意大利语屈折关系：zingar- + -o → zingaro（阳性单数）；zingar- + -i → zingari（阳性复数）。相关意大利语形式为 zingara（阴性单数）和 zingare（阴性复数）；这些是性数变化，不是英语派生词。英语中 zingari 已是复数，不再加 -s；意大利语中的形容词用法不应自动列为该英语借词的常用词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Borrowed Italian inflection: zingar- + -o → zingaro, masculine singular; zingar- + -i → zingari, masculine plural. Related Italian forms are zingara, feminine singular, and zingare, feminine plural; these are gender-and-number inflections rather than English derivatives. In English, zingari is already plural and does not take an additional -s; its adjectival use in Italian does not automatically constitute a common English adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Roma（罗姆人）和 Romani people（罗姆族人）是现代通常采用的族群名称；Gypsies（吉普赛人）是历史上常见的外部称谓，在许多语境中被视为冒犯性用语，但部分群体也自称如此。zingari 更具意大利语色彩，在现代英语中主要用于历史材料或对该称谓本身的讨论。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Roma and Romani people are usual modern names for the ethnic group; Gypsies is a longstanding external designation considered offensive in many contexts, although some communities use it for themselves. Zingari has a more specifically Italian association and now appears chiefly in historical material or discussion of the term itself.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Change -o to -i: one zingaro, several zingari; recognize it as a historical ethnic designation.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由英国作家 J. B. 普里斯特利于20世纪中叶创造，将 ad（广告）与 mass（大众）组合起来。它带有批评意味，既指广告影响下的大众，也指大众传媒推动的物质消费文化。
etymology_story.en: The British writer J. B. Priestley coined the word in the mid-twentieth century by combining ad with mass. It critically describes both the public shaped by advertising and the materialistic consumer culture encouraged by mass media.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：ad（advertisement“广告”的缩略形式）+ mass（大众）→ admass。通常作集合名词或不可数名词，没有常用的独立派生词；admass society（广告消费社会）中的 admass 是名词作定语，不必另立形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: ad, a shortening of advertisement, + mass → admass. It normally functions as a collective or uncountable noun and has no established common derivatives; in admass society, admass is a noun modifier rather than a separate adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mass audience（大众受众）侧重传播内容的接收者；consumer society（消费社会）侧重以购买和消费为中心的社会；mass culture（大众文化）侧重大规模传播的文化形式。admass 特别强调广告塑造大众欲望，并通常含有批评意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mass audience emphasizes recipients of media content; consumer society emphasizes a society organized around buying and consuming; mass culture emphasizes widely distributed cultural forms. Admass specifically highlights advertising's influence on public desires and usually carries a critical tone.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经新拉丁语源自希腊语 amphibios，意为“过双重生活的”，由 amphi-（两者、两边）与 bios（生命、生活）构成。它后来成为两栖纲的分类名称，名称反映了许多两栖动物与水陆两种环境的联系。
etymology_story.en: The word comes through New Latin from Greek amphibios, meaning 'living a double life,' formed from amphi- meaning 'both' and bios meaning 'life.' It became the name of a zoological class, reflecting the association of many amphibians with both water and land.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常将 Amphibia 作为整体借入的分类名称，不把它视为可自由生成的普通派生词；历史结构可分析为 amphi-（两者）+ bi-（来自 bios“生命、生活”的词干成分）+ -a（中性复数词尾）。常用相关词族：amphibian（两栖动物；两栖动物的）、amphibians（两栖动物，复数）、amphibious（两栖的；水陆两用的）、amphibiously（以两栖或水陆两用的方式）、amphibiousness（两栖性；水陆两用性）；这些形式共享历史词根，并非都直接由 amphibia 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats Amphibia as a borrowed taxonomic name rather than a freely productive derivative; its historical structure is amphi- meaning 'both' + bi-, a stem element from bios meaning 'life,' + the neuter plural ending -a. The usual related family includes amphibian, amphibians, amphibious, amphibiously, and amphibiousness; these forms share historical roots and are not all direct derivatives of amphibia.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: amphibians（两栖动物）是现代普通英语中更自然的称呼；batrachians（蛙类；旧时也泛指两栖动物）较旧且范围随用法而异。Amphibia 主要用于正式动物分类，不能用 water animals（水生动物）准确替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Amphibians is the usual modern everyday term; batrachians is older and may refer specifically to frogs and toads or more broadly to amphibians, depending on usage. Amphibia chiefly belongs to formal zoological classification and is not equivalent to water animals.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: amphi- 表示“两边”，bios 表示“生活”：名称让人联想到水陆两种生活环境。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Amphi- means 'both' and bios means 'life': connect the name with life associated with water and land.

etymology_story.zh: 该词在19世纪作为新拉丁语属名进入科学命名，源自希腊语 anōphelēs，意为“无益的、无用的”，由否定成分 an- 与表示“益处”的 ophelos 构成。后来英语也用小写 anopheles 指该属的一只蚊子；原始词义本身并不表示“传播疟疾”。
etymology_story.en: The word entered scientific nomenclature in the nineteenth century as a New Latin genus name from Greek anōphelēs, meaning 'unprofitable' or 'useless,' formed with negative an- and ophelos, 'benefit.' English later also used lowercase anopheles for an individual mosquito of the genus; the original Greek meaning does not itself mean 'malaria carrier.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 anopheles 是整体借词，单复数通常同形；科学属名写作 Anopheles。相关形式采用词干 anophel-：anophel- + -ine → anopheline（按蚊的；按蚊），名词复数为 anophelines；这里的 -es 不是英语复数词尾，不能按普通复数规则删除。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, anopheles is a borrowed word whose singular and plural are normally identical; the scientific genus name is capitalized Anopheles. Related forms use the stem anophel-: anophel- + -ine → anopheline, an adjective meaning 'of anopheles mosquitoes' and a noun meaning one such mosquito, with the plural anophelines; the ending -es is not an English plural suffix.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: anopheline（按蚊）是名词用法中的近义表达，也可作形容词；mosquito（蚊子）范围更广，包括许多其他属；malaria vector（疟疾传播媒介）强调传播功能，并不等同于所有按蚊。不是每种按蚊、也不是每只按蚊都传播疟疾。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Anopheline is a close equivalent when used as a noun and also functions as an adjective; mosquito is broader and includes many other genera; malaria vector emphasizes the role of transmitting malaria rather than membership in the genus. Not every anopheles species or individual transmits malaria.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 词源逻辑是“无益”；现代识别锚点是“按蚊属，其中一些种类传播疟疾”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The historical hook is 'without benefit'; the modern identification hook is the mosquito genus containing some malaria vectors.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语 asperger 源自拉丁语 aspergere，意为“洒向、溅上”，其历史构成与 ad-（向）和 spargere（散布、洒）有关。英语保留了洒水的含义，尤其用于宗教仪式中洒圣水的语境。
etymology_story.en: The word comes through French asperger from Latin aspergere, meaning 'to sprinkle upon,' historically formed from ad- meaning 'toward' and spargere meaning 'to scatter or sprinkle.' English retained the sprinkling sense, especially in religious ceremonies involving holy water.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 asperge 作为整体动词词干；规则变化为 asperges（第三人称单数）、asperged（过去式及过去分词）、asperging（现在分词，去掉词尾 e）。较少见的 asperger（洒水者；洒圣水器）可分析为 asperg- + -er；历史同源词包括 aspergillum（洒圣水器，复数 aspergilla 或 aspergillums）、asperse（诽谤）和 aspersion（诽谤言论；较旧义为洒水），后几项不能都当作现代英语直接加后缀形成的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats asperge as a whole verb stem; its regular forms are asperges, asperged, and asperging, with final e dropped before -ing. The rare asperger, meaning a person or instrument that sprinkles, can be analyzed as asperg- + -er; historical relatives include aspergillum, a holy-water sprinkler with plurals aspergilla or aspergillums, asperse, and aspersion, whose older sprinkling sense developed figuratively into damaging allegations. These historical relatives are not all direct modern suffix formations from asperge.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sprinkle（洒）是最普通的词，强调散落少量液滴或颗粒；spray（喷洒）强调液体以细滴喷出；besprinkle（洒满、洒上）较文学化。asperge 极少见，尤其带有宗教仪式色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sprinkle is the ordinary word for scattering small drops or particles; spray emphasizes liquid projected in fine droplets; besprinkle is literary and means to scatter drops or particles over something. Asperge is very rare and particularly associated with religious ritual.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 沿词源记“向某物散洒水滴”，再连接到仪式中的“洒圣水”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture drops scattered onto something, then connect that action with the ritual sprinkling of holy water.

etymology_story.zh: briony 是 bryony 的异体拼写；这个植物名经古法语和拉丁语传入英语，远源为希腊语 bryōnia。该希腊词通常与表示“繁茂生长”的 bryein 联系起来，呼应这种植物旺盛的攀缘生长。
etymology_story.en: Briony is a spelling variant of bryony, a plant name that reached English through Old French and Latin from Greek bryōnia. The Greek name is generally connected with bryein, meaning “to grow luxuriantly,” reflecting the plant’s vigorous growth.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，briony 是不可再作常用词缀分析的植物名；复数为 brionies，常见异体及其复数为 bryony、bryonies。相关专业词 bryonin（泻根苷）可分析为植物名词干 bryon- + 物质名后缀 -in，不宜简单理解为 briony 直接去掉 y 后加后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, briony is a plant name without a productive prefix-and-suffix breakdown; its plural is brionies, and the usual alternative forms are bryony and bryonies. The related technical term bryonin, a glycoside obtained from bryony, contains the botanical stem bryon- and the substance suffix -in; it is not simply formed by removing y from briony.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bryony 与 briony 指同一种植物名称，区别仅在拼写，前者更常见；white bryony（白泻根）和 red bryony（红泻根）指其中的具体种类，不能在所有语境中替换这个统称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bryony is an exact spelling equivalent and is more usual. White bryony and red bryony name particular kinds of bryony, so they are narrower terms rather than interchangeable synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住词源中的“繁茂生长”：泻根藤沿树篱旺盛攀长；briony 与 bryony 是同名异拼。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the historical idea of luxuriant growth with a vine climbing vigorously through a hedge; briony and bryony are alternative spellings.

etymology_story.zh: caeca 是 caecum 的拉丁式复数；caecum 源自拉丁语 intestinum caecum，字面意思是“盲的肠道”。“盲”指囊袋一端封闭，后来这个名称也用于其他类似的解剖结构。
etymology_story.en: Caeca is the Latin plural of caecum, shortened from Latin intestinum caecum, literally “blind intestine.” “Blind” describes the closed end of the pouch, and the name was extended to comparable anatomical structures.

morphology_enriched.zh: 屈折变化公式：caecum 的词尾 -um → -a，得到复数 caeca；-a 在这里是拉丁式复数词尾。相关词族包括 caecum（盲肠、盲囊）、caecal（盲肠的）和 caecectomy（盲肠切除术）；美式拼写通常为 cecum、ceca、cecal、cecectomy。
morphology_enriched.en: Inflectional pattern: replace the -um ending of caecum with -a to form caeca; -a is a Latin plural ending here. Related forms include caecum, caecal, and caecectomy; the usual American spellings are cecum, ceca, cecal, and cecectomy.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ceca 是美式等义拼写；caecal pouches（盲肠囊、盲囊）是解释性表达；blind pouches（盲端囊袋）范围更广，并非所有盲端囊袋都称为 caeca。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ceca is the equivalent American spelling. Caecal pouches is an explanatory expression, while blind pouches is broader and can describe structures that are not specifically called caeca.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “盲”就是一端不通：一个 caecum，多个 caeca。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think “blind-ended pouch”: one caecum, several caeca.

etymology_story.zh: callisthenic 属于十九世纪形成的 callisthenics 词族，其希腊语构词成分分别表示“美”和“力量”。这个名称把强健体魄与优美、协调的身体动作联系起来。
etymology_story.en: Callisthenic belongs to the nineteenth-century word family of callisthenics, formed from Greek elements meaning “beauty” and “strength.” The name links physical strength with graceful, coordinated movement.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：calli-（美）+ sthen-（力量）+ -ic（……的）→ callisthenic。核心词族为 callisthenic（形容词）和 callisthenics（徒手健身体操、训练体系；形式以 -s 结尾，通常作不可数名词）；单写一个 l 的 calisthenic、calisthenics 也是标准拼写，尤见于美式英语。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: calli- “beauty” + sthen- “strength” + -ic “relating to” → callisthenic. The core family consists of the adjective callisthenic and the usually uncountable noun callisthenics, whose final -s does not normally indicate a countable plural; calisthenic and calisthenics are standard single-l spellings, especially in American English.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bodyweight（自重训练的）强调以自身重量作为阻力，与本词最接近；gymnastic（体操的）更强调体操技巧，也可涉及器械；conditioning（体能训练的）范围更广，可涵盖耐力、力量等训练。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bodyweight is the closest alternative and emphasizes using your own weight as resistance. Gymnastic emphasizes gymnastics skills and may involve apparatus, while conditioning covers a wider range of training for physical fitness.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “美”+“力量”：用自身重量练出有力而协调的动作。
mnemonic_anchor.en: “Beauty” plus “strength”: use your own body weight to build strong, coordinated movement.

etymology_story.zh: canzona 借自意大利语，是 canzone“歌曲”的变体，远源为拉丁语 cantio“歌”，与 canere“唱”同源。这个名称最初指歌曲，后来也用于受声乐作品影响而发展的器乐曲。
etymology_story.en: Canzona was borrowed from Italian as a variant of canzone, meaning “song,” ultimately from Latin cantio, related to canere, “to sing.” Originally referring to songs, the name also came to denote instrumental compositions developed from vocal models.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 canzona 作为完整借词使用，不宜强拆为英语词根与词缀；复数可用 canzonas 或意大利式 canzone。相关借词包括 canzone（歌曲；亦指意大利诗体）、canzonet 和 canzonetta（短小轻快的歌曲）；意大利语 canzonetta 可分析为 canzon-（歌曲词干）+ -etta（指小后缀）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats canzona as a whole borrowed word rather than a productive English root-and-affix formation; its plurals are canzonas and Italian canzone. Related borrowings include canzone, canzonet, and canzonetta; Italian canzonetta contains the stem canzon- “song” and the diminutive suffix -etta.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: canzone 在歌曲义上与本词密切重合，但还可指一种诗体；chanson（法语歌曲）是器乐坎佐纳的重要历史来源之一，并非同一体裁名称；instrumental piece（器乐曲）可解释其常见含义，但范围远大于 canzona。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Canzone closely overlaps with the song sense but can also name a poetic form. Chanson denotes a French song and was an important historical model for instrumental canzonas; instrumental piece is a useful explanation but is much broader.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“唱”到“奏”：名字源于歌曲，后来也指带有歌曲渊源的器乐曲。
mnemonic_anchor.en: From singing to playing: the name began with songs and came to include instrumental music with vocal origins.

senses.meaning_zh: 厘克（质量单位，等于百分之一克，即十毫克）
senses.meaning_en: A metric unit of mass equal to one hundredth of a gram, or ten milligrams.
senses.english_definition: A centigram is a unit of mass equal to one hundredth of a gram.
senses.collocation_zh: 一厘克；几厘克

senses.sentence_zh: 这个样品的质量为一厘克，即十毫克。

etymology_story.zh: centigram 来自法语 centigramme，是公制命名体系中 centi-“百分之一”与 gramme“克”的组合。centi- 最终源于拉丁语 centum“百”，在公制中表示基本单位的百分之一。
etymology_story.en: Centigram comes from French centigramme, combining the metric prefix centi-, “one hundredth,” with gramme, “gram.” Centi- ultimately derives from Latin centum, “hundred,” and denotes one hundredth of a base unit in metric names.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：centi-（百分之一）+ gram（克）→ centigram（厘克）；复数为 centigrams，异体拼写为 centigramme，复数为 centigrammes，单位符号为 cg。相关构词系列包括 gram（克）、milligram（毫克）、decigram（分克）和 kilogram（千克），它们是在 gram 前加不同单位前缀形成的平行词。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: centi- “one hundredth” + gram → centigram; the plural is centigrams, with alternative forms centigramme and centigrammes, and the unit symbol is cg. Related parallel formations include gram, milligram, decigram, and kilogram, which use different metric prefixes with gram.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: centigramme 是等义异体拼写；one hundredth of a gram（百分之一克）和 ten milligrams（十毫克）是完全等值的表达，区别在于单位写法，本词没有另一个常用的独立词汇近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Centigramme is an equivalent spelling. One hundredth of a gram and ten milligrams express exactly the same mass using different unit expressions; there is no separate everyday lexical synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: centi- 就是百分之一：100 厘克 = 1 克，1 厘克 = 10 毫克。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Centi- means one hundredth: 100 centigrams make 1 gram, and 1 centigram equals 10 milligrams.

etymology_story.zh: 这个名称取自英国作家埃德蒙·克莱里休·本特利的中间名；他创作并推广了这种诙谐人物短诗。人名由此变成了诗体名称。
etymology_story.en: The name comes from the middle name of the English writer Edmund Clerihew Bentley, who devised and popularized this humorous biographical verse form. A personal name thus became the name of a poetic form.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为不可再分析的名词词干使用，不宜拆成有意义的词根和词缀。常用屈折形式：clerihew → clerihews（复数）；没有通行的常用派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, clerihew is an unanalyzable noun stem rather than a meaningful combination of roots and affixes. Its regular plural is clerihews; it has no established family of commonly used derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 近义或相关词：humorous verse（诙谐诗）是上位概念；limerick（五行打油诗）有五行，通常采用 AABBA 韵式；epigram（警句短诗）强调简短机智，不必描写人物，也不限定四行。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Related terms: humorous verse is the broader category; a limerick has five lines and normally follows an AABBA rhyme scheme; an epigram emphasizes brevity and wit without necessarily describing a person or having four lines.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 本特利的中间名，变成“四行人物漫画诗”的名字。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bentley's middle name became a label for a four-line verbal caricature.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在19世纪从法语借入 cretonne，用来称呼一种装饰织物，其所指后来主要是印花棉布。该法语名称的更早来源并不确定，不能把它确定地解释为源自某个村名。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed cretonne from French in the nineteenth century as the name of a furnishing fabric, later chiefly associated with printed cotton. The French word's deeper origin is uncertain, so its derivation from a particular village name should not be presented as established.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 cretonne 是整体借入的单纯词，不能可靠地拆分为英语词根和词缀。通常作不可数名词；cretonne curtains 中的 cretonne 是名词作定语，没有因此形成独立的常用形容词词性；无常用派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Cretonne is a simplex loanword in modern English and has no reliable breakdown into English roots and affixes. It is normally uncountable; in cretonne curtains, the noun functions attributively without establishing a separate common adjective. There is no commonly used derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 近义或相关词：chintz（印花上光棉布）通常有光泽；calico（印花棉布或本色棉布）含义随英美用法变化，不专指家具装饰用途；upholstery fabric（家具包覆面料）强调用途，范围比 cretonne 更广。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Related terms: chintz typically has a glazed finish; calico varies in meaning between British and American English and is not specifically a furnishing fabric; upholstery fabric describes a use and covers a wider range of materials than cretonne.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词联想：窗帘与家具罩上的厚实印花布。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture sturdy patterned cloth covering curtains and furniture.

etymology_story.zh: czarina 与 czar 同源，并通过欧洲语言中的女性称号形式形成，历史上对应俄语 tsaritsa；czar 最终可追溯到拉丁语 Caesar。它先表示皇室女性称号，后来也比喻某个领域中权力很大的女性。
etymology_story.en: Czarina belongs to the same title family as czar and developed through European feminine title forms, historically corresponding to Russian tsaritsa; czar ultimately goes back to Latin Caesar. The royal title later acquired a figurative use for a woman with exceptional power in a particular field.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可按 czar（沙皇；掌权者）+ -ina（此称号中的女性形式成分）理解，但 -ina 不是英语中可任意套用的常用女性后缀。复数：czarinas；异体拼写：tsarina、tzarina；相关词族：czar/tsar、czardom/tsardom（沙皇统治或领土）、czarist/tsarist（沙皇主义者；沙皇制度的）、czarism/tsarism（沙皇制度）。
morphology_enriched.en: Synchronically, the word can be understood as czar plus the feminine title element -ina, although -ina is not a freely productive feminine suffix in English. The plural is czarinas; spelling variants include tsarina and tzarina. Related family members include czar/tsar, czardom/tsardom, czarist/tsarist, and czarism/tsarism.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tsarina 是异体拼写，意义相同；empress（女皇；皇后）适用于不同帝国，范围更广；queen（女王；王后）通常对应王国，在历史称号中不能随意替代 czarina。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tsarina is a spelling variant with the same meaning; empress is a broader title used across different empires; queen normally refers to a kingdom and is not freely interchangeable with czarina as a historical title.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: czar 的女性称号：从皇宫里的女皇、皇后，延伸到行业里的女掌门。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of the female counterpart of a czar: royal power extended to professional power.

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自科学拉丁语分类名称 Dicotyledones，由表示“二”的成分和表示“子叶”的 cotyledon 构成。cotyledon 远源于希腊语中表示“小杯、杯状凹部”的词，后来被用于植物的子叶。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from the scientific Latin classification name Dicotyledones, combining an element meaning 'two' with cotyledon, 'seed leaf.' Cotyledon ultimately derives from a Greek word for a small cup or cup-shaped hollow and was later applied to a plant's seed leaf.

morphology_enriched.zh: di-（二）+ cotyledon（子叶）→ dicotyledon；复数：dicotyledons。主要相关形式：dicotyledonous（双子叶的）、dicot（常用简称，双子叶植物）、dicots（其复数）；基础词族包括 cotyledon（子叶）和 cotyledonary（子叶的）。monocotyledon（单子叶植物）是平行构词；eudicot（真双子叶植物）是相关的现代分类名称，并不等于传统双子叶植物的全部。
morphology_enriched.en: Di- 'two' + cotyledon 'seed leaf' forms dicotyledon; the plural is dicotyledons. Principal related forms are dicotyledonous, the shortened noun dicot, and its plural dicots; the base family includes cotyledon and cotyledonary. Monocotyledon is a parallel formation, while eudicot is a related modern classification term that does not cover every traditional dicotyledon.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dicot 是 dicotyledon 的常用简称；dicotyledonous plant 是同义描述；eudicot（真双子叶植物）只指传统双子叶植物中的一个演化支，不能作为完全同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dicot is the usual shortened synonym; dicotyledonous plant is an equivalent descriptive expression; eudicot denotes an evolutionary lineage within the traditional dicotyledons and is not an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: di- 表示二，cotyledon 表示子叶：胚里两片子叶。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Di- means two: picture two seed leaves inside the embryo.

etymology_story.zh: droits 是 droit 的复数；droit 借自法语，既表示“权利”，也表示“依法应收的税费”，最终与拉丁语 directum 所表达的“正当、正义”概念相关。税费义体现了从“有权收取”到“应收款项”的语义发展。
etymology_story.en: Droits is the plural of droit, borrowed from French, where the word can mean both a right and a legally payable duty; it ultimately relates to Latin directum and the idea of what is right or just. The financial sense reflects a development from an entitlement to collect something to the payment itself.

morphology_enriched.zh: droit（权利；应收税费）+ -s（复数）→ droits。它是名词的复数形式，不是独立派生词；现代普通英语中没有常用的直接派生词族。此处词尾 -s 读 /s/，整个词通常采用英语读音。
morphology_enriched.en: Droit 'right; due' + the plural ending -s forms droits. This is an inflected plural rather than a separate derivation, and there is no common family of direct derivatives in general modern English. The final -s is pronounced /s/ in the usual anglicized pronunciation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: rights（权利）对应依法享有的权益；dues（应缴款项）强调按规定应付的钱款；duties（税，尤指关税）强调征税，最接近 droits 的旧关税义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rights corresponds to legal entitlements; dues emphasizes payments owed under an established obligation; duties refers to taxes, especially customs taxes, and is closest to the older customs sense of droits.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 有权收取的钱，就是依法应缴的税费；-s 表示复数。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A right to collect becomes a due to pay; -s makes it plural.

etymology_story.zh: 这是由希腊语来源的 epi-（在……上、向……）和 -scope（观察仪器）构成的科学仪器名称。其技术含义指利用物体表面反射的光形成投影。
etymology_story.en: This scientific instrument name combines Greek-derived epi-, meaning 'on' or 'upon', with -scope, meaning a viewing instrument. Its technical meaning concerns projection using light reflected from an object's surface.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：epi-（在……上）+ -scope（观察仪器）→ episcope。词族包括复数 episcopes，以及技术形容词 episcopic（实物投影的）；相关词 epidiascope（实物与透明片两用投影仪）与它共享词根。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: epi- ('on, upon') + -scope ('viewing instrument') → episcope. Its family includes the plural episcopes and the technical adjective episcopic ('relating to opaque projection'); the related word epidiascope denotes a projector for both opaque and transparent material.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: opaque projector（不透明物体投影仪）是直接近义词，明确说明投影对象；epidiascope（两用投影仪）是相关仪器名称，除实物外还能投射透明片，功能范围更广。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Opaque projector is a direct synonym that explicitly identifies the material projected. Epidiascope names a related instrument with a broader function: it can project both opaque objects and transparencies.

mnemonic_anchor.en: View light reflected from a surface, then project the object's image.

etymology_story.zh: fettling 来自动词 fettle，原有准备妥当、整理或使恢复良好状态等含义，后来发展出铸造、陶瓷和炉床修整方面的技术用法。fettle 的更早来源并不完全确定，有词源解释将它与古英语 fetel（带子）联系起来，但不宜将这一联系视为定论。
etymology_story.en: Fettling comes from fettle, a verb meaning to prepare, arrange, or put into good condition, which developed technical uses in casting, pottery, and furnace maintenance. The verb's earlier origin is uncertain; a proposed connection with Old English fetel, 'a belt', should not be treated as established.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：fettle 去掉不发音的词尾 e + -ing → fettling，既可作过程或材料名词，也可作动词现在分词。词族包括 fettle、fettles、fettled、fettling，以及 fettler（清理工、修整工）；名词 fettle 还表示状态，常见于 in fine fettle（状态很好）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: fettle drops its silent final e and takes -ing → fettling, used as a process or material noun and as a present participle. The family includes fettle, fettles, fettled, fettling, and fettler ('a worker who cleans or finishes items'); the noun fettle also means condition, especially in in fine fettle.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: finishing（精整）范围更广，指使产品达到最终状态的加工；deburring（去毛刺）专指清除毛刺或锐边；dressing（修整）强调处理表面、边缘或形状。这些近义词主要对应加工义，不对应炉床材料义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Finishing is broader and covers work that brings a product to its final condition. Deburring specifically removes burrs or sharp edges, while dressing concerns treating a surface, edge, or shape. These alternatives relate mainly to the processing sense, not the furnace-material sense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心是“收拾妥当”：铸件修整好，炉床修补好，机器调整好。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'put into good order': finish the casting, repair the hearth, adjust the machine.

etymology_story.zh: flitch 源自古英语 flicce，指一侧猪肉，与其他日耳曼语言中表示肉片或肉块的词有亲缘关系。后来它扩展到形状相似的纵切木板和加固板，并由木材名词义产生了加工动词义。
etymology_story.en: Flitch comes from Old English flicce, meaning a side of pork, and has relatives in other Germanic languages referring to pieces of meat. It later extended to similarly shaped timber slabs and reinforcing plates, with the woodworking noun also giving rise to a verb.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 flitch 是不可再作常用词缀拆分的基础词。词族为 flitch、flitches、flitched、flitching；常见技术复合词包括 flitch plate（组合梁夹钢板）和 flitch beam（木材与钢板组合梁）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, flitch is a base word without a productive internal affix division. Its family consists of flitch, flitches, flitched, and flitching; technical compounds include flitch plate and flitch beam, a beam combining timber with steel reinforcement.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: side of bacon（一整侧腌猪肉）最接近肉食义；slab（厚板、厚片）强调厚而扁平的形状，适用材料更广；plank（木板）通常指已加工成较规则形状的板材，而 flitch 可保留原木的自然边缘。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Side of bacon closely matches the meat sense. Slab emphasizes a thick, flat shape and applies to many materials. Plank usually suggests a more regularly shaped board, whereas a timber flitch may retain the log's natural edges.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture one substantial flat piece: a side of pork, a slab of timber, or a reinforcing plate.

etymology_story.zh: hanaper 经中古英语借自盎格鲁法语或古法语 hanapier，原指盛放杯子的容器，源于 hanap（杯子）。英语中的词义后来转向装公文的柳条篮；现代词 hamper 也由这个词的缩略形式发展而来。
etymology_story.en: Hanaper entered Middle English from Anglo-French or Old French hanapier, originally a container for cups, from hanap, 'a cup'. In English it came to denote a wicker basket for documents; hamper also developed from a shortened form of this word.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 hanaper 应作为整体词记忆，复数为 hanapers，没有常用的现代派生词。历史结构为 hanap（杯子）+ 法语后缀 -ier（形成相关器物名称）；hamper 是历史上由它演变出的相关词，并非现代英语加词缀产生的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, hanaper is best treated as a whole word; its plural is hanapers, and it has no common modern derivatives. Historically, it contains hanap ('cup') and the French suffix -ier forming an associated container name; hamper is a historically developed relative, not a modern affixal derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: wicker basket（柳条篮）只说明材质与器物类型；document basket（公文篮）说明用途；hamper（大篮子）是历史相关词，现代通常用于装食物、衣物等，不带 hanaper 特有的旧时公文管理含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wicker basket identifies the material and type of container. Document basket identifies its purpose. Hamper is historically related but now usually denotes a large basket for things such as food or laundry, without hanaper's specific historical administrative associations.

senses.english_definition: Hirudin is a protein found in the saliva of blood-feeding leeches that prevents blood from clotting by blocking the action of thrombin.

etymology_story.zh: hirudin 是以拉丁语 hirudo（水蛭；属格为 hirudinis）为基础、采用物质名称词尾 -in 构成的科学名称。它因来源于水蛭分泌物而得名，特指其中能够抑制凝血酶的抗凝蛋白。
etymology_story.en: Hirudin is a scientific name based on Latin hirudo, 'leech', whose genitive is hirudinis, using the substance ending -in. Named for its source in leech secretions, it specifically denotes the anticoagulant protein that inhibits thrombin.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习性拆分可记为 hirud-（水蛭，拉丁语来源）+ -in（蛋白质或其他物质名称常见词尾）→ hirudin。该词通常作不可数名词，hirudins 可指不同类型的水蛭素；同源相关词有 hirudinean（水蛭类的；水蛭类动物）和 hirudotherapy（水蛭疗法），但它们并非由 hirudin 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: For modern learning, the word can be analyzed as hirud- ('leech', from Latin) + -in, an ending common in names of proteins and other substances. Hirudin is normally uncountable, while hirudins can denote different forms; root-related words include hirudinean ('relating to leeches; a leech') and hirudotherapy ('leech therapy'), neither directly derived from hirudin.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: leech anticoagulant（水蛭抗凝物质）是描述性近义表达，但可能涵盖其他成分；direct thrombin inhibitor（直接凝血酶抑制剂）是按作用机制划分的上位术语；anticoagulant（抗凝剂）范围最广，还包括通过其他机制发挥作用的物质。这些表达均不能在所有语境中与 hirudin 完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Leech anticoagulant is a descriptive near-equivalent but may include other substances. Direct thrombin inhibitor is a broader category defined by mechanism. Anticoagulant is broader still and includes substances acting through other mechanisms. None is fully interchangeable with hirudin in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.en: A feeding leech needs blood to keep flowing: hirud- points to the leech, and hirudin blocks clotting.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 kalmia 来自新拉丁语植物属名 Kalmia，该属名为纪念植物学家 Pehr Kalm 而创制。属名后来成为英语普通名词，用来指该属的植物。
etymology_story.en: English kalmia comes from the New Latin genus name Kalmia, coined in honor of the botanist Pehr Kalm. The genus name subsequently became an English common noun for a plant belonging to that genus.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常作为完整借词使用；其命名结构为 Kalm（人名）+ -ia（植物属名中常见的拉丁化词尾）。可数名词复数为 kalmias；正式属名写作 Kalmia，首字母大写，无常用派生动词、形容词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, kalmia normally functions as a whole borrowed word; its naming structure is Kalm, a surname, + -ia, a Latinizing ending common in botanical genus names. The count-noun plural is kalmias; the formal genus name is capitalized Kalmia, and there are no common derived verbs, adjectives, or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 相关名称：mountain laurel（阔叶山月桂，通常指 Kalmia latifolia）和 sheep laurel（狭叶山月桂，通常指 Kalmia angustifolia）。两者都是山月桂属的具体植物名称，范围比 kalmia 窄，不能在所有语境中替换它。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Related names are mountain laurel, usually Kalmia latifolia, and sheep laurel, usually Kalmia angustifolia. Both name particular members of the genus and are therefore narrower than kalmia, rather than interchangeable synonyms in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Kalm 的名字留在花丛里：Kalm → Kalmia → 山月桂属灌木。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Kalm's name lives in the flowers: Kalm → Kalmia → a flowering shrub.

morphology_enriched.zh: kiang 是不可按英语词根和词缀继续拆分的借词。复数可用 kiang 或 kiangs；Tibetan + kiang 等属于修饰语组合，不是派生词，无常用派生动词、形容词或副词。

etymology_story.zh: lambkin 由 lamb（羔羊）加表示小或亲昵的后缀 -kin 构成，该后缀与中古荷兰语的指小形式有关。这个词既指小羊羔，也通过羔羊温顺可爱的形象转用于亲昵称呼。
etymology_story.en: Lambkin combines lamb with -kin, a diminutive or affectionate suffix associated with Middle Dutch diminutive forms. Besides naming a little lamb, it became an affectionate term for a person through the lamb's associations with gentleness and innocence.

morphology_enriched.zh: lamb + -kin（小、亲昵）→ lambkin；复数为 lambkins，lamb 中的 b 在 lambkin 中仍不发音。基础词族包括 lamb、lambs、lambed、lambing；常见相关复合词有 lambskin 和 lambswool。lambkin 本身无常用派生动词、形容词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: Lamb + -kin, meaning small or dear, → lambkin; the plural is lambkins, and the b of lamb remains silent. The base family includes lamb, lambs, lambed, and lambing; common related compounds include lambskin and lambswool. Lambkin itself has no common derived verbs, adjectives, or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lamb is the neutral animal name, while lambkin sounds more diminutive, affectionate, and often literary; darling is a broader term of affection; sweetheart can address a child or romantic partner and expresses warmth more directly.

etymology_story.zh: mudrock 是英语 mud（泥）和 rock（岩石）构成的透明复合词。它把细粒泥质沉积物与其固结后形成的岩石联系起来，在地质学中用作一类细粒沉积岩的总称。
etymology_story.en: Mudrock is a transparent English compound of mud and rock. It links fine muddy sediment with the rock formed after that sediment becomes consolidated and serves in geology as a collective term for fine-grained sedimentary rocks.

morphology_enriched.zh: mud + rock → mudrock，是名词加名词的复合结构。可作不可数材料名称，也可用复数 mudrocks 指不同种类或岩体；相关基础词族有 mud、muddy、muddiness、rock、rocky，常见相关地质复合词有 mudstone 和 claystone，但它们不是 mudrock 的词缀派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Mud + rock → mudrock is a noun–noun compound. It can function as a mass noun, while mudrocks refers to different types or bodies of such rock; related base families include mud, muddy, muddiness, rock, and rocky. Related geological compounds include mudstone and claystone, but these are not affixal derivatives of mudrock.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mudstone（泥岩）通常指不易沿薄层劈开的泥质岩；shale（页岩）强调能够沿薄层劈开的性质；argillaceous rock（黏土质岩石）强调黏土成分，其适用范围与 mudrock 不完全重合。mudrock 常作为包含若干细粒沉积岩类型的总称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mudstone usually denotes mudrock without pronounced splitting into thin sheets; shale emphasizes that fissile character; argillaceous rock emphasizes clay content and does not have exactly the same scope as mudrock. Mudrock commonly serves as an umbrella term for several fine-grained sedimentary rock types.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 泥变成岩石：mud + rock → 泥质沉积岩。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Mud becomes rock: mud + rock → fine-grained sedimentary rock.

senses.meaning_zh: 糜棱岩；强烈韧性剪切变形形成的细粒变质岩
senses.meaning_en: A fine-grained metamorphic rock formed through intense ductile shearing.
senses.english_definition: Mylonite is rock whose mineral grains have become smaller as the rock has been strongly deformed, especially within a shear zone.
senses.collocation_zh: 糜棱岩带；富石英糜棱岩
senses.sentence_en: The geologists mapped a narrow band of mylonite along the shear zone.
senses.sentence_zh: 地质学家沿剪切带绘出了一条狭窄的糜棱岩带。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在19世纪由希腊语中表示“磨坊”的词与岩石名称后缀 -ite 构成，名称体现了岩石仿佛被磨细的外观。现代地质学强调其韧性变形与重结晶过程。[词源](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/mylonite)、[地质释义](https://snl.no/mylonitt)
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in the nineteenth century from a Greek word meaning 'mill' and the rock-name suffix -ite, reflecting the rock's apparently ground-down texture. Modern geology emphasizes ductile deformation and recrystallization in its formation. [Etymology](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/mylonite), [geological description](https://snl.no/mylonitt)

morphology_enriched.zh: 学术构词：mylon-（磨坊）+ -ite（岩石名称后缀）→ mylonite（糜棱岩）。主要词族：mylonitic（糜棱岩的；糜棱状的）；mylonitize / mylonitise（使糜棱岩化）；mylonitization / mylonitisation（糜棱岩化）；mylonitized / mylonitised（已糜棱岩化的）。相关分类词：protomylonite（初糜棱岩）、ultramylonite（超糜棱岩）、blastomylonite（变余糜棱岩）。复数为 mylonites。
morphology_enriched.en: Learned formation: mylon- ('mill') + -ite (a rock-name suffix) → mylonite. Principal family: mylonitic ('relating to mylonite or its texture'); mylonitize / mylonitise ('to transform into mylonite'); mylonitization / mylonitisation ('that transformation'); mylonitized / mylonitised ('having undergone it'). Related classification terms include protomylonite, ultramylonite, and blastomylonite. The plural is mylonites.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 无严格同义词。相关术语：tectonite（构造岩）范围较广；cataclasite（碎裂岩）主要由脆性破碎形成；schist（片岩）突出片理构造。mylonite 特指强烈韧性剪切及粒度减小形成的岩石。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact synonym. Related terms: tectonite is broader; cataclasite forms mainly through brittle fragmentation; schist emphasizes a foliated metamorphic texture. Mylonite specifically identifies rock shaped by intense ductile shearing and grain-size reduction.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 磨坊意象 → 岩粒变细 → 糜棱岩；实际成因抓住“韧性剪切”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a mill making grains smaller: mylonite has reduced mineral grains. Connect the actual process with ductile shearing.

senses.meaning_en: Eye-shaped markings on an animal's body, wings, or feathers.

etymology_story.zh: ocelli 是 ocellus 的拉丁式复数；ocellus 源自拉丁语 oculus（眼）的指小形式，意为“小眼睛”。该词经新拉丁语进入科学英语，既指简单的眼，也指外形像眼睛的斑纹。[词源与义项](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/ocellus)
etymology_story.en: Ocelli is the Latin-form plural of ocellus, a diminutive of Latin oculus, 'eye', meaning 'little eye'. Through New Latin, the word entered scientific English for both simple eyes and markings resembling eyes. [Etymology and senses](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/ocellus)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代屈折关系：ocell-us（单数）→ ocell-i（拉丁式复数）；不能把 ocelli 当作单数。主要词族：ocellar（单眼的）；ocellate / ocellated（有眼状斑的）；ocellation（眼状斑纹；眼状斑的分布）。历史上的指小构词属于拉丁语，不是现代英语中可自由套用的后缀规则。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern inflection: ocell-us (singular) → ocell-i (Latin-form plural); ocelli is not singular. Principal family: ocellar ('relating to ocelli'); ocellate / ocellated ('marked with eyespots'); ocellation ('eyelike markings or their arrangement'). The historical diminutive formation belongs to Latin rather than to a freely productive modern English suffix pattern.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: simple eyes（单眼）对应感光器官义；eyespots（眼点；眼状斑）可指简单感光结构，也可指装饰性斑纹，须看语境；eye-like markings（眼形斑纹）明确表示外观，通常不涉及视觉功能。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Simple eyes matches the sensory-organ sense. Eyespots can refer either to simple light-sensitive structures or to decorative markings, depending on context. Eye-like markings explicitly describes appearance and usually implies no visual function.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “小眼睛”有两种：真的小眼，或看起来像眼睛的小斑；-i 提醒复数。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'little eyes': actual simple eyes or spots resembling eyes. The ending -i signals the plural.

senses.meaning_zh: 成套首饰；设计相配的一套珠宝或饰物
senses.meaning_en: A matching set of jewelry or ornaments.
senses.english_definition: A parure is a set of matching pieces of jewelry, such as a necklace, earrings, and a bracelet, designed to be worn together.

senses.sentence_zh: 博物馆展出了一套19世纪的祖母绿首饰。

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自法语 parure（装饰；饰物），与 parer（装饰）相关，最终可追溯至拉丁语 parare（准备；安排）。英语中的珠宝义把较宽泛的“装饰物”具体化为彼此配套的一组首饰。[词源与释义](https://ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=parure)
etymology_story.en: The word comes from French parure, 'adornment', related to parer, 'to adorn', and ultimately to Latin parare, 'to prepare or arrange'. Its jewelry sense in English specializes the broader idea of adornment into a coordinated set of ornaments. [Etymology and definition](https://ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=parure)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为完整借词记忆，不强拆为英语词根和后缀。复数：parures。主要相关构词：demi-（半；部分）+ parure → demi-parure（规模较小或不完整的配套首饰，常见为项链与耳环等组合）；完整套装可称 full parure 或 complete parure。没有常用的同词干动词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, treat parure as a complete loanword rather than splitting it into English roots and suffixes. Plural: parures. Principal related formation: demi- ('half or partial') + parure → demi-parure, a smaller or incomplete matching jewelry set, often a necklace and earrings. A full set may be called a full parure or complete parure. There is no common same-stem verb or adverb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: jewelry set（首饰套装）最通俗，适用范围广；suite of jewels（成套珠宝）较正式，强调成组相配；demi-parure（半套首饰）指较小的配套组合。parure 常用于历史珠宝、收藏和拍卖语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Jewelry set is the ordinary, broadly applicable expression. Suite of jewels is more formal and emphasizes a coordinated group. Demi-parure denotes a smaller matching set. Parure is especially associated with historical jewelry, collecting, and auctions.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect 'adornment' with pieces worn together: matching necklace, earrings, and bracelet.

etymology_story.zh: poind 保留了苏格兰语的历史拼写，可追溯至古英语 pyndan（圈住；扣留），与表示围栏的 pound 同源。由“圈住牲畜”发展出的扣留概念，也用于扣押财物抵债。[词源与历史用法](https://www.dsl.ac.uk/entry/snd/poind)
etymology_story.en: Poind preserves a historical Scots spelling and goes back to Old English pyndan, 'to enclose or impound', related to pound meaning an enclosure. The idea of confining animals also extended to seizing property for debt. [Etymology and historical usage](https://www.dsl.ac.uk/entry/snd/poind)

morphology_enriched.zh: poind 在现代分析中作为完整词干。屈折形式：poinds、poinded、poinding；名词复数也为 poinds。主要派生：poind + -able → poindable（可被扣押抵债的）；poind + -er → poinder（扣押财物者；扣留牲畜的人员）；poinding 也作名词，表示扣押抵债。名词各义均属历史或地域用法。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat poind as a whole stem in modern analysis. Inflected forms: poinds, poinded, poinding; the noun plural is also poinds. Principal derivatives: poind + -able → poindable ('liable to seizure for debt'); poind + -er → poinder ('a person who seizes goods or impounds animals'); poinding also functions as a noun for seizure for debt. The noun senses are historical or regional.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: distrain（扣押财物追偿）最接近其抵债动词义；impound（依法扣留）常用于车辆或牲畜，未必涉及债务；seize（查扣；夺取）范围最广。poind 带有明确的苏格兰地域及历史色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Distrain is closest to the debt-recovery verb sense. Impound commonly concerns vehicles or livestock and need not involve debt. Seize is much broader. Poind has a specifically Scottish and historical character.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 与 pound（牲畜圈）联想：先把牲畜圈住，再把财物扣住；poind 读 /pɪnd/。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link it with pound, an animal enclosure: confine the animal, then extend the idea to holding goods for debt. Pronounce poind /pɪnd/.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古英语 pursevant 等形式，来自古法语 pursuivant，即表示“跟随；追随”的动词的现在分词。其“跟随者”之义逐渐与随从、传令使者以及级别低于纹章官的职务相联系。[词源与义项](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/pursuivant)
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English in forms such as pursevant from Old French pursuivant, the present participle of a verb meaning 'to follow or pursue'. The idea of a follower became associated with attendants, official messengers, and the heraldic office below a herald. [Etymology and senses](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/pursuivant)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为完整借词使用；历史结构为古法语 pursuiv-（跟随）+ -ant（现在分词词尾）。复数：pursuivants；职务或身份名词：pursuivantship（助理纹章官的职位或身份）。pursuivant extraordinary 是名词加后置形容词构成的职称短语。pursue（追随）、pursuit（追求）和 pursuant（依照的）属于相关词源家族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats it as a complete loanword; historically it contains Old French pursuiv- ('follow') + -ant (a present-participle ending). Plural: pursuivants; office or status noun: pursuivantship. Pursuivant extraordinary is a title phrase containing a following adjective. Pursue, pursuit, and pursuant belong to the related etymological family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: herald（纹章官；传令官）在正式纹章体系中级别高于 pursuivant；messenger（信使）只说明传递消息的职责；attendant（随从）强调侍从身份。三者分别与其不同义项相关，不能在正式职称中随意替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Herald denotes a higher rank in the formal heraldic hierarchy. Messenger describes the communication function. Attendant emphasizes accompanying or serving someone. Each relates to a different sense, and they are not interchangeable as official titles.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “跟随的人” → 随从、传令使者 → 跟随纹章官办事的低阶官员。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with 'one who follows': an attendant or messenger, then a junior officer serving within the heraldic hierarchy.

senses.meaning_zh: 利血平；一种从萝芙木属植物中提取、曾用于降血压和治疗精神疾病的生物碱
senses.meaning_en: An alkaloid obtained from rauwolfia plants and historically used to treat high blood pressure and psychiatric disorders.
senses.english_definition: Reserpine is an alkaloid from rauwolfia plants that has been used as a medicine for high blood pressure and certain psychiatric disorders.
senses.collocation_zh: 利血平治疗；利血平引起的耗竭
senses.sentence_en: The researchers measured dopamine levels after reserpine treatment.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员测定了利血平处理后的多巴胺水平。

etymology_story.zh: 英语 reserpine 在20世纪中叶借自德语 Reserpin，其名称与植物学名 Rauwolfia serpentina 有关。这是经过缩合和变形形成的药物名称，不能按现代英语词根规则逐段拆解。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed reserpine from German Reserpin in the mid-twentieth century; the name is associated with the botanical name Rauwolfia serpentina. It is a shortened and reshaped drug name rather than a transparent combination of modern English roots.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中把 reserpine 作为整体药名记忆；词尾 -ine 符合许多生物碱名称的形式，但其余部分不宜硬拆。相关派生词包括 reserpinize（用利血平处理）、reserpinized（经利血平处理的）和 reserpinization（利血平处理）；英式拼写也用 reserpinise、reserpinised、reserpinisation。reserpine + induced → reserpine-induced（由利血平引起的）是复合形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat reserpine as a whole drug name in modern English; its ending -ine follows a common alkaloid naming pattern, but the remaining letters do not support a useful modern breakdown. Related derivatives include reserpinize, reserpinized, and reserpinization, with British variants reserpinise, reserpinised, and reserpinisation. Reserpine + induced forms the compound adjective reserpine-induced.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有通用的严格同义词。Rauwolfia alkaloid（萝芙木生物碱）按来源指称一个更大的类别；antihypertensive（降压药）按用途分类；alkaloid（生物碱）则是范围更广的化学类别，三者都不能唯一指代利血平。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym. Rauwolfia alkaloid identifies a broader group by plant source; antihypertensive classifies a substance by its blood-pressure-lowering use; alkaloid names a much broader chemical category. None uniquely identifies reserpine.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把整词连到“萝芙木根中的生物碱”；-ine 提醒你这是一个生物碱药名。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the whole word to an alkaloid from rauwolfia roots; -ine provides a familiar alkaloid-name cue.

senses.meaning_zh: 塔勒；旧时德意志及其他欧洲地区使用的一种大型银币或货币单位
senses.meaning_en: A large silver coin or monetary unit formerly used in German-speaking lands and elsewhere in Europe.

etymology_story.zh: taler 借自德语 Taler，旧拼作 Thaler，是 Joachimstaler 的缩略形式，原指在波希米亚 Joachimsthal 地区铸造的银币。这一币名后来传播到其他语言，英语 dollar 也出自同一名称传统。
etymology_story.en: Taler comes from German Taler, formerly spelled Thaler, a shortening of Joachimstaler, originally a silver coin minted in the Joachimsthal area of Bohemia. The coin name spread into other languages, and English dollar ultimately belongs to the same naming tradition.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 taler 是整体借词，不拆成英语词根和后缀；复数为 talers，异体拼写 thaler 的复数为 thalers。double + taler → double taler（双塔勒币），是面值名称组合；dollar 是历史相关词，不是 taler 在现代英语中的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, taler is a whole borrowed word, with the plural talers; the spelling variant thaler has the plural thalers. Double + taler forms double taler, a denomination name. Dollar is historically related, rather than a modern English derivative of taler.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: thaler 是同一币名的异体拼写；Reichstaler（帝国塔勒）指神圣罗马帝国体系中的特定塔勒币或货币单位；silver coin（银币）只是宽泛类别，不能说明具体币制。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Thaler is a spelling variant of the same name. Reichstaler refers to a particular taler coin or monetary unit within the Holy Roman Empire's monetary system. Silver coin is a broad category and does not identify a specific currency.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Joachimsthal 的银币 → Joachimstaler → taler；再联想到同源的 dollar。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A silver coin from Joachimsthal became a Joachimstaler, then a taler; connect it with the historically related dollar.

senses.meaning_zh: 小麦属；该属植物，包括普通小麦等
senses.meaning_en: The wheat genus, or a plant belonging to it.
senses.english_definition: Triticum is the scientific name of the genus of grasses that includes wheat.

senses.sentence_en: The study compared several species of Triticum.

etymology_story.zh: triticum 来自拉丁语 triticum，意为“小麦”，后来用作小麦属的科学名称。这个拉丁词与 terere（磨、搓）及其分词形式 tritum 有关，体现了谷物经搓磨或脱粒处理的联系。
etymology_story.en: Triticum comes from Latin triticum, meaning wheat, and was adopted as the scientific name of the wheat genus. The Latin word is related to terere, meaning to rub or grind, and its participial form tritum, connecting the grain with rubbing or threshing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中把 triticum 作为整体拉丁借词；正式属名写作 Triticum，并通常用斜体，不把 -um 当作英语派生后缀。Triticum（小麦属）与 Secale（黑麦属）的部分形式缩合为 triticale（小黑麦）；这是缩合造词，不是简单添加词缀。该词没有常用的英语动词、副词等派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat triticum as a whole Latin borrowing in modern English. The formal genus name is capitalized Triticum and normally italicized; -um is not an English derivational suffix here. Parts of Triticum and Secale, the rye genus, were blended to form triticale. There is no commonly used English family of derived verbs or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: wheat genus（小麦属）是属名的直白释义；wheat（小麦）通常指作物或籽粒；wheat plant（小麦植株）指具体植物个体。Triticum 强调分类学上的属，后三者的指称范围并不完全相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wheat genus is a plain-language equivalent of the genus name. Wheat usually refers to the crop or its grain, while wheat plant refers to an individual plant. Triticum specifically identifies the taxonomic genus, so these expressions are not interchangeable in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“搓磨、脱粒”想到麦粒，再把 Triticum 锚定为“小麦属”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of rubbing or threshing grain, then anchor Triticum to the wheat genus.

etymology_story.zh: arachnophobia 由源自古希腊语 arachnē（蜘蛛）的 arachno- 和源自 phobos（恐惧）的 -phobia 组合而成。这个名称通过“蜘蛛＋恐惧”直接表示对蜘蛛的强烈恐惧。
etymology_story.en: Arachnophobia combines arachno-, from ancient Greek arachnē, meaning spider, with -phobia, ultimately from phobos, meaning fear. The formation directly names an intense fear of spiders.

morphology_enriched.zh: arachno-（蜘蛛）+ -phobia（恐惧症）→ arachnophobia（蜘蛛恐惧症）。主要相关词有 arachnophobe（害怕蜘蛛的人）和 arachnophobic（患蜘蛛恐惧症的；也可作名词，指患者）；arachnophobes 和 arachnophobics 是相应的名词复数形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Arachno- (spider) + -phobia (fear or phobia) forms arachnophobia. The main related forms are arachnophobe, a person who fears spiders, and arachnophobic, an adjective meaning affected by this fear and also a noun for such a person. Their noun plurals are arachnophobes and arachnophobics.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: spider phobia（蜘蛛恐惧症）是直接的通俗对应说法；fear of spiders（害怕蜘蛛）范围更宽，也可只是普通害怕；aversion to spiders（厌恶蜘蛛）强调排斥或反感，不一定包含强烈恐惧。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Spider phobia is a direct plain-language equivalent. Fear of spiders is broader and can describe ordinary fear. Aversion to spiders emphasizes dislike or avoidance and does not necessarily imply intense fear.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: arachno- 是蜘蛛，-phobia 是恐惧：蜘蛛一出现，恐惧就启动。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Arachno- means spider and -phobia means fear: the spider appears, and the fear switches on.

senses.meaning_zh: 晨歌；黎明时演唱或演奏的歌曲、乐曲

senses.english_definition: An aubade is a song or piece of music that celebrates the morning or is performed at dawn.

senses.meaning_zh: 咏晨诗；尤指描写恋人在黎明时分离别的诗
senses.meaning_en: A poem about dawn, especially the parting of lovers at daybreak.
senses.english_definition: An aubade is a poem about the coming of morning, especially one in which lovers must part at dawn.
senses.collocation_en: write an aubade; a traditional aubade
senses.collocation_zh: 写一首咏晨诗；一首传统咏晨诗

etymology_story.zh: aubade 借自法语，指黎明时的歌唱或音乐，与 aube（黎明）相关，最终可追溯到拉丁语表示“白色”的 albus 及其阴性形式 alba。英语保留了晨歌义，也用它指以黎明、尤其是恋人晨别为主题的诗。
etymology_story.en: Aubade was borrowed from French for singing or music at daybreak and is related to aube, meaning dawn, ultimately from Latin albus, meaning white, through its feminine form alba. English retained the musical meaning and also uses the word for a dawn poem, especially one about lovers parting.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 aubade 是整体法语借词，不宜按英语词缀拆解；规则复数为 aubades。它没有常用的派生动词、形容词或副词；dawn song（晨歌）是释义性短语，不是其形态派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, aubade is a whole French borrowing rather than a transparent combination of English affixes; its regular plural is aubades. It has no commonly used derived verb, adjective, or adverb. Dawn song is an explanatory phrase, not a morphological derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dawn song（黎明之歌）最直接突出时间；morning song（晨歌）范围较宽，不一定涉及恋人离别；alba（奥克语抒情诗中的晨别歌）指特定文学传统中的相关体裁。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dawn song most directly emphasizes daybreak. Morning song is broader and need not involve parting lovers. Alba names a related dawn-parting genre in the Occitan lyric tradition.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: aube 是“黎明”：天色泛白，晨歌响起，恋人将别。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with French aube, dawn: the sky whitens, a morning song begins, and lovers prepare to part.

etymology_story.en: Bicarb is a clipping of bicarbonate; in everyday cooking and cleaning, it usually also leaves sodium understood and means sodium bicarbonate. Medical usage retains the broader meaning of bicarbonate.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：bicarbonate → bicarb，属于截短构词，不宜把 bicarb 重新拆成独立的现代词根和词缀。bicarb 本身没有常用派生词；相关完整形式有 bicarbonate（碳酸氢盐）、sodium bicarbonate（碳酸氢钠），常用组合有 bicarbonate of soda、bicarb soda（均指小苏打）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: bicarbonate → bicarb by clipping; bicarb is not normally analyzed into productive modern roots and affixes. synonyms_and_nuances.en: Baking soda is the everyday term, especially in American English; sodium bicarbonate is the precise chemical name; bicarbonate of soda is a familiar full expression in British English. senses.meaning_zh: 滴定管；可精确控制和测量放出液体体积的带刻度细管
senses.meaning_en: A graduated laboratory tube used to deliver measured volumes of liquid, especially during titration.
senses.english_definition: A burette is a narrow glass tube with measurement marks and a tap that you use to release an accurately measured amount of liquid.

etymology_story.zh: burette 借自法语，原指小瓶或小壶，是 buire（一种壶或容器）的指小形式。这个表示小容器的词后来用于能够精确放出液体的实验室仪器。
etymology_story.en: Burette was borrowed from French, where it meant a small bottle or flask and was a diminutive of buire, a type of jug or vessel. The small-container name was later applied to the laboratory instrument used to deliver liquid precisely.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中把 burette 作为完整的借入词学习；历史上可分析为法语 buire + 指小后缀 -ette，并伴有词干变化。常用词形有复数 burettes、美式异体 buret 及其复数 burets；没有常用派生动词或形容词。常用组合：burette stand（滴定管架）、burette clamp（滴定管夹）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, burette is best learned as a complete loanword; historically it contains French buire plus the diminutive suffix -ette, with a stem change. Common forms are the plural burettes, the American spelling buret, and its plural burets; there are no common derived verbs or adjectives. Useful combinations include burette stand and burette clamp.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: buret 是同一仪器的异体拼写，尤其见于美式英语；pipette（移液管）是相关仪器，通常用于量取并转移液体，而 burette 特别适合在滴定中逐步控制加入量，两者不能直接互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Buret is an alternative spelling for the same instrument, especially in American English. A pipette is a related measuring and transfer instrument, whereas a burette is particularly suited to controlling successive additions during titration; the two instrument names are not interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从法语“小容器”联想到实验台上带刻度、能逐滴放液的细管。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the original French “small vessel” to a marked laboratory tube that releases liquid drop by drop.

senses.meaning_zh: 百金花；尤指百金花属中开粉红色花、味苦的草本植物
senses.meaning_en: A usually pink-flowered, bitter herb, especially a plant of the genus Centaurium.

etymology_story.zh: centaury 经早期英语形式追溯到拉丁语 centaureum 和希腊语 kentaureion，词源与 centaur（半人马）有关。传统说法将这种药草与半人马喀戎联系起来，传说他曾用它疗伤。
etymology_story.en: Centaury comes through earlier English forms from Latin centaureum and Greek kentaureion, a plant name connected with the word for centaur. Tradition associates the herb with the centaur Chiron, who was said to have used it to heal a wound.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 centaury 是完整的植物名称，不宜机械地分析为 centaur + 现代能产后缀 -y。复数为 centauries，常用派生词缺乏；centaur（半人马）是词源相关词。实际植物名称包括 common centaury（普通百金花）和 lesser centaury（小百金花，也是普通百金花的传统名称）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, centaury is an established plant name, not a productive formation of centaur plus the modern suffix -y. Its plural is centauries, and it has no common derivatives; centaur is an etymologically related word. Established plant names include common centaury and lesser centaury, a traditional name for common centaury.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: common centaury（普通百金花）通常特指 Centaurium erythraea；lesser centaury 是同一植物的传统通名。centaury 单独使用时范围较宽，可指百金花属中的其他近缘植物，因此具体物种宜用完整名称确认。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Common centaury usually specifies Centaurium erythraea; lesser centaury is a traditional common name for the same plant. Centaury alone has a wider scope and can refer to related plants in Centaurium, so the fuller name helps identify the species.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: centaur 是半人马：把 centaury 记成传说中半人马喀戎用的药草。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Centaur → Chiron's healing herb → centaury.

senses.meaning_zh: 欧洲鳃金龟等大型金龟子；成虫多呈褐色，幼虫以植物根部为食

etymology_story.zh: cockchafer 由 cock 和 chafer 构成；chafer 是源自古英语的甲虫名称。这里的 cock 通常被解释为表示“大”或“显眼”的加强成分，具体命名缘由并不完全确定，不能据此理解成与公鸡有关的甲虫。
etymology_story.en: Cockchafer combines cock with chafer, an English beetle name inherited from Old English. Cock is generally interpreted as an intensifying element suggesting a large or conspicuous beetle, although the precise naming motivation is uncertain.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：cock + chafer（金龟子类甲虫）→ cockchafer，属于固定复合名词；cock 在这里不是独立的现代词缀。复数为 cockchafers，没有常用派生动词或形容词。相关基础词为 chafer；常用组合有 cockchafer grub（鳃金龟的蛴螬）和 common cockchafer（欧洲鳃金龟）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: cock + chafer → cockchafer, a lexicalized compound noun; cock is not an independent modern affix here. The plural is cockchafers, and there are no common derived verbs or adjectives. Chafer is the related base noun; useful combinations include cockchafer grub and common cockchafer.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: May bug（五月甲虫）是 cockchafer 的常见别名；chafer（金龟子类甲虫）范围更广，cockchafer 是其中一类；June beetle（六月甲虫）通常用于其他近缘金龟子，不能一概当作同一物种。

senses.meaning_zh: 搞砸的事；因处理不当造成的大失误（英国非正式用语，略粗俗）
senses.meaning_en: A badly mishandled situation or serious mistake; informal British English, sometimes considered mildly vulgar.
senses.english_definition: A cockup is a mistake or confused situation that happens because someone handles something badly.
senses.collocation_en: a complete cockup; an administrative cockup

senses.sentence_zh: 由于行政工作中的一次大失误，几名申请人收到了错误的结果。

etymology_story.zh: cockup 通常写作 cock-up，由表示“搞砸”的动词短语 cock up 转成名词。cock 虽然另有“使翘起”的旧义，但“搞砸”这一用法的具体起源并无定论。
etymology_story.en: Cockup, usually written cock-up, is a noun formed from the phrasal verb cock up, meaning to mishandle something. Although cock also has an older meaning of raising or tilting something, the precise origin of the bungling sense is uncertain.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：动词短语 cock up → 复合名词 cock-up，也写 cockup；复数为 cock-ups 或 cockups。相关动词形式：cock up、cocks up、cocked up、cocking up；cocked-up 可作形容词，表示“被搞砸的”。分写的 cock up 是相关动词短语，不能直接作为单词 cockup 的动词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: the phrasal verb cock up produces the compound noun cock-up, also spelled cockup; its plurals are cock-ups and cockups. Related verb forms are cock up, cocks up, cocked up, and cocking up; cocked-up can function adjectivally, meaning badly mishandled. The separately written cock up is a related phrasal verb, rather than a verb use of the single word cockup.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: blunder 指明显且往往严重的错误；bungle 强调因笨拙或无能而处理失败；fiasco 强调整个事件令人难堪地失败。cockup 带有鲜明的英国口语色彩，可指具体失误，也可指由此造成的混乱。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A blunder is an obvious and often serious mistake; a bungle emphasizes incompetent handling; a fiasco emphasizes the embarrassing failure of an entire undertaking. Cockup is distinctly informal and British, covering either the mistake itself or the resulting mess.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cock up 是“把事情搞砸”；a cockup 就是“一件搞砸了的事”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: To cock something up is to mess it up; a cockup is the resulting mistake or mess.

senses.meaning_zh: 百科全书；某一领域的百科全书（旧式拼写或旧称）
senses.meaning_en: An encyclopedia covering knowledge generally or a particular subject; an older form of the word.
senses.english_definition: A cyclopaedia is a book or set of books containing information about many subjects or many aspects of one subject.
senses.collocation_en: a cyclopaedia of biography; a cyclopaedia of practical medicine
senses.collocation_zh: 人物传记百科全书；实用医学百科全书
senses.sentence_en: The library holds a nineteenth-century cyclopaedia of practical medicine.
senses.sentence_zh: 这家图书馆藏有一部十九世纪的实用医学百科全书。

etymology_story.zh: cyclopaedia 来自近代拉丁语 cyclopaedia，是 encyclopaedia 的缩短形式。其更深层来源是希腊语中表示“通识教育”的词组 enkuklios paideia，后来由教育体系的名称发展为汇集知识的书籍名称。
etymology_story.en: Cyclopaedia comes from modern Latin cyclopaedia, a shortened form of encyclopaedia. Its deeper source is the Greek expression enkuklios paideia, meaning general education, which eventually gave its name to a comprehensive collection of knowledge.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 cyclopaedia 作为完整借词处理；辅助分析可用 cyclo-（圆、循环）和 -paedia（教育），但这不是英语中临时拼接出的普通派生词。复数：cyclopaedias；异体：cyclopedia；相关形容词：cyclopaedic、cyclopedic；相关形式：encyclopaedia、encyclopedia、encyclopaedic、encyclopedic。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cyclopaedia is normally treated as a whole borrowed word; cyclo- meaning circle and -paedia referring to education provide a useful analysis, rather than an ordinary productive English derivation. Plural: cyclopaedias; alternative spelling: cyclopedia; related adjectives: cyclopaedic and cyclopedic; related forms: encyclopaedia, encyclopedia, encyclopaedic, and encyclopedic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: encyclopaedia 是现代常用的对应词，美式英语通常拼作 encyclopedia；compendium 是某一主题知识的简明汇编，不一定按词条组织；dictionary 通常侧重词语释义，也可指按字母排列的专业知识词典。cyclopaedia 与 encyclopaedia 的主要区别是时代和文体色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Encyclopaedia, usually encyclopedia in American English, is the normal modern equivalent; a compendium is a concise collection of information that need not use separate entries; a dictionary usually explains words, though it may also cover specialist subjects alphabetically. Cyclopaedia differs from encyclopaedia chiefly in its historical or old-fashioned register.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把“圆”联想到知识的完整一圈：覆盖整个知识圈的书，就是百科全书。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of a complete circle of learning: a book covering that circle is a cyclopaedia.

senses.meaning_zh: 采石场；采石坑；挖出的坑（英国地域用语或古旧用语）
senses.meaning_en: A quarry or excavated pit; regional British or archaic usage.

senses.meaning_zh: 代尔夫特陶器；锡釉陶器（delft 的少见异体）
senses.meaning_en: Delftware or tin-glazed earthenware; an uncommon variant of delft.
senses.english_definition: Delf is pottery covered with an opaque glaze, often decorated in blue and white.
senses.collocation_en: blue-and-white delf; a piece of delf
senses.collocation_zh: 青花锡釉陶器；一件代尔夫特陶器
senses.sentence_en: The cabinet contained several pieces of blue-and-white delf.
senses.sentence_zh: 陈列柜里放着几件青花锡釉陶器。

etymology_story.zh: 表示“采石坑”的 delf 源自中古英语及更早的古英语挖掘类名词，与 delve“挖掘”有历史联系。表示陶器的 delf 则是 delft 的异体，名称来自荷兰陶器产地 Delft；不能把两个义项当作同一词义自然演变的结果。
etymology_story.en: Delf meaning a quarry descends through Middle English from Old English nouns associated with digging and is historically related to delve. Delf meaning pottery is instead a variant of delft, named after the Dutch pottery town Delft; the two English senses should not be presented as a single continuous semantic development.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：delf 在两个义项中都作为完整词处理，没有可自由拆分的现代英语词缀。采石坑义为可数名词，复数 delfs，历史相关词为 delve；陶器义通常为不可数名词，相关形式为 delft 和 delftware。delve 不是在现代英语中由 delf 添加词缀派生而成的。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: delf is treated as an unsegmented word in both senses, with no productive English affixes. The quarry sense is countable, with plural delfs, and is historically related to delve; the pottery sense is normally uncountable and is associated with delft and delftware. Delve is not a modern affixal derivative of delf.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 采石坑义：quarry 明确指开采石料的场所，pit 泛指坑或某些矿坑，excavation 强调挖掘形成的空间。陶器义：delftware 是更明确的对应名称；earthenware 泛指陶器，范围更广；faience 常指锡釉陶器，但其地域和工艺用法有所不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the digging sense, quarry specifically denotes a stone-extraction site, pit is a broader term for a hole or certain mines, and excavation emphasizes a space created by digging. For pottery, delftware is the more explicit equivalent; earthenware is broader; faience often denotes tin-glazed pottery but differs in regional and technical usage.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 采石坑义联想 delve“挖”：挖出来的坑是 delf；陶器义则联想荷兰地名 Delft，分开记忆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the quarry sense with delve: digging leaves a delf. Link the pottery sense separately with the Dutch town Delft.

usage_note: 音乐专门词；本卡只学管风琴音栓或音管组义。遇到讲音域或八度的旧文，可能是另一个义项。

senses.meaning_zh: 管风琴的主音栓；产生管风琴典型基本音色的一组音管
senses.meaning_en: An organ principal stop, or its rank of pipes, producing the instrument's characteristic basic tone.

senses.meaning_en: The full range or complete extent of something; literary or figurative usage.

etymology_story.zh: diapason 经拉丁语来自希腊语 dia pasōn，字面意思是“贯穿所有”，其中省略了表示弦或音的词，原指八度音程。它后来发展出完整音域、宏亮合声以及管风琴主音栓等意义。
etymology_story.en: Diapason came through Latin from Greek dia pasōn, literally through all, with a word for strings or notes understood, and originally denoted the octave. It later developed meanings involving a complete tonal range, rich combined sound, and the principal tone-producing stops of an organ.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：diapason 是完整借词，不宜分析成现代英语中可自由组合的 dia- 加 pason。复数为 diapasons；罕见相关形容词为 diapasonal。历史分析 dia“贯穿”加 pasōn“所有的”有助于理解词源，但 pason 不是现代英语中独立使用的词根。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: diapason is a whole borrowed word, rather than a productive English combination of dia- and pason. Its plural is diapasons; a rare related adjective is diapasonal. The historical elements dia meaning through and pasōn meaning of all explain its origin, but pason is not an independently used modern English base.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: principal 在管风琴语境中是主音栓义的近义词；octave 对应其历史上的八度音程义；gamut 对应比喻性的全部范围义。这些词分别对应不同义项，不能在所有语境中互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Principal is a close equivalent in organ terminology; octave matches the historical interval sense; gamut matches the figurative meaning of a complete range. These alternatives correspond to different senses and are not interchangeable in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Through all the notes suggests a complete octave and a full range, then the organ's rich foundational tone.

senses.meaning_zh: 二烯；含有两个碳碳双键的化合物，尤指此类烃
senses.meaning_en: A compound, especially a hydrocarbon, containing two carbon–carbon double bonds.
senses.english_definition: A diene is a chemical compound whose molecules contain two carbon–carbon double bonds.
senses.collocation_zh: 共轭二烯；二烯合成
senses.sentence_en: Buta-1,3-diene is a conjugated diene used to make synthetic rubber.
senses.sentence_zh: 1,3-丁二烯是一种用于制造合成橡胶的共轭二烯。

etymology_story.zh: diene 是现代化学命名形成的词，由表示“二”的希腊语源前缀 di- 与表示碳碳双键的命名后缀 -ene 组合而成。它把两个构词成分的含义直接用于标示分子中的两个碳碳双键。
etymology_story.en: Diene was formed in modern chemical nomenclature from the Greek-derived prefix di-, meaning two, and the naming suffix -ene, indicating a carbon–carbon double bond. The resulting name directly identifies the presence of two such double bonds in a molecule.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：di-（二）+ -ene（碳碳双键命名后缀）→ diene；复数 dienes。相关形容词：dienic、dienyl（常作取代基名称成分）；相关术语：alkadiene（二烯烃）、butadiene（丁二烯）、cyclopentadiene（环戊二烯）、dienophile（亲二烯体）。同一命名系列包括 alkene（烯烃）、triene（三烯）和 polyene（多烯），但它们并非全部由 diene 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: di- meaning two + -ene, the suffix indicating a carbon–carbon double bond, gives diene; plural dienes. Related adjectival forms include dienic and dienyl, the latter often used in substituent names; related terms include alkadiene, butadiene, cyclopentadiene, and dienophile. The same naming system includes alkene, triene, and polyene, although these are not all direct derivatives of diene.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: diolefin 是 diene 的传统近义名称；alkadiene 更明确地指含两个碳碳双键的非环状烃；conjugated diene 仅指两个双键之间隔着一个单键的共轭二烯，是 diene 的一个子类。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Diolefin is a traditional alternative name for diene; alkadiene more specifically denotes an acyclic hydrocarbon with two carbon–carbon double bonds; conjugated diene denotes the subclass in which one single bond separates the two double bonds.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: di- 数“二”，-ene 看“双键”：两个碳碳双键，就是二烯。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Di- counts two; -ene signals a double bond: a diene has two carbon–carbon double bonds.

senses.meaning_zh: 小嘴鸻；某些其他鸻类鸟的名称
senses.meaning_en: A small plover, especially the Eurasian dotterel.
senses.english_definition: A dotterel is a small bird belonging to the plover family, especially a species that breeds on open uplands in Europe and Asia.
senses.collocation_zh: 小嘴鸻；新西兰鸻
senses.sentence_en: We spotted a dotterel feeding on the open hillside.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们发现一只小嘴鸻正在开阔的山坡上觅食。

etymology_story.zh: 该词见于中古英语，由 dote 的旧义“举止愚笨”和带贬义的后缀 -rel 构成，早期也曾指愚人。鸟名反映了过去人们认为这种鸟容易接近和捕捉的看法，并不是对其智力的科学判断。
etymology_story.en: Recorded in Middle English, dotterel combines dote in its old sense of behaving foolishly with the disparaging suffix -rel; it also formerly meant a foolish person. The bird's name reflects an old belief that it was easily approached and caught, rather than a scientific assessment of its intelligence.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常将 dotterel 作为不可再作能产拆分的完整鸟名；历史结构为 dote + -rel。复数为 dotterels；dottrel 是异体拼写。历史相关词族包括 dote（溺爱；旧义为举止愚笨）、doting（溺爱的）、dotingly（溺爱地）和 dotage（年老昏聩），但它们不是由现代鸟名派生而来。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dotterel is normally treated as a whole bird name rather than a productively formed word; its historical structure is dote + -rel. Its plural is dotterels, and dottrel is a spelling variant. Historically related words include dote, doting, dotingly, and dotage, but these are not derivatives of the modern bird name.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: plover（鸻）是范围更大的类名；Eurasian dotterel（小嘴鸻）明确指通常所说的欧亚物种；dottrel 与 dotterel 含义相同，只是较少见的异体拼写。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Plover is the broader group name; Eurasian dotterel identifies the particular Eurasian species commonly meant by dotterel; dottrel has the same meaning but is a less usual spelling.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 旧时被误认为“呆、好抓”的鸟 → dotterel；这是名称来历，不是鸟的真实性格。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A bird once thought foolish and easy to catch → dotterel: remember the naming belief, not a fact about its intelligence.

senses.meaning_zh: 乙烯，分子式为 C₂H₄ 的最简单烯烃
senses.meaning_en: The simplest alkene, C₂H₄, a colourless flammable gas.
senses.english_definition: Ethene is a colourless gas with two carbon atoms joined by a double bond, used to make plastics and other chemicals.

senses.sentence_en: Ethene molecules join together to form polyethene.

etymology_story.zh: ethene 形成于19世纪的化学命名体系，以 ethyl 词族中的 eth- 加上表示烯烃的 -ene 构成。它与较早使用、至今仍很常见的 ethylene 指同一种化合物。
etymology_story.en: Ethene arose in nineteenth-century chemical nomenclature, combining eth- from the ethyl naming family with the alkene suffix -ene. It names the same compound as the older and still widely used term ethylene.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代命名结构为 eth-（两个碳原子的碳链）+ -ene（碳碳双键）→ ethene。直接相关形式包括 polyethene（聚乙烯）；ethylene 是同义名称，polyethylene 是 polyethene 的同义名称。ethane（乙烷）、ethyne（乙炔）、ethyl（乙基）和 ethanol（乙醇）属于相关命名词族，不能都视为 ethene 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern naming structure is eth- for a two-carbon chain + -ene for a carbon–carbon double bond → ethene. Directly related formations include polyethene; ethylene is an alternative name, and polyethylene is an alternative name for polyethene. Ethane, ethyne, ethyl, and ethanol belong to the related naming family rather than all being direct derivatives of ethene.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ethylene（乙烯）是同一化合物的常用同义名称，尤其常见于工业和植物生理学语境；alkene（烯烃）是包含乙烯的一类化合物的总称，不能作为精确同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ethylene is an exact alternative name, especially common in industrial and plant-physiology contexts. Alkene names the broader class containing ethene and is therefore not an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: eth- 记两个碳，-ene 记双键：CH₂=CH₂。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Eth- means two carbons; -ene signals a double bond: CH₂=CH₂.

morphology.text: geo-（地球）+ -oid（形状、类似物）→ geoid（大地水准面）。先用“地球的形状”联想，再记住它是由重力决定的参考面。

etymology.text: 英语借自德语 Geoid，更早的希腊语 geoeidēs 意为“像地球的”。把它想成海水在重力作用下形成、并延伸到陆地下方的一张参考面。

usage_note: 测绘、地球物理术语。它与海洋平均海平面近似重合，并向陆地下方延伸；不能把它理解成地面高低起伏的实际地形。

senses.meaning_zh: 大地水准面：近似全球平均海平面、并延伸至陆地下方的地球重力等位面
senses.meaning_en: An equipotential surface of Earth's gravity field that approximates global mean sea level and extends beneath the continents.
senses.english_definition: The geoid is an imaginary surface that closely follows average sea level around the Earth and continues beneath the land, with the same gravity potential at every point.
senses.collocation_zh: 大地水准面模型；大地水准面高
senses.sentence_en: Surveyors use a geoid model to convert satellite-derived heights into elevations above mean sea level.
senses.sentence_zh: 测量人员利用大地水准面模型，将卫星测得的高度转换为相对于平均海平面的高程。

etymology_story.zh: 英语 geoid 借自19世纪德语 Geoid，最终源于希腊语表示“像地球的”的 geoeidēs。这个原本强调地球形状的名称，在大地测量学中专指由地球重力场确定的参考等位面。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed geoid from nineteenth-century German Geoid, ultimately based on Greek geoeidēs, meaning earthlike. A name suggesting Earth's shape acquired the precise geodetic meaning of a reference equipotential surface determined by Earth's gravity field.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词分析为 geo-（地球）+ -oid（类似……的形体）→ geoid。主要词形包括复数 geoids 和形容词 geoidal（大地水准面的）；geodesy（大地测量学）、geodetic（大地测量的）与其共享 geo-，但不是 geoid 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern combining-form analysis is geo- meaning Earth + -oid meaning a resembling form → geoid. Principal forms include the plural geoids and the adjective geoidal. Geodesy and geodetic share geo- but are not derivatives of geoid.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有通用的精确单词同义词。equipotential surface（等位面）是更宽泛的数学和物理概念；mean sea-level surface（平均海平面）是理解大地水准面的近似描述；reference ellipsoid（参考椭球）是光滑的数学参考面，与受重力场影响而起伏的大地水准面不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no usual exact single-word synonym. Equipotential surface is a broader mathematical and physical term; mean sea-level surface provides an approximate description; a reference ellipsoid is a smooth mathematical reference surface, distinct from the gravity-dependent undulations of the geoid.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: geo- 地球 + -oid 形体：想象全球海水静止后形成、并穿过陆地下方的重力参考面。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Geo- Earth + -oid form: picture a gravity-defined surface traced by an ideal resting ocean and continued beneath the land.

etymology_story.en: Graduand entered English in the nineteenth century from Medieval Latin graduandus, meaning someone to be awarded a degree, from graduare, to confer a degree. It preserves the Latin gerundive idea of a person awaiting an action.

morphology_enriched.zh: graduand 是整体借入的词；历史上可分析为 gradu-（授予学位）+ -and（源自拉丁语表示有待接受动作的形式），不能把 -and 当作现代英语中可自由使用的后缀。复数为 graduands；相关词族包括 graduate（毕业；毕业生）、graduation（毕业；学位授予）、graduating（即将毕业的）、undergraduate（本科生）和 postgraduate（研究生；研究生的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Graduand is a borrowed whole word, historically analysable as gradu- relating to conferring a degree + -and from a Latin form indicating an action to be undergone; -and is not a freely productive modern English suffix. The plural is graduands. Related family members include graduate, graduation, graduating, undergraduate, and postgraduate.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: degree candidate（学位申请人或候选人）范围更宽，不一定已临近授位；graduating student（即将毕业的学生）是较通用的近义表达；graduate（毕业生、学位获得者）通常表示已经获授学位。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Degree candidate is broader and need not imply that conferral is imminent; graduating student is a more general near-equivalent; graduate normally describes someone whose degree has already been awarded.

meaning: 屋顶由多排柱子支撑的

morphology.text: hypo-（在下方）+ -style（柱子）→ hypostyle（由下方柱子撑起屋顶的）。这里的 -style 与柱子有关，可联想一排排立柱托住屋顶。

etymology.text: 源自希腊语 hypostylos，意思是“由柱子支撑的”，其中 stylos 表示柱子。记住屋顶下面布满柱子的画面，就容易抓住建筑含义。

etymology_story.zh: 该词最终源自希腊语 hypostylos，意为“由柱子支撑的”，由 hypo-（在下方）与 stylos（柱子）组成。它进入建筑术语后，既可形容这种屋顶支承方式，也可作名词指采用这种结构的大厅。
etymology_story.en: The word ultimately comes from Greek hypostylos, meaning supported by columns, from hypo- meaning underneath and stylos meaning a column. In architectural usage, it functions both as an adjective describing this roof-support system and as a noun for a hall built with it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可识别的古典语构词成分为 hypo-（在下方）+ -style（柱式，源自希腊语 stylos），其中 -style 与表示“风格”的普通英语 style 来源不同。hypostyle 同形兼作形容词和名词，名词复数为 hypostyles；peristyle（柱廊、周柱式）和 prostyle（前柱式的）是共享柱式词根的相关建筑词，并非 hypostyle 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Its recognisable classical components are hypo- meaning underneath + -style relating to columns, from Greek stylos; this -style has a different origin from ordinary English style meaning manner or fashion. Hypostyle serves unchanged as both adjective and noun, with the noun plural hypostyles. Peristyle and prostyle are related architectural formations sharing the column element, not direct derivatives of hypostyle.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: columned（有柱的）和 pillared（有支柱的）只说明存在柱子，不一定表示柱子成排承托屋顶；column-supported hall（柱子承顶的大厅）是名词义的近义描述，但 hypostyle 更明确地指多排柱子的建筑布置。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Columned and pillared indicate the presence of columns without necessarily specifying rows supporting a roof. Column-supported hall is a descriptive near-equivalent of the noun, while hypostyle more specifically denotes an arrangement with rows of supporting columns.

etymology_story.zh: lychgate 由 lych 和 gate 组成；lych 源自古英语 līc，意为“身体、遗体”。这个名称保留了门廊的传统用途：送葬队伍在此停放灵柩，等待牧师迎接。
etymology_story.en: Lychgate combines lych, from Old English līc meaning 'body' or 'corpse', with gate. Its name preserves its traditional function as a sheltered place where a funeral party rested the coffin while awaiting the priest.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代结构为 lych（仅在少数传统词语中保留的“遗体”）+ gate（门），属于复合名词。复数为 lychgates；异体拼写有 lichgate 和 lych-gate；没有常用的动词、形容词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern structure is lych, an old word for 'corpse' surviving in a few traditional expressions, + gate, forming a compound noun. The plural is lychgates; spelling variants include lichgate and lych-gate. There are no commonly used derived verbs, adjectives, or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: churchyard gate（教堂墓园入口的门）不一定有顶；covered gateway（有顶的入口）不限定宗教场所；porch（门廊）通常附设于建筑入口。这些是相关表达，并非完全同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A churchyard gate need not have a roof; a covered gateway need not belong to a churchyard; a porch usually shelters the entrance to a building. These are related expressions rather than exact synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: lych＝遗体，gate＝门：让灵柩暂歇的有顶墓园门。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Lych means 'corpse' and gate means 'entrance': picture a roofed churchyard gate sheltering a coffin.

etymology.text: 英语借用拉丁语 quinquennium；它把表示“五”的 quinque 与表示“年”的 annus 连在一起。整个词就是把五个年份装进同一个时间框。
